title: [tool_crash] Unhandled ProcessPackageException (OS Error 206: The filename or extension is too long) in _DefaultPub._preloadPubCache
body:
## Summary
`flutter pub get` crashes on Windows with an unhandled `ProcessPackageException` (`ProcessException: The filename or extension is too long`, OS error code `206` / `ERROR_FILENAME_EXCED_RANGE`) in `_DefaultPub._preloadPubCache` (`package:flutter_tools/src/dart/pub.dart:645`) / `ErrorHandlingProcessManager.runSync` (`package:flutter_tools/src/base/error_handling_io.dart:1310`).

## Crash Telemetry (Flutter `stable/3.47.7`)
* **Signature**: `ProcessPackageException at LocalProcessManager.runSync at package:process/src/interface/local_process_manager.dart-313da74f`
* **Rank**: #10 Top Crasher in `3.47.7`
* **Total Occurrences**: 19 (3.7% of Top 10, 1.9% of all `3.47.7` crashes, ~2.5 crashes/day)
* **Platform Distribution**: Windows: 19 (100.0%)
* **Sample Command**: `flutter pub get`
* **Error**:
```text
ProcessException: The filename or extension is too long (at ../../runtime/bin/process_win.cc:579) | Command: C:\Users\User\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\d--Dotlinker-Laravel-New-Set...
```

## Stack Trace
```text
#0      LocalProcessManager.runSync (package:process/src/interface/local_process_manager.dart:118)
#1      ErrorHandlingProcessManager.runSync.<anonymous closure> (package:flutter_tools/src/base/error_handling_io.dart:1310)
#2      _runSync (package:flutter_tools/src/base/error_handling_io.dart:1118)
#3      ErrorHandlingProcessManager.runSync (package:flutter_tools/src/base/error_handling_io.dart:1308)
#4      _DefaultPub._preloadPubCache (package:flutter_tools/src/dart/pub.dart:645)
#5      _DefaultPub._getPubCacheIfAvailable (package:flutter_tools/src/dart/pub.dart:624)
#6      _DefaultPub._createPubEnvironment (package:flutter_tools/src/dart/pub.dart:664)
#7      _DefaultPub._runWithStdioInherited (package:flutter_tools/src/dart/pub.dart:379)
```

## Root Cause
1. In `_DefaultPub._preloadPubCache` (`package:flutter_tools/src/dart/pub.dart`), `flutter_tools` passes all `.tar.gz` archive paths in `$FLUTTER_ROOT/.pub-preload-cache` to a single `_processManager.runSync(<String>[..._pubCommand, 'cache', 'preload', ...cacheFiles])` invocation. When the Flutter SDK or current working directory is located in a deep Windows path (or the concatenated `.tar.gz` paths exceed Windows `CreateProcessW` / `MAX_PATH` limits in `runtime/bin/process_win.cc`), Windows fails with error code `206` (`ERROR_FILENAME_EXCED_RANGE`: `The filename or extension is too long`).
2. In `_handleWindowsException` (`package:flutter_tools/src/base/error_handling_io.dart:1467-1522`), error code `206` is not listed in the `switch (errorCode)` statement, so `_onProcessException` returns without throwing a `ToolExit` and `_runSync` rethrows the raw `ProcessPackageException`.

## Recommendation
1. Add `const kFilenameExcedRange = 206;` (`ERROR_FILENAME_EXCED_RANGE`) to `_handleWindowsException` in `package:flutter_tools/src/base/error_handling_io.dart` so process/filesystem calls failing with error code `206` exit cleanly with a `ToolExit` instructing the user to move the

title: [tool_crash] Unhandled RangeError in CompactReporter._progressLine / truncate when terminal width is narrow
body:
## Summary
`flutter test` crashes with an unhandled `RangeError` in `truncate` (`package:test_core/src/util/pretty_print.dart:65`) called from `CompactReporter._progressLine` (`package:test_core/src/runner/reporter/compact.dart:445`) when `stdout.terminalColumns` (`lineLength`) is narrow enough that `lineLength - length < 4`.

## Crash Telemetry (Flutter `stable/3.47.7`)
* **Signature**: `RangeError at RangeError.checkValidRange at dart:core/errors.dart-aa4dd664`
* **Rank**: #2 Top Crasher in `3.47.7`
* **Total Occurrences**: 79 (15.3% of Top 10, 8.0% of all `3.47.7` crashes, ~10.3 crashes/day)
* **Platform Distribution**: Windows: 77 (97.5%), macOS: 2 (2.5%)
* **Sample Command**: `flutter test test/app_state_test.dart --plain-name AppState Model and Discovery State Tests 3. Clearing search restores the correct filtered results`
* **Error**:
```text
RangeError (start): Invalid value: Not in inclusive range 0..81: 84
```

## Stack Trace
```text
#0      RangeError.checkValidRange (dart:core/errors.dart:387)
#1      _StringBase.substring (dart:core-patch/string_patch.dart:437)
#2      truncate (package:test_core/src/util/pretty_print.dart:65)
#3      CompactReporter._progressLine (package:test_core/src/runner/reporter/compact.dart:445)
#4      CompactReporter._onTestStarted (package:test_core/src/runner/reporter/compact.dart:216)
#5      _rootRunUnary (dart:async/zone_root.dart:56)
#6      _CustomZone.runUnary (dart:async/zone.dart:816)
#7      _CustomZone.runUnaryGuarded (dart:async/zone.dart:710)
```

## Root Cause
In `CompactReporter._progressLine` (`package:test_core/src/runner/reporter/compact.dart:444-450`), the reporter computes the visible prefix length `var length = withoutColors(buffer.toString()).length` (e.g. `11` characters for `\r00:00 +0: `) and calls `utils.truncate(message, lineLength - length)` followed by `' ' * (lineLength - withoutColors(buffer.toString()).length)`. ## Recommendation
1. In `truncate` (`package:test_core/src/util/pretty_print.dart`), guard against `maxLength <= 4` (e.g., return `''` when `maxLength <= 0` and `'.' * maxLength` when `maxLength <= 3`, or clamp the `substring` start index to `0..text.length`).
2. In `CompactReporter._progressLine` (`package:test_core/src/runner/reporter/compact.dart`), clamp `lineLength - length` to a non-negative value before calling `utils.truncate` and before repeating `' '`.

title: [tool_crash] Unhandled TimeoutException in _runUnderFileLock / FlutterNativeAssetsBuildRunnerImpl.build during flutter test
body:
## Summary
`flutter test` (and builds with native assets) crashes with an unhandled `TimeoutException` in `_runUnderFileLock` (`package:hooks_runner/src/locking/locking.dart:127`) / `FlutterNativeAssetsBuildRunnerImpl.build` (`package:flutter_tools/src/isolated/native_assets/native_assets.dart:616`) when waiting more than 5 minutes (`singleHookTimeout`) to acquire an exclusive file lock on `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/.../.lock`.

## Crash Telemetry (Flutter `stable/3.47.7`)
* **Signature**: `TimeoutException at _runUnderFileLock at package:hooks_runner/src/locking/locking.dart-edfd86c7`
* **Rank**: #1 Top Crasher in `3.47.7`
* **Total Occurrences**: 83 (16.1% of Top 10, 8.4% of all `3.47.7` crashes, ~10.8 crashes/day)
* **Platform Distribution**: Windows: 74 (89.2%), macOS: 9 (10.8%)
* **Sample Command**: `flutter test --no-pub test/decoder_workshop_design_capture_test.dart test/decoder_workshop_ui_test.dart test/decoder_address_sheet_test.dart`
* **Error**:
```text
TimeoutException after 0:05:00.000000: Could not acquire the lock to C:\Users\...\current\.dart_tool\hooks_runner\shared\...
```

## Stack Trace
```text
#0      _runUnderFileLock (package:hooks_runner/src/locking/locking.dart:127)
#1      runUnderDirectoriesLock (package:hooks_runner/src/locking/locking.dart:21)
#2      NativeAssetsBuildRunner._runHookForPackageCached.<anonymous closure> (package:hooks_runner/src/build_runner/build_runner.dart:448)
#3      NativeAssetsBuildRunner._timeAsync (package:hooks_runner/src/build_runner/build_runner.dart:1189)
#4      NativeAssetsBuildRunner.build.<anonymous closure> (package:hooks_runner/src/build_runner/build_runner.dart:198)
#5      NativeAssetsBuildRunner._timeAsync (package:hooks_runner/src/build_runner/build_runner.dart:1189)
#6      FlutterNativeAssetsBuildRunnerImpl.build (package:flutter_tools/src/isolated/native_assets/native_assets.dart:616)
#7      _build (package:flutter_tools/src/isolated/native_assets/native_assets.dart:910)
```

## Root Cause
In `NativeAssetsBuildRunner._runHookForPackageCached` (`package:hooks_runner/src/build_runner/build_runner.dart`), `runUnderDirectoriesLock` / `_runUnderFileLock` attempts to acquire an exclusive lock (`randomAccessFile.lock(FileLock.exclusive)`) on `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/shared/<pkg>/build/.lock` and `.dart_tool/hooks_runner/<pkg>/<hash>/.lock` with `timeout: singleHookTimeout` (5 minutes). When a concurrent `flutter test` / IDE background test runner, a hung child build hook process, or Windows file syncing (e.g. OneDrive `Documents`) holds the lock past the timeout, `_runUnderFileLock` throws a raw `TimeoutException` instead of returning `Failure(HooksRunnerFailure.infra)`. title: RenderObject.attach builds semantics state for every render object when semantics is off
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Build any screen with semantics off (no screen reader, no SemanticsHandle).
2. Take a live heap profile after a full collection, for example with
   `getAllocationProfile(gc: true)` from package:vm_service, before and
   after the screen is shown.
3. Count the instances of `_RenderObjectSemantics`,
   `_SemanticsConfigurationProvider`, `SemanticsConfiguration` and
   `AttributedString`.

`RenderObject.attach` in packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/object.dart
ends with:

```dart
if (_semantics.configProvider.effective.isSemanticBoundary &&
    (_semantics.parentDataDirty || !_semantics.built)) {
  markNeedsSemanticsUpdate();
}
```

Reading `_semantics` creates the late `_RenderObjectSemantics` with its
lists and map, and `effective` creates a `SemanticsConfiguration` and calls
`describeSemanticsConfiguration`. This happens for every attached render
object before anything checks for a semantics owner, while
`markNeedsSemanticsUpdate` itself returns early when there is none.

### Expected results

With semantics off, attaching a render object should not build its
semantics configuration, and the screen should keep no semantics state.

### Actual results

Every attached render object keeps one `_RenderObjectSemantics`, one
`_SemanticsConfigurationProvider`, one `SemanticsConfiguration` and five
`AttributedString`s, plus the lists and maps they create, and
`describeSemanticsConfiguration` runs once per render object. No
`SemanticsNode` is ever created.

Measured on a Pixel 7 Pro in profile mode, on a screen of 39 components
(texts, Material text fields, checkboxes, sliders and dividers, 594 render
objects):

| | Flutter 3.47.7 | With the change below |
|---|---|---|
| Live heap kept by the screen | 1,385 KB | 991 KB |
| Objects kept by the screen | 31,304 | 21,701 |
| Semantics classes listed above | 232 KB in 4,752 objects | none |

Per component type, in KB kept per component:

| | 3.47.7 | With the change |
|---|---|---|
| Text | 7.8 | 5.0 |
| TextField | 75.9 | 57.0 |
| Checkbox with label | 51.5 | 37.4 |
| Slider | 27.2 | 19.0 |
| Divider | 12.2 | 6.1 |

It also costs time when a screen is created. Alternating builds with and
without the change on the same device, 20 rounds each, the frame that
draws the 39 components took 8.5 ms with 3.47.7 and 8.1 ms with the
change at the median, and the slowest build while creating 7.8 ms against
7.4 ms.

A possible change is to check for a semantics owner first, as
`markNeedsSemanticsUpdate` does:

```dart
if (owner._semanticsOwner != null &&
    _semantics.configProvider.effective.isSemanticBoundary &&
    (_semantics.parentDataDirty || !_semantics.built)) {
  markNeedsSemanticsUpdate();
}
```

When semantics is turned on later, `scheduleInitialSemantics` on the root
rebuilds the tree, so no update should be lost. With this change the
rendering, semantics, widgets and material test suites pass, apart from
six tests in test/rendering/paragraph_test.dart that call
`assembleSemantics

title: [iOS] Data race in FlutterPlatformViewsController: computeViewsToDispose mutates raster-thread-only state on the platform thread (SIGSEGV in submitFrame)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Preconditions: any iOS app that embeds `UiKitView` platform views and pops a route containing them while frames keep rendering (a normal `MaterialPageRoute` transition is enough). The field crash below came from an app whose nav bar on most pages holds `UiKitView`-backed `UIVisualEffectView(effect: UIGlassEffect())` buttons, so every back navigation disposes one to three platform views mid-animation.

1. Push a route that contains one or more `UiKitView`s. Let the transition finish.
2. Pop the route. When the route is removed, Dart sends `dispose` for each platform view → `onDispose:` adds the id to `viewsToDispose` (platform thread).
3. The next `submitFrame:` on the raster thread posts `performSubmit:` to the platform thread. `performSubmit:` calls `computeViewsToDispose`, which erases the id from `currentCompositionParams` and `viewsToRecomposite` **on the platform thread**.

Disposing a platform view must not mutate raster-thread-only state from the platform thread. No crash.

[web] SemanticScrollable sets scrollTop before resizing its overflow, so the browser clamps it
body:
Reproduced on Flutter 3.47.4 stable (9584c6713b), Chrome on macOS. The code involved is unchanged on master 697012a97f (links below).

When one semantics update both grows a scrollable's extent and moves its position past the old maximum, `SemanticScrollable` assigns `scrollTop` before it resizes `flt-semantics-scroll-overflow`. The browser clamps the value to the old maximum, the DOM and the framework disagree from then on, and the next browser-driven scroll (an assistive technology's scroll, or a scroll-into-view) makes the list jump.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Build the code sample below for web (`flutter build web --profile`), serve `build/web` and open it in Chrome.
2. Turn semantics on, for example by running `document.querySelector('flt-semantics-placeholder').click()` in the DevTools console, or by using a screen reader.
3. Activate "Grow". One tap adds ten rows and calls `jumpTo(800)` in the same frame, so the larger extent and the new position reach the engine in one semantics update. Before the tap the list can scroll 400px; after it, 800px.
4. Read the `scrollTop` of the scrolling `flt-semantics` element.
5. Scroll that element up by 40px, as an assistive technology's scroll or a browser scroll-into-view would. For example, run `sc.scrollTop -= 40` on it.

The scripts that produced the logs below are under "Logs".

### Expected results

After Grow, the DOM `scrollTop` is 800, matching the framework. A 40px scroll up moves the list to 760, which leaves Row 19 at the top.

### Actual results

The framework asks for 800, but the browser clamps the value to the old maximum of 400, because the overflow element is still sized for the old extent (800px tall in a 400px viewport). Node positions stay visually right, since `verticalScrollAdjustment` is read from the clamped `scrollTop`. The DOM and the framework now disagree by 400px, and nothing corrects that until the scrollable's node is updated again with a different position.

The next browser scroll is computed from 400. `_recomputeScrollPosition` sends `scrollToOffset(360)`, so the list jumps 440px, from Row 20 to Row 9, instead of 40px. A screenshot taken at that point confirms that the painted list matches: Row 9 is at the top.

In a real app this showed up as a type-ahead list under a text field. Opening it near the foot of the page grows the page's scroll extent, and `Scrollable.ensureVisible` scrolls to it in the same frame. The page then jumped visibly when the screen reader moved.

```dart

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: Scaffold(body: Grow())));

/// One tap adds rows and scrolls to the new end in the same frame, so the
/// larger scroll extent and the new position reach the engine in one
/// semantics update. Before the tap the list can scroll 400px; after it, 800px.
class Grow extends StatefulWidget {
  const Grow({super.key});
  @override
  State<Grow> createS

[go_router_builder] Allow build 5.0.0 so apps can use build_runner 2.17.1
body:
### Use case

`build_runner` 2.17.1 requires `build >=5.0.0 <5.1.0`. `build` 5.0.0 is the retracted `build` 4.1.0 republished as a major version (https://github.com/dart-lang/build/issues/5223). `go_router_builder` 4.5.0, and `main` at 4.5.1, constrain `build: ">=3.0.0 <5.0.0"`, so an app that uses `go_router_builder` stays on `build_runner` 2.16.x.

### Steps to reproduce

1. In an app with `go_router_builder: ^4.5.0` in `dev_dependencies`, set `build_runner: ^2.17.1`.
2. Run `flutter pub get`.

Expected: resolves.
Actual: version solving fails, because `go_router_builder` requires `build <5.0.0` and `build_runner` 2.17.1 requires `build >=5.0.0`.

### What we checked

With `dependency_overrides: build: ^5.0.0` and `build_runner` 2.17.1, `dart run build_runner build` generates our typed routes (`StatefulShellRoute` with nested `GoRouteData`) and `flutter analyze` reports no issues. This was on Flutter 3.47.6 and Dart 3.13.5.

### Proposal

Widen the constraint to `build: ">=3.0.0 <6.0.0"` (and `source_gen` if needed) in a release. Related: freezed (rrousselGit/freezed#1378) and json_serializable (google/json_serializable.dart#1598, merged) are doing the same.

[engine] Zero lease assertion when an expired caller draws while another engine keeps shared queues merged
body:
## Attachments

- [lease-zero-demo-sanitized.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33544786/lease-zero-demo-sanitized.zip)
- [zero-lease-crash-sanitized.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33544788/zero-lease-crash-sanitized.zip)
- [engine-validation-sanitized.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33544787/engine-validation-sanitized.zip)

## Summary

SharedThreadMerger::DecrementLease() can abort on `lease_term_ref > 0` when an engine resumes drawing after its lease expires while another engine keeps the shared raster/platform queues merged.

This issue isolates the zero-lease assertion from the broader PlatformView problems in #153211. It does not cover the separate deadlock or foreground/background symptoms. Proposed fix: #194200.

## Steps to reproduce

Use two RasterThreadMerger instances sharing one SharedThreadMerger and the same distinct platform/raster task queues:

1. A calls MergeWithLease(1).
2. A calls DecrementLease(). Its lease reaches zero and the queues unmerge, but its map entry remains.
3. B calls MergeWithLease(2), merging the shared queues again.
4. A resumes drawing and calls DecrementLease(). The shared merged-state check succeeds because B has an active lease.
5. A's stale zero-valued entry triggers the fatal assertion.

The corresponding Android scenario uses engines in the same FlutterEngineGroup, with B's PlatformView keeping the queues merged while A resumes rendering. The affected implementation is shared C++ code; the iOS demo from #153211 has not been validated with the patch.

## Android device reproduction

Confirmed on an Android test device running Android 17, using Flutter 3.35.3, Engine `ddf47dd3ff`, debug mode, and Impeller Vulkan. The attached demo uses two FlutterActivity instances in the same FlutterEngineGroup and a native TextView in hybrid composition; no WebView plugin is required.

1. On the bottom page, press ADD PlatformView and wait for the 40-frame sequence.
2. Press REMOVE PlatformView and wait for the next 40-frame sequence.
3. OPEN the top Activity containing another PlatformView.
4. Return to the bottom page and repeat ADD, REMOVE, OPEN in the same app process if needed.

Two initial automated cycles did not crash. A subsequent manual cycle triggered SIGABRT with the exact zero-lease assertion. The observed crash occurred while opening the top Activity again, after top onPostResume and before pressing return. Reproduction is timing-dependent; no reproduction rate is claimed. The demo uses an ordinary opaque top Activity, not a translucent variant.

Observed event sequence:

```text
 Bottom ADD completed
 Bottom REMOVE and 40-frame sequence completed
 Top onPostResume
 FATAL shared_thread_merger.cc(59): lease_term_ref > 0, lease_term=0
```

The attachments above contain the source, build/run instructions, app-specific crash stack, and lifecycle timeline. Patched Android validation results are included in the validation attachment and in #194200; iOS application vali

title: [packages] Warnings in Swift code aren't caught in CI
body:
The repo tool `analyze` command is supposed to [fail on warnings](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/916d4c9c0b33c3ef7d1dbb8d02984a895dc0216d/script/tool/lib/src/analyze_command.dart#L556), which has allowed us to keep our code warning-free, and in particular to find deprecated code in advance of it becoming a problem using the `*-min-version` flags in CI.

Except we wrote that tooling when all of the code was Obj-C, so `GCC_TREAT_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS` was all we needed. But `GCC_TREAT_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS` doesn't apply to Swift, so we've been silently losing warning coverage in CI as we ported plugins to Swift 🤦

I haven't tried yet, but hopefully we just need to add `SWIFT_TREAT_WARNINGS_AS_ERRORS` to that command to restore things. Doing so is going to require fixing all the latent warnings that have been introduced though, so it will probably be non-trivial.

title: [iPhone Duo] Idle app redraws seconds late after input on the simulator's inner screen (iOS 27.1)
body:
## Steps to reproduce

1. With Xcode 27.1, install the iOS 27.1 simulator runtime and create an
   iPhone Duo simulator:

   ```sh
   xcodebuild -downloadPlatform iOS -buildVersion 27.1
   xcrun simctl create "Duo-27.1" com.apple.CoreSimulator.SimDeviceType.iPhone-Duo com.apple.CoreSimulator.SimRuntime.iOS-27-1
   ```

2. In Device Hub, put the device in the Book or Open pose, so the app runs on
   the inner screen.
3. Run the app below with `flutter run -d Duo-27.1` (the iOS deployment
   target must be raised to 15.0 for Xcode 27.1).
4. Tap the floating action button once, then look at the counter.

## Code sample

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';

void main() => runApp(const MaterialApp(home: Counter()));

class Counter extends StatefulWidget {
  const Counter({super.key});

  @override
  State<Counter> createState() => _CounterState();
}

class _CounterState extends State<Counter> {
  int _taps = 0;

  @override
  Widget build(BuildContext context) => Scaffold(
    body: Center(
      child: Text('taps $_taps', style: const TextStyle(fontSize: 32)),
    ),
    floatingActionButton: FloatingActionButton(
      onPressed: () => setState(() => _taps++),
      child: const Icon(Icons.add),
    ),
  );
}
```

## Expected results

The counter shows `taps 1` right after the tap, as on other simulators.

## Actual results

The screen keeps showing `taps 0` for several seconds, then `taps 1` appears
without any further input. The tap itself is handled at once (the state has
changed); only the redraw is late. In a larger app this makes taps look
ignored: a second tap reveals the result of the first one.

The delay only shows while the app is idle. With a continuous animation on
screen (a `CircularProgressIndicator`), frames keep coming and updates look
normal.

## Comparisons

| Setup | Redraw after a tap |
| --- | --- |
| Code sample, iPhone Duo simulator (iOS 27.1), inner screen | several seconds late |
| Code sample, iPhone 17 Pro simulator (iOS 26.4) | immediate |
| UIKit-only app (a `UILabel` updated from a tap gesture), iPhone Duo simulator, inner screen | immediate |

In the same UIKit-only app on the iPhone Duo inner screen, a display link
created like the engine's (`[CADisplayLink displayLinkWithTarget:selector:]`,
which follows the main screen) ticks at 60 Hz, as does one from
`-[UIWindowScene displayLinkWithTarget:selector:]`.

Possibly relevant: `vsync_waiter_ios.mm` creates its display link with
`displayLinkWithTarget:selector:` and reads `UIScreen.mainScreen` for the
refresh rate. On the iPhone Duo the main screen is the outer one, even while
the app is on the inner screen (`UIScreen.mainScreen.bounds` stays 466x678).
iOS 27.0 deprecates `-[UIScreen displayLinkWithTarget:selector:]` in favor of
`-[UIWindowScene displayLinkWithTarget:selector:]`, which "is automatically
retargeted when the scene moves between displays". I have not confirmed this
is the cause, since the main-screen display link does tick in a UIKit app.

title: [Android] ~35–45ms (+6–8%) cold startup load latency regression after #191444
body:
### Description

In an internal Android app, we observed a **~33–36 ms (+6.2% mean / +6.7% median) regression** in cold startup home screen load latency introduced by https://github.com/flutter/flutter/commit/f47d7bb0f722ef070954478b7ad55854f5ca7d00 (`Cleanup VSync infrastructure and improve iOS touch to present latency (#191444)`) compared to its parent commit https://github.com/flutter/flutter/commit/37f611358f41c93489880a5f9f029c56bbb2661c.

Full internal benchmark details and logs are in b/572346031.

---

### Metrics Tracked

The benchmark runs 20 cold-startup iterations (`n = 20` per run) of an internal app on physical Android devices and tracks:
* **Home Page / Home Tab On-Launch Load Latency** *(regressed metric)*: Time (mean and median, in ms) from cold app launch until the initial home tab finishes loading and rendering on screen.
* **Cold Startup Time to Interactive from Process Creation**: Time from Android process creation until the app is interactive.

---

### Before vs. After (`37f611358f4` vs. `f47d7bb0f72`)

We ran multiple verification passes (`n = 20` cold startups per run) on the two adjacent commits:

* **Before — `37f611358f41c93489880a5f9f029c56bbb2661c` (Parent commit)**:
  * Run 1 (`n = 20`): **Mean = 549.77 ms**, **Median = 545.77 ms** (SD = 32.88 ms)

  * *(Preceding commits `12b69d68b57` and `ea4ba77b187` measured **510.41 ms** and **525.71 ms** mean, respectively.)*

* **After — `f47d7bb0f722ef070954478b7ad55854f5ca7d00` (PR #191444)**:
  * Run 1 (`n = 20`): **Mean = 575.42 ms**, **Median = 572.90 ms** (SD = 40.49 ms)
  * Run 2 (`n = 20`): **Mean = 590.29 ms**, **Median = 588.41 ms** (SD = 34.66 ms)
  * Run 3 (`n = 20`): **Mean = 562.57 ms**, **Median = 565.49 ms** (SD = 32.47 ms)
  * **Multi-run average (`n = 60`)**: **Mean = 576.09 ms**, **Median = 575.60 ms**

* **Delta (`37f611358f4` → `f47d7bb0f72`)**:
  * **Mean**: **+33.40 ms (+6.15%)** (`542.69 ms` → `576.09 ms`)

title: [Web] With semantics enabled, the browser's context menu has no Copy for a SelectionArea selection
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the sample below with `flutter run -d chrome`.
2. Select the text, by a drag or a double-click.
3. Right-click the selection.

The sample calls `SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics()`. Without that line, everything works. An app without it gets the same bug as soon as a user activates Flutter web's hidden "Enable accessibility" button, so screen reader users hit it in any Flutter web app.

### Expected results

The browser's context menu offers Copy for the selected text, as it does without semantics.

### Actual results

The browser shows its page menu (Back, Forward, Reload, Save As..., etc.) without Copy, as if nothing were selected. `document.getSelection()` is empty when the menu opens.

Without `ensureSemantics()`, `document.getSelection()` holds the selected text and the browser offers Copy.

What I found: without semantics, the right-click lands on the `web-selectable-region-context-menu` element of `PlatformSelectableRegionContextMenu`, which puts the selection in the DOM for the browser's menu. With semantics enabled, `document.elementFromPoint` at the same spot returns the text's `flt-semantics` node, whose computed `pointer-events` is `auto`. The right-click goes to that node instead, so the browser sees no selection.

The workaround is to turn the browser's menu off with `BrowserContextMenu.disableContextMenu()`, so that Flutter's own menu shows. Toggling it while a `SelectionArea` is mounted, for example on hover, triggers #186459 on stable (fixed on master by #186553). Even with it turned off once at startup, the menu's Copy button runs into a separate issue: #194449.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/semantics.dart';

void main() {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics();

title: [Web] With semantics enabled, SelectableText copies other text than the highlighted selection
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the sample below with `flutter run -d chrome` (also reproduces with `flutter build web --release`).
2. Triple-click "Paragraph four".
3. Press Cmd+C (Ctrl+C), then paste somewhere.

The sample calls `SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics()`. Without that line, everything works. An app without it gets the same bug as soon as a user activates Flutter web's hidden "Enable accessibility" button, so screen reader users hit it in any Flutter web app.

### Expected results

The clipboard holds "Paragraph four: triple-click here, then press Cmd+C.", the paragraph Flutter highlights.

### Actual results

Flutter highlights paragraph four, but the clipboard holds "Paragraph five.\n", the next paragraph.

Without `ensureSemantics()`, the highlighted paragraph is copied.

What I found: with semantics enabled, the `SemanticTextField` role puts a transparent `<textarea>` over the text, with the whole text in it. That textarea accepts pointer events (`acceptsPointerEvents`), and its text is laid out in the browser's default font (Chrome's computed style is `13.3333px monospace`), not in the app's font. So its lines wrap and stack differently from what Flutter paints. The browser's own selection in that textarea (which Cmd+C copies) then lands on other text than Flutter's selection. Without semantics, the hidden textarea used by `DefaultTextEditingStrategy` is focused and holds the right selection.

Workaround: `SelectionArea` around a `Text` instead of `SelectableText`, which does not create a textarea.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:flutter/semantics.dart';

void main() {
  WidgetsFlutterBinding.ensureInitialized();
  SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics();
  runApp(
    const MaterialApp(
      home: Scaffold(
        body: Padding(padding: EdgeInsets.all(24), child: SelectableText(text)),
      ),
    ),
  );
}

const text = '''Paragraph one.

Paragraph two, a little longer so that it takes some room on its line.

https://example.com/a/very/long/address?code=97419fa9368553036f6d410be97879144bab42437dfc822748efed2823e81b3a1e1da69b6f7f9eafd38ab9c4e17f3bdb7502fa2a39a0fc4b543c743b13e52d95

title: [Web] With semantics enabled, the Copy button of SelectionArea's context menu does nothing
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the sample below with `flutter run -d chrome`.
2. Double-click "Select" to select it.
3. Right-click the selection: Flutter's context menu opens (the sample turns the browser's menu off).
4. Click Copy, then paste somewhere.

The sample calls `SemanticsBinding.instance.ensureSemantics()`. Without that line, everything works. An app without it gets the same bug as soon as a user activates Flutter web's hidden "Enable accessibility" button, so screen reader users hit it in any Flutter web app.

### Expected results

The clipboard holds "Select".

### Actual results

The menu closes, the selection is cleared, and the clipboard is unchanged. The button's `onPressed` is never called: a `contextMenuBuilder` that logs in `onPressed` logs nothing.

Without `ensureSemantics()`, Copy works.

What I think happens: with semantics enabled, the click lands on the button's semantics node, which takes the focus first. `SelectableRegion._handleFocusChanged` then clears the selection because the region lost the focus. That hides the toolbar before the tap reaches the button.

Workaround: keep the toolbar's buttons out of the focus tree.

```dart
SelectionArea(
  contextMenuBuilder: (context, state) => ExcludeFocus(
    child: AdaptiveTextSelectionToolbar.selectableRegion(
      selectableRegionState: state,
    ),
  ),
  child: ...,
)
```

title: [proposal] - flutter create templates ship outdated dependency versions and require manual built-in Kotlin migration
body:
### Use case

When creating new projects with the latest stable Flutter (`flutter create`), the generated templates are already out of date, so every new project needs manual fixes right after creation:

1. The project still needs the manual "Migrate to built-in Kotlin" steps (https://docs.flutter.dev/release/breaking-changes/migrate-to-built-in-kotlin/for-app-developers), even though it was generated seconds ago by the Flutter tool itself.
2. Default dependency versions in the templates are behind pub.dev:
   - App: `cupertino_icons: ^1.0.8` (latest: `^2.0.0`)
   - Plugin: `plugin_platform_interface: ^2.0.8` (latest: `^2.1.8`)
   - Plugin (web): `web: ^1.0.0` (latest: `^1.1.1`)
3. `flutter create --template=package` generates no `example/` app, unlike plugins.

Is your feature request related to a problem?

Yes. Every new app/plugin/package starts in an outdated state. Developers have to (a) manually apply the built-in Kotlin migration to a brand-new project, (b) manually bump dependency constraints, and (c) manually create an example app for packages. This is repetitive, easy to forget, and gives a poor first impression of the "latest" template. It also makes pub.dev scoring worse for packages that ship without an example.

Question: why doesn't `flutter create` generate the built-in Kotlin configuration by default? Since the template is fully controlled by the Flutter tool, I would expect a fresh project (app and plugin) to already be in the migrated state. If there is a technical reason (AGP/Gradle minimum versions, compatibility with older plugins, etc.), it would be helpful to document it in the migration guide.

Requested changes:
- Generate the built-in Kotlin setup by default in app and plugin templates.
- Update template dependency defaults to the latest versions (and ideally add a CI check so they don't drift behind in the future).
- Generate a minimal `example/` for `--template=package` (or add a flag such as `--with-example`).

Describe the alternative solutions you’ve considered:

- Manually applying the built-in Kotlin migration after every `flutter create`.
- Running `flutter pub upgrade --major-versions` after creating a project, which fixes dependency constraints but must be repeated for every new project.
- Manually running `flutter create example` inside the package folder to add an example app.
- I'm not aware of any package on pub.dev that solves this, since it is about the defaults of the `flutter create` command itself.

### Proposal

Update the `flutter create` templates so that a freshly generated project is already up to date and needs no manual fixes:

1. App and plugin templates generate the built-in Kotlin configuration by default (per https://docs.flutter.dev/release/breaking-changes/migrate-to-built-in-kotlin/for-app-developers), so no migration is needed on a newly created project.

2. Template dependency defaults match the latest published versions:
   - `cupertino_icons: ^2.0.0` (currently generates `^1.0.8`)
[truncated]

title: Proposal: Desktop support for the AdSense plugin (Windows, macOS, Linux)
body:
The package only supports web today, so Flutter desktop builds have no way to serve ads at all.

Desktop Flutter apps are growing; players, tools, wrappers, all kinds of stuff. The lack of any monetization path is one of the reasons developers pick Electron over Flutter for desktop, or skip desktop completely.

Desktop demand already exists. This doesn't need mobile AdMob inventory; desktop display demand can be filled from AdSense/Ad Manager through real-time bidding, the same way mediation layers route third-party demand on mobile today.

Could Google add a desktop implementation? Even one or two formats (banner, interstitial) would cover most desktop app use cases. Happy to help test if there's any appetite for it.

title: ReorderableList: gap flips on every pointer move when the dragged item is taller than the item above it
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Build a `ReorderableListView` (or `SliverReorderableList`) whose items have different heights, for example `[68, 85, 126, 97, 54, 106, 110, 119]`.
2. Long-press the item of height 106 (index 5) and drag it **up**, slowly, over the item of height 54 (index 4) above it.
3. Keep the finger moving slowly while the top of the dragged item is in the upper half of item 4 (a band of about 26 px here).

The widget test below reproduces it deterministically.

### Expected results

Item 4 slides down once and stays down while the finger rests or creeps inside that band. Each new position of the finger gives the same gap position as the previous check.

### Actual results

Item 4 flips between its resting position and its pushed-down position on **every** pointer move, however small (0.5 px in the test). On a device this looks like the rows below the dragged item flickering, and any app reacting to the gap moving (for example with a haptic) fires repeatedly.

The gap calculation in `SliverReorderableListState._dragUpdateItems` is not idempotent in this situation:

- In state "gap above item 4" (item 4 shifted down by the drag extent), nothing in the loop matches except the dragged item's own slot, whose branch `if (item.index == _dragIndex!) { if (itemMiddle <= proxyItemEnd && proxyItemEnd <= itemEnd) newIndex = _dragIndex!; }` sets the gap back to the dragged index. Item 4 moves back up.
- In state "gap in own slot", item 4 is at rest and its branch `itemStart <= proxyItemStart && proxyItemStart <= itemMiddle` moves the gap above item 4 again.

Both branches match whenever the dragged item is taller than the item above it: the proxy's top is in that item's upper half while the proxy's bottom is still in the lower half of its own slot. The band is `[max(top_k, top_k + h - g/2), top_k + h/2]` for a dragged extent `g` and an upper neighbour of height `h`, so it never occurs with equal-height items, which is probably why it went unnoticed.

The own-slot branch was added in #151026 (for #150843). Since #172380, `_dragEnd` already treats `_insertIndex == item.index + 1` as "returned to the start", and `_handleReorderItem` already normalises `newIndex > oldIndex`, so that branch seems redundant now. Skipping the dragged item in the loop for the forward direction, as the reverse branch already does (`if (item.index == _dragIndex! || !item.mounted) continue;`), fixes the flip, and the existing regression tests for #150843, #88331 and #110949 still pass with that change (checked on 3.44.1).

Still present on `master` as of today.

title: [Linux] Impeller (default since 3.47) causes jank on pointer-driven repaints on AMD radeonsi/Mesa (Wayland); Skia opt-out is smooth — affects debug and release
body:
### Environment
- Flutter 3.47.7 stable (engine `deb287481e`), Dart 3.13.5, snap install
- Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS, GNOME on Wayland, kernel 6.8.0-146-generic
- GPU: AMD Radeon Vega 8 (Picasso), Mesa 25.2.8 (radeonsi, ACO), OpenGL 4.6
- HiDPI: 2560x1440 at 2x scale

### Summary
Since 3.47 (Impeller became the default Linux desktop renderer), the app stutters whenever the pointer moves over the UI (hover-driven repaints of custom-painted widgets: table, heatmap grid, 3D view). The same app was smooth on Flutter 3.38.x (Skia). Switching the renderer makes the jank appear/disappear deterministically (A→B→A tested in one session, only variable = the renderer), in **both debug and release** builds.

### Steps to reproduce
1. `flutter run -d linux` on 3.47.7 (Impeller default) → move pointer across the UI → visible jank.
2. `flutter run -d linux --no-enable-impeller` (Skia) → same interaction → smooth.
3. Repeat (1) → jank returns.
4. Release: `flutter build linux --release` → **same jank**.
   Note: setting `FLUTTER_ENGINE_SWITCH_1=enable-impeller=false` in the environment has **no effect in release** builds — the release `libflutter_linux_gtk.so` does not contain the `FLUTTER_ENGINE_SWITCH_*` parsing that the debug engine has (the two engine binaries differ), and `--no-enable-impeller` is documented as debug-only.

### Renderer identification
Impeller runs print:

```
[IMPORTANT:flutter/shell/platform/embedder/embedder_surface_gl_impeller.cc(126)] Using the Impeller rendering backend (OpenGLESSDF).
```

Skia runs never print it — so on Linux desktop the renderer is OpenGL ES + SDF text, not Vulkan.

### Additional context
- Several `Timed out waiting for OpenGL frame of size 2560x1440 (have 1280x720)` warnings appear during startup with **both** renderers, so they seem unrelated (size negotiation at 2x scale); mentioned only as possibly related observations.
- Workaround we ship: `fl_dart_project_set_enable_impeller(project, FALSE)` in the Linux runner — works for debug and release. Since this opt-out is deprecated upstream, we'd rather stay on Impeller long-term.
- No raster/UI thread profile yet and not reduced to a minimal template app — happy to provide a DevTools timeline under hover or a minimal repro if needed.

[material_ui] Nested IconButtonThemes drop the Material 3 Expressive opt-in (IconButtonThemeData.variant isn't inherited)
body:
### Problem

`IconButtonThemeData.variant` opts icon buttons into Material 3 Expressive (flutter/packages#12832). `IconButton` resolves it with:

```dart
IconButtonTheme.of(context).variant ?? StyleVariant.material3
```

`IconButtonTheme.of` only returns the **closest** `IconButtonTheme`. If that theme doesn't set `variant` (for example, it only sets `style`), its `null` variant becomes `StyleVariant.material3`, even when an ancestor opted in. Once any `IconButtonTheme` widget is above the button, `ThemeData.iconButtonTheme` isn't consulted either.

Some Material widgets wrap their children in an internal `IconButtonTheme` that doesn't set a variant, so the opt-in currently has no effect on icon buttons in:

* `ListTile` leading and trailing
* `InputDecorator` prefix and suffix icons (for example, in a `TextField`)
* `AppBar` leading and actions when their icon colors are customized, for example with `foregroundColor`, `iconTheme`, or `actionsIconTheme`

### Steps to reproduce

```dart
MaterialApp(
  theme: ThemeData(
    iconButtonTheme: const IconButtonThemeData(variant: StyleVariant.material3Expressive),
  ),
  home: Material(
    child: Column(
      children: <Widget>[
        // Material 3 Expressive: a square (rounded rectangle) button.
        IconButton(
          onPressed: () {},
          style: const ButtonStyle(shapeVariant: ButtonShapeVariant.square),
          icon: const Icon(Icons.add),
        ),
        // Material 3: a stadium-shaped button, because ListTile's internal
        // IconButtonTheme doesn't set a variant.
        ListTile(
          title: const Text('Title'),
          trailing: IconButton(
            onPressed: () {},
            style: const ButtonStyle(shapeVariant: ButtonShapeVariant.square),
            icon: const Icon(Icons.add),
          ),
        ),
      ],
    ),
  ),
)
```

**Expected:** both buttons use the Material 3 Expressive square shape.

**Actual:** only the first one does. The same happens when an `IconButtonTheme` that only sets `style` is nested inside an `IconButtonTheme` with `variant: StyleVariant.material3Expressive`.

Tested with material_ui 1.6.0 and Flutter 3.47.7.

### Proposal

Treat a `null` variant as "inherit" instead of "Material 3", as described in the [material_ui and cupertino_ui architecture doc](https://flutter.dev/go/material-ui-cupertino-ui-architecture) ("Defaults to the closest non-null variant"):

* Add `IconButtonTheme.variantOf(BuildContext)`. It returns the first non-null `variant` of the enclosing `IconButtonTheme`s, depending on each theme it visits, and then falls back to `ThemeData.iconButtonTheme.variant`. `IconButton` would use `IconButtonTheme.variantOf(context) ?? StyleVariant.material3`.
* `style` keeps its current behavior: the closest theme replaces its ancestors.
* An explicit `variant: StyleVariant.material3` still opts a subtree out.
* Every component that adds Material 3 Expressive support uses the same resolution.

Once we have added the fix, we

title: [Impeller] Reduce per-frame CPU and GLES state overhead on WebGL2 ☂️
body:
When rendering 100–1,000-element 2D and text scenes on WebGL2 (`--wasm` with Impeller for Web, #174980), [`RenderPassGLES`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/e81f444cc0835365bda671876183e3f9cd149925/engine/src/flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/gles/render_pass_gles.cc#L428-L695) and [`BufferBindingsGLES`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/e81f444cc0835365bda671876183e3f9cd149925/engine/src/flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/gles/buffer_bindings_gles.cc#L201-L343) issue redundant per-command Emscripten→WebGL2 FFI calls (`6,383` WebGL2 calls/frame on a 128-sprite scene and `81,165` calls/frame on a 1,000-cell dashboard instead of deduplicating unchanged pass state), while [`ParagraphSkia::Paint`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/e81f444cc0835365bda671876183e3f9cd149925/engine/src/flutter/txt/src/skia/paragraph_skia.cc#L59-L124) and [`RenderTargetCache::CreateOffscreen`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/e81f444cc0835365bda671876183e3f9cd149925/engine/src/flutter/impeller/entity/render_target_cache.cc#L58-L163) repeat CPU work across frames.

### Tracked Work & Areas Under Investigation

- [x] #193407 — Compile `wasm_release` and `wasm_profile` with `IMPELLER_DEBUG=0` to strip per-draw `glPushDebugGroupKHR` / `glGetError` WebGL2 round-trips.
- [x] #193427 — Deduplicate orthogonal `RenderPassGLES` blend, stencil, cull, depth, scissor, and viewport state across draw calls.
- [x] #193922 — Consolidate per-pass GLES state into `RenderPassStateCache` and deduplicate texture sampler parameter calls (`glTexParameteri`) via `SamplerStateCache`.
- [ ] #194135 — Deduplicate per-pass `GL_ARRAY_BUFFER` / `GL_ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER` bindings, enabled vertex attribute arrays (`uint64_t` bitmask), `glVertexAttribPointer` descriptors, active texture units, and sampler location uniforms (`glUniform1i`) via `VertexAttribStateCache` (`-51.3%` to `-57.3%` total WebGL2 calls/frame).
- [ ] #194123 — Cache `DlText` on `txt::ParagraphSkia` and `Skwasm::Paragraph` across repeated `canvas.drawParagraph` calls (invalidated on `Layout()`) and use header-only `SkBulkGlyphMetrics` in [`MakeTextFrameFromTextBlobSkia`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/e81f444cc0835365bda671876183e3f9cd149925/engine/src/flutter/impeller/typographer/backends/skia/text_frame_skia.cc#L45-L58) (`-29.1%` to `-48.3%` `canvas_drawParagraph` CPU self-time).
- [x] #194139 — Implement Wasm worker futex semaphores (`emscripten_atomic_wait_u32` / `emscripten_atomic_notify` on workers, `thread_local`-cached spin fallback on main browser thread) to prevent cross-thread `FT_Face` races (#193695).
- [ ] #194532 — Pass `/*prepare_rtree=*/true` in `skwasm`'s `PictureRecorder::BeginRecording` and skip `FirstPassDispatcher::drawText` when `cull_rect_state_.back().IsEmpty()` (`31.8x` faster `dynamic_clip_on_static_picture` on WIMP: `38.41 ms` -> `1.21 ms`; `2.40x` faster on Skwasm: `1.75 ms` -> `0.73 ms`).

title: [Android][HCPP] GPU memory leaks each time a full-screen overlay with an animation appears above a platform view
body:
## Summary

With hybrid composition++ (`io.flutter.embedding.android.EnableHcpp=true`), showing and removing a
full-screen Flutter layer with an animated child (a translucent `ColoredBox` + `CircularProgressIndicator`)
above a `SurfaceView` platform view leaks GPU memory every time. The memory is counted by the Mali kbase
driver against the app's process and is never released, even after the overlay is gone and the app sits idle.

The same app does not grow when the overlay is not shown (media changes only, or the platform view being
resized on each change), and an app drawing its video into a `SurfaceProducer` texture instead of an HCPP
platform view does not grow at all.

## Environment

- Flutter 3.47.0 (stable), framework 4cf2416426, engine 59d54a2b28, Dart 3.13.0
- Impeller, Vulkan backend; HCPP active (`HybridAndroidViewController.checkIfSupported()` = true)
- Xiaomi Mi TV box (MiTV-AFMU0), Android 14 (API 34), Amlogic SoC, Mali-G310
- Profile build; Media3 ExoPlayer 1.11.1 rendering into the `SurfaceView`

## Minimal reproduction

**Repository:** https://github.com/amenti-stack/flutter-hcpp-overlay-leak

A single-screen app (attached): one ExoPlayer rendering into a `SurfaceView` in a platform view created
with `PlatformViewsService.initHybridAndroidView`, full screen. Every 6 s it loads a new public test video
(same player, same surface). Two phases of 40 changes:

- **Phase A:** on each change, a full-screen `ColoredBox(Color(0x99000000))` with a centred
  `CircularProgressIndicator` is shown above the platform view for 2 s, then removed.
- **Phase B:** on each change, the platform view is resized (full screen ↔ a 4:3 box), no overlay.

No input, no screenshots or dumpsys during the run.

## Measurement

The Mali kbase driver's per-process count (`/sys/class/misc/mali0/device/gpu_memory`, used_pages × 4 KB
summed over the process's contexts), every 10 s:

| | GPU memory |
|---|---|
| start | 32 MB |
| after phase A (40 overlay show/hide cycles) | **44 MB**, rising in 4 MB steps |
| after phase B (40 resizes, no overlay) | 44 MB (flat) |
| idle afterwards | 44 MB (never released) |

A first run of the same app with only a small text banner (not full screen, no animation) over the
platform view, for 300 media changes, stayed flat (28 → 32 MB).

In our production app the overlay is a loading screen shown on every channel change. There the growth was
**0.56 MB per change** (81 → 250 MB over 300 changes), never released. With HCPP disabled (video in a
`SurfaceProducer` texture) the same 300 changes stayed level (49 → 39 MB).

## Expected

Showing and removing a Flutter overlay above an HCPP platform view returns its GPU memory.

## Impact

On 1–2 GB Android TV boxes a few hundred channel changes bring the process to the size at which the
low-memory killer ends it. We have disabled HCPP as a workaround.

Raw sample files are available on request.

## flutter doctor -v (summary)

```
[√] Flutter (Channel stable, 3.47.0, on Microsoft Windows [Ve

title: [flutter_tools] Remove AzureDetector IMDS probe from BotDetector
body:
[`AzureDetector.isRunningOnAzure`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/1d71d2fd583ba7d25ea7f491b28293fe0d3ca9a5/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/base/bot_detector.dart#L86-L122) probes the Azure Instance Metadata Service (`http://169.254.169.254/metadata/instance`) on startup and caches `isRunningOnBot = true` in `~/.flutter_tool_state`, which classifies every Azure-hosted developer workstation as a CI bot and forces `BotDetector.isRunningOnBot` to be asynchronous.

- **Root cause**: [`BotDetector.isRunningOnBot`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/1d71d2fd583ba7d25ea7f491b28293fe0d3ca9a5/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/base/bot_detector.dart#L73-L79) falls back to an HTTP GET to `169.254.169.254` whenever no CI environment variable is set, treating any HTTP response (including `HttpException` at `#L108-L111`) as a bot and persisting that result in `persistentToolState`. Meanwhile, [`bot_detector.dart#L42`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/1d71d2fd583ba7d25ea7f491b28293fe0d3ca9a5/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/base/bot_detector.dart#L42) checks `_platform.environment.containsKey('CI')`, treating `CI=false` and `CI=0` as bots.
- **Impact**: Human developers using GitHub Codespaces, Microsoft Dev Box, or Azure VMs are permanently flagged as bots—suppressing analytics (`NoOpAnalytics()`), skipping update checks ([`flutter_command_runner.dart#L477`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/1d71d2fd583ba7d25ea7f491b28293fe0d3ca9a5/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/runner/flutter_command_runner.dart#L477)), and auto-deleting `~/.gradle` without prompting on Gradle errors ([`gradle_errors.dart#L195`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/1d71d2fd583ba7d25ea7f491b28293fe0d3ca9a5/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/android/gradle_errors.dart#L195))—while non-Azure users pay up to a 250ms–1s network timeout on first run or hit proxy redirect issues (see [`#189456`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/189456)). Azure Pipelines CI runs are already detected synchronously via `TF_BUILD` ([`bot_detector.dart#L69`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/1d71d2fd583ba7d25ea7f491b28293fe0d3ca9a5/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/base/bot_detector.dart#L69)).

### Proposed Fix

- Remove `AzureDetector` and the `persistentToolState.isRunningOnBot` cache from [`packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/base/bot_detector.dart`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/1d71d2fd583ba7d25ea7f491b28293fe0d3ca9a5/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/base/bot_detector.dart#L73-L122), matching [`pkg/dartdev`](https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/blob/97584cc61b49d97a279e16df1c43338bf64f7c02/pkg/dartdev/lib/src/unified_analytics.dart#L207-L255).
- Require `CI` in [`bot_detector.dart#L42`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/1d71d2fd583ba7d25ea7f491b28293fe0d3ca9a5/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/base/bot_detector.dart#L42) to be non-empty and not `'false'` or `'0'` (and delegate to `package:unified_analytics` once centralized in [`dart-lang/tools#2672`](https://github.com/dart-lang/to

title: [Linux] Disposing an FlEngine calls eglTerminate() on the process-wide EGLDisplay, crashing the remaining windows/engines
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create --platforms=linux bug`
2. In `linux/runner/my_application.cc`, add the code below. It opens a second `GtkWindow` whose `FlView` is created with `fl_view_new()`, so it has its own `FlEngine`, and destroys that window after 5 seconds.
3. `flutter run -d linux --release`
4. Wait about 6 seconds. The sample forces a repaint of the first window 1 second after destroying the second one. Hovering over or clicking the first window triggers the same crash.

### Expected results

The second window and its engine go away, and the first window keeps working.

### Actual results

The app crashes with SIGSEGV at the next repaint of the remaining window. The crash happens on the GTK main thread, inside `gdk_window_end_draw_frame()`, right after GDK logs `eglMakeCurrent failed` five times. See the logs below.

Test environment: Ubuntu 26.04, GNOME on Wayland, Flutter 3.47.7 stable.

| Driver | Result |
|---|---|
| NVIDIA proprietary 595.84 (RTX 5060 Ti) | Crashed 3/3 |
| Mesa llvmpipe (`__EGL_VENDOR_LIBRARY_FILENAMES=/usr/share/glvnd/egl_vendor.d/50_mesa.json LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`) | Crashed 4/4 |

**Analysis**

1. `fl_opengl_manager_dispose()` in `shell/platform/linux/fl_opengl_manager.cc` destroys its three contexts and then calls `eglTerminate(self->display)`.
2. The display comes from `eglGetPlatformDisplayEXT(EGL_PLATFORM_WAYLAND_EXT, gdk_wayland_display_get_wl_display(...))`. Per the EGL spec, this returns the same `EGLDisplay` for the same native display. So the display is shared by every `FlEngine` in the process and by GDK's own GL contexts.
3. EGL displays are not reference counted, unless `EGL_KHR_display_reference` is used. Disposing any one engine therefore terminates EGL for everyone, and the next GDK repaint fails.
4. Every engine creates an `FlOpenGLManager` in `fl_engine_init()`. This affects any app or plugin that disposes one of several engines, for example multi-window plugins such as desktop_multi_window (one engine per window) and headless engines.

Evidence from gdb:
- A breakpoint on `eglTerminate` shows it is called from the engine's dispose (`g_object_unref` chain) right after the second window is destroyed. The `eglMakeCurrent failed` warnings and the crash follow.
- Making `eglTerminate` return `EGL_TRUE` without running it (gdb `return 1` at the breakpoint) removes the crash completely. The first window keeps working.

The code is unchanged on master (`fl_opengl_manager.cc`, checked on 2026-10-14).

**Suggested fix:** don't call `eglTerminate()` in `fl_opengl_manager_dispose()`, because the display belongs to the process and GDK, not to one engine. Alternatively, share one reference-counted manager per display and terminate only when the last one is disposed.

**Related:** MixinNetwork/flutter-plugins#488 (desktop_multi_window: closing a child window crashes the app on Linux).

**Side note:** `fl_view_dispose()` also calls `fl_engine_remove_view()` for the implicit view. This logs `'Flutt

title: [camera] integration test failed because of thread merge causing sleep to block the main thread
body:
1. Follow https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/191202 to run integration test for camera plugin
2. Observe 2 of the tests (control audio/video bit rate tests) failed (sometimes got stuck when I tried it)   

The test failed because this sleep: 

https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/24a3833ea0c602a64154e99d4f1ee9b420c9c714/packages/camera/camera_avfoundation/example/integration_test/camera_test.dart#L288-L297

Previously, before thread merge, this worked, because sleep only blocks the UI thread. 

Now, after thread merge, the UI thread and platform thread are the same. So `sleep` would block all the internal setups (such as dart's event channel set up and `DispatchQueue.main.async` calls on the native side. 

Then once sleep is done, it stops the video recording immediately. 

```
        await controller.startVideoRecording();
        sleep(const Duration(milliseconds: 500));
        final XFile file = await controller.stopVideoRecording();
```

The solution is to use `await Future<void>.delayed(const Duration(milliseconds: 500));` instead

title: [iOS] Accessibility hit test in a scrollable never reaches a platform view's native subviews
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create --platforms ios bug`, then replace `lib/main.dart` and `ios/Runner/AppDelegate.swift` with the code sample below. It shows a bare `UISegmentedControl` in a `UiKitView` twice: once outside any scrollable, once as the first child of a `ListView`.
2. Run it on an iOS simulator.
3. Run the UI test below in a UI-testing bundle targeting the app (`XCUIApplication(bundleIdentifier:)`). It prints each segment's frame and `isHittable`.

### Expected results

Every segment is hittable, inside the `ListView` as well as outside it.

### Actual results

Outside the list every segment is hittable. Inside the list no segment is, though each has a real frame and the segmented control itself reads hittable:

```

REPRO control0 segment1 label=Out2 frame=(86.0, 78.0, 70.0, 32.0) hittable=true
REPRO control0 segment2 label=Out3 frame=(156.0, 78.0, 70.0, 32.0) hittable=true
REPRO control1 frame=(16.0, 142.0, 370.0, 32.0) hittable=true
REPRO control1 segment0 label=In1 frame=(16.0, 142.0, 123.0, 32.0) hittable=false
REPRO control1 segment1 label=In2 frame=(139.0, 142.0, 123.0, 32.0) hittable=false
REPRO control1 segment2 label=In3 frame=(262.0, 142.0, 124.0, 32.0) hittable=false
```

The window's accessibility hit test at an in-list segment's centre returns the list's `FlutterSemanticsScrollView`; outside the list it returns the `UISegment`. VoiceOver touch exploration goes through the same hit test, so a VoiceOver user cannot touch a single segment inside a scrolling list (VoiceOver itself was not run, the simulator has none). A `UISwitch` and a `UISlider` in the same list stay hittable.

**Root cause** (engine at `5f77625673248ee5846fbcaf5d3e1a3878386fd7`):

- `SemanticsObject.mm:567` `_accessibilityHitTest:withEvent:` returns `[self search:point]`, and `search:` (`:543`) returns the first node holding the point that `isFocusable`.

A `ListView`'s node carries `scrollToOffset | scrollUp` (`actions=8388624` in a widget test at the same revision), so the list counts as focusable.
- The platform view's node has no label or action, so `search:` skips it and returns the scroll node. The platform view's own subtree is never asked.

title: Add PasswordRules to describe password requirements for autofill (iOS UITextInputPasswordRules)
body:
### Use case

Apps that create accounts often have password requirements, such as a minimum length or
required character classes. On iOS, when a text field uses `AutofillHints.newPassword`,
the system suggests a strong password. The app has no way to describe its requirements,
so the suggested password can be rejected by the app or its backend. The user then has to
type a password manually.

Native iOS apps solve this with [`UITextInputTraits.passwordRules`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uitextinputpasswordrules).
Flutter does not expose it today. The only workaround is to embed a native `UITextField`
in a platform view, which loses the Flutter text field features. I found no package on
pub.dev that solves this, and it can't be done in a package because it needs the engine's
text input view.

### Proposal

Add a platform-agnostic `PasswordRules` class that describes password requirements, and
let text fields pass it to the platform through the autofill configuration.

```dart
@immutable
class PasswordRules {
  const PasswordRules({
    this.required = const <Set<PasswordCharacterClass>>[],
    this.allowed = const <PasswordCharacterClass>{},
    this.minLength,
    this.maxLength,
    this.maxConsecutive,
  });

  /// Each set must be satisfied by at least one character from that set.
  final List<Set<PasswordCharacterClass>> required;

  /// The characters that may appear in the password, in addition to [required].
  final Set<PasswordCharacterClass> allowed;

  final int? minLength;
  final int? maxLength;

  /// The maximum number of identical consecutive characters.
  final int? maxConsecutive;
}
```

`PasswordCharacterClass` would cover upper case, lower case, digits, special characters,
ASCII printable, Unicode, and custom character sets (for example `-_`).

Usage:

```dart
TextField(
  autofillHints: const <String>[AutofillHints.newPassword],
  passwordRules: const PasswordRules(
    required: <Set<PasswordCharacterClass>>[
      <PasswordCharacterClass>{PasswordCharacterClass.upper},
      <PasswordCharacterClass>{PasswordCharacterClass.digit},
    ],
    minLength: 12,
  ),
  obscureText: true,
)
```

Details:

- The new `PasswordRules? passwordRules` property would be added to `AutofillConfiguration`
  and `EditableText`, and passed through by the Material and Cupertino text fields.
- The default is `null`, which keeps the platform's default behavior. Flutter would not
  hardcode Apple's default rules, because Apple does not document them and they can change.
- On the platform channel, the rules are sent as a structured map inside the `autofill`
  configuration, not as an Apple-specific string. Each embedder converts the map to its own
  format.
- iOS: the engine builds a password rules descriptor from the map and sets
  `UITextInputPasswordRules` on the text input view.
- Other platforms ignore the value for now. Android has no equivalent API that I know of.
  Web could map it to the `passwordrules` HTML attribute lat
[truncated]

title: [webview_flutter_wkwebview] HTTP Digest authentication challenges are not forwarded to onHttpAuthRequest on iOS
body:
### Summary

On iOS, `NavigationDelegate.onHttpAuthRequest` appears to be called only for HTTP Basic and NTLM challenges. Judging from the code, a server that protects a page with HTTP Digest authentication never reaches the callback, so an app cannot show its own credential prompt for it.

### Cause

In `WebKitNavigationDelegate`, the `didReceiveAuthenticationChallenge` handler only dispatches these authentication methods to `onHttpAuthRequest`:

```dart
case NSUrlAuthenticationMethod.httpBasic:
case NSUrlAuthenticationMethod.httpNtlm:
```

`NSUrlAuthenticationMethod.httpDigest` is not handled. It falls through to the default response at the end of the handler, `UrlSessionAuthChallengeDisposition.performDefaultHandling` without credentials.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a `WebViewController` with a `NavigationDelegate` that sets `onHttpAuthRequest` and answers with `request.onProceed(...)`.
2. Load a URL protected by HTTP Digest authentication on iOS.
3. Check whether `onHttpAuthRequest` is called.

I found this by reading the code and have not verified on a device what the page shows in that case.

### Expected

`onHttpAuthRequest` is called for Digest challenges as well, like for Basic and NTLM. `HttpAuthRequest.onProceed` takes a `WebViewCredential` (user and password), which should be enough to answer a Digest challenge too.

### Proposed fix

Add `NSUrlAuthenticationMethod.httpDigest` next to the existing cases. We currently apply this one-line change as a local patch on top of 3.25.1. The dispatch is unchanged on `main`.

### Versions

- webview_flutter_wkwebview 3.25.1
- Flutter 3.41.9

title: [macOS] SemanticsService.sendAnnouncement Future does not complete because accessibility channel handler omits reply
body:
## Summary

On macOS, the embedder's handler for the `flutter/accessibility` channel never calls its `reply` callback. `SemanticsService.sendAnnouncement` (and the deprecated `SemanticsService.announce`) ends with `await SystemChannels.accessibility.send(...)`, which only completes when the platform replies. According to the source, the returned `Future` therefore never completes on macOS. The Windows, Linux and Android embedders do reply.

The iOS embedder contains the same handler pattern (source reading only, not checked at run time; see below).

This report is only about the missing reply. I have **not** verified whether VoiceOver speaks the announcement.

## Evidence, kept separate

### 1. Source reading (Flutter 3.44.8, commit `058e0af2c2b57e369d905a03ac9748b0ebf543c6`)

- Framework: [`semantics_service.dart` L81-L93](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/058e0af2c2b57e369d905a03ac9748b0ebf543c6/packages/flutter/lib/src/semantics/semantics_service.dart#L81-L93). `sendAnnouncement` ends with `await SystemChannels.accessibility.send(event.toMap())`.
- macOS: [`FlutterEngine.mm` L1384-L1386](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/058e0af2c2b57e369d905a03ac9748b0ebf543c6/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/macos/framework/Source/FlutterEngine.mm#L1384-L1386):

  ```objc
  [_accessibilityChannel setMessageHandler:^(id message, FlutterReply reply) {
    [weakSelf handleAccessibilityEvent:message];
  }];
  ```

  `reply` is not called. `handleAccessibilityEvent:` ([L1533-L1556](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/058e0af2c2b57e369d905a03ac9748b0ebf543c6/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/darwin/macos/framework/Source/FlutterEngine.mm#L1533-L1556)) posts `NSAccessibilityAnnouncementRequestedNotification` and returns nothing to the channel.

title: [in_app_purchase_storekit] StoreKit 2 purchase uses Product.purchase(options:) without a scene; App Review rejected subscription purchases on iPad (iPadOS 27)
body:
### What package does this bug report belong to?

in_app_purchase

### What target platforms are you seeing this bug on?

iOS

### Have you already upgraded your packages?

Yes

### Dependency versions

<details><summary>pubspec.lock</summary>

```lock
  in_app_purchase:
    version: "3.3.1"
  in_app_purchase_platform_interface:
    version: "1.4.1"
  in_app_purchase_storekit:
    version: "0.4.13+2"
```

</details>

### Steps to reproduce

We could not reproduce this ourselves. App Review hit it on two submissions in a row:

1. Our app is a universal iOS app (iPhone and iPad) on the UIScene lifecycle (`FlutterSceneDelegate`), with StoreKit 2 enabled in `in_app_purchase_storekit`.
2. On an **iPad Air 11-inch (M3) running iPadOS 27.0**, App Review opened the purchase screen and bought an auto-renewable subscription (`buyNonConsumable` with an app account token).
3. The purchase failed, and Apple rejected the app under Guideline 2.1(b): "we tried to purchase the subscription and the app returned an error".

### Expected results

Apple's payment sheet opens and the purchase completes, as it does on iPhone.

### Actual results

The purchase fails before anything is charged.

- The sandbox App Store Server Notifications history holds no `SUBSCRIBED` notification from App Review in any review round, so StoreKit refused before the purchase completed.
- The same builds complete sandbox purchases on iPhone.
- On the iPad simulator with iPadOS 26.5 the payment sheet opens. We have no iPadOS 27 device, so we don't know the exact error StoreKit returned.

### Analysis

`InAppPurchasePlugin+StoreKit2.swift` buys with `product.purchase(options: purchaseOptions)`, which passes no UI context. Apple's documentation for [`Product.purchase(options:)`](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/storekit/product/purchase(options:)) says:

> Use `purchase(confirmIn:options:)` for apps that use UIKit. […] Use `purchase(options:)` for apps that runs on watchOS.

A Flutter iOS app is a UIKit app. Without a scene, StoreKit has to pick the window for the payment sheet itself. On iPad (resizable windows, Stage Manager) that seems to be the step that fails.

There are two more pointers in the same direction:

- In the iOS 18 SDK, the deprecation messages for the StoreKit 1 purchase APIs name `Product.purchase(confirmIn:options:)` as the replacement (see #170442).
- The plugin already resolves the window scene through `registrar?.viewController?.view.window?.windowScene` for `presentOfferCodeRedeemSheet`.

### Proposal

On iOS 17+, confirm the purchase in the window scene of the Flutter view. If that view has no window, use the foreground scene. Keep `purchase(options:)` only when there is no scene or the OS is older. On macOS 15.2+, `purchase(confirmIn:)` with the `NSWindow` could be used the same way.

We shipped exactly this as a patched copy of 0.4.13+2, and App Review approved the next build on the first try. That evidence is circumstantial, because Apple doesn't say whic

title: [widget_inspector] getRootWidgetTree cannot include creation locations without fullDetails
body:
### Use case

The Dart MCP server's `get_widget_tree` tool calls `ext.flutter.inspector.getRootWidgetTree` with `fullDetails: false`, so AI agents can see a running app's widget tree. Agents also need each widget's `creationLocation` to go from a node in the tree to the line of code that created it (dart-lang/ai#424). Today they have to select widgets one at a time with `getSelectedSummaryWidget` to get that.

### Problem

`creationLocation` is only added when `fullDetails` is true (`InspectorSerializationDelegate.additionalNodeProperties`). `fullDetails: true` uses the recursive `toJsonMap`, which overflowed the stack on large trees (flutter/devtools#8553), and is why callers use the reduced, iterative tree. So no caller can get both the reduced tree and creation locations.

### Proposal

An opt-in `withCreationLocations` parameter on `getRootWidgetTree` that adds `creationLocation` to each node of the reduced tree. It would go through the existing additional-properties callback that `withPreviews` already uses. The default stays off, so DevTools and other callers are unaffected.

[in_app_purchase_android] Migrate from deprecated setSubscriptionReplacementMode to SubscriptionProductReplacementParams
body:
### Summary

As of Google Play Billing Library 8.1.0 (and continuing in 9.x), `BillingFlowParams.SubscriptionUpdateParams.Builder.setSubscriptionReplacementMode` is deprecated in favor of `BillingFlowParams.ProductDetailsParams.SubscriptionProductReplacementParams` (`ProductDetailsParams.Builder.setSubscriptionProductReplacementParams`).

In https://github.com/flutter/packages/pull/12781 (fixing https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/189974), the deprecation warning in `MethodCallHandlerImpl.launchBillingFlow` was suppressed with `@SuppressWarnings("deprecation")` to avoid introducing a breaking API change during the Play Billing Library 9.1.0 update.

### Details

Migrating to `SubscriptionProductReplacementParams` is not a drop-in internal change:
- Replacement mode configuration moves from subscription-level (`SubscriptionUpdateParams`) to product-level (`ProductDetailsParams.SubscriptionProductReplacementParams`), which requires both `setOldProductId` and `setReplacementMode`.
- `SubscriptionProductReplacementParams.ReplacementMode` renumbered the replacement mode integer constants compared to `SubscriptionUpdateParams.ReplacementMode`, which affects the values exposed by the Dart `ReplacementMode` enum / Pigeon conversion.

This issue tracks migrating `in_app_purchase_android` to `SubscriptionProductReplacementParams` (and removing the deprecation suppression in `MethodCallHandlerImpl.java`) as a follow-up breaking change.

title: Replace dynamic free-port probing with OS port-0 binding
body:
## Problem

Across `flutter_tools`, `package:dwds`, `dev/bots`, `package:web_benchmarks`, and `flutter/devtools`, several code paths dynamically locate a "free" TCP port by probing a port (`ServerSocket.bind(..., 0)` or `RawSocket.connect`), closing the socket, and passing that port number to an HTTP server or child process (`Chrome`, `chromedriver`) to bind later. Other test harnesses hardcode fixed ports (`9999`, `10000`, `10001`), pushing downstream callers to add their own port probes.

Probing for a free port before binding has two flaws that cause recurring CI flakes:

1. **TOCTOU race condition**: Once the probe socket closes (or `RawSocket.connect` fails), the port is unreserved. Under parallel CI load, another test shard or process can claim the port before the target server or browser binds it. Worse, `RawSocket.connect` probes only detect sockets actively listening on `localhost`, missing sockets that are bound but not yet listening.
2. **Address-family and dual-stack mismatch**: The probe socket rarely matches the target bind's address family or socket flags. On macOS and Linux, an IPv4 socket bound to `127.0.0.1:P` or `0.0.0.0:P` does not conflict with an IPv6-only (`v6Only: true`) probe on `[::1]:P`.
   - For example, `dwds`'s `findUnusedPort()` probes `[::1]` with `v6Only: true`, then `HttpMultiServer.bind('any', port)` binds `[::]` dual-stack (`v6Only: false`). If the kernel hands out a port held by an IPv4 socket, the probe succeeds on `[::1]` and the subsequent `[::]` bind fails with `EADDRINUSE` (`errno = 48` on macOS, `98` on Linux). Under congested ephemeral port ranges, all 5 retry attempts fail in ~500ms.

The [Flutter Style Guide](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/main/docs/contributing/Style-guide-for-Flutter-repo.md#never-check-if-a-port-is-available-before-using-it-never-add-timeouts-and-other-race-conditions) already prohibits this pattern (*"Never check if a port is available before using it... Instead, have the code that opens the port pick an available port and return it"*), and `dev/bots/utils.dart` even names its helper `findAvailablePortAndPossiblyCauseFlakyTests()`.

### Past Flakes & Failures

| Date | Subsystem | Failure Mode & Impact | Links |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-10 | `flutter/packages` `DriveExamplesCommand` | Hardcoded `chromedriver --port=4444` inside the per-example loop combined with `chromedriver.kill()` without awaiting `exitCode`. When a package has multiple web examples (`google_maps_flutter_web`'s `example/latest` and `example/3-64`), the dying `chromedriver` from the first example still holds port `4444` when the second example spawns a new `chromedriver --port=4444`, so the second `chromedriver` fails to bind and exits immediately. | https://github.com/flutter/packages/pull/13355, [build 1](https://ci.chromium.org/b/8667405073082275745), [build 2](https://ci.chromium.org/b/8667406160854692097), [build 3](https://ci.chromium.org/b/8667756860257169345) |
| 2026-10 | `dwds` `startHttpServe

title: [Impeller] Off-frame rendering advances `RenderTargetCache`'s frame clock, evicting onscreen `saveLayer` targets
body:
I noticed this behavior too the other day when looking into https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/190613 but forgot to file an issue.  Here's gemini's writeup.

## Summary

The keep-alive in `RenderTargetCache` is counted in calls to `End()`. One onscreen frame is supposed to be one tick. In practice, every `impeller::Canvas` calls `Start()`/`End()` on the `ContentContext`'s single shared cache. That includes the canvases used for `Picture.toImageSync` / `toImage`, `Scene.toImage`, and screenshots. So every snapshot counts as a frame.

With the default `keep_alive_frame_count = 4`, if more than 4 snapshots run between two onscreen frames, the onscreen frame's cached `saveLayer` render targets are evicted. The next frame has to allocate them again. Apps that make several snapshots per frame (multi-pass effects, `toImageSync` chains) and also use `saveLayer` onscreen pay for new texture allocations every frame, even though their render targets never change.

## Where the cache ticks

- [`Canvas::SetupRenderPass`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/engine/src/flutter/impeller/display_list/canvas.cc#L1724) calls `renderer_.GetRenderTargetCache()->Start()`.
- [`Canvas::EndReplay`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/engine/src/flutter/impeller/display_list/canvas.cc#L2767) calls `renderer_.GetRenderTargetCache()->End()`.
- Both run for every `Canvas`, whatever it renders to. Callers include:
  - `RenderToTarget` (onscreen surfaces: `gpu_surface_metal_impeller.mm`, `gpu_surface_vulkan_impeller.cc`, `gpu_surface_gl_impeller.cc`, `embedder_external_view_embedder.cc`)
  - `DisplayListToTexture` (`snapshot_controller_impeller.cc` for `toImage`/`toImageSync`, `Rasterizer::ScreenshotLayerTreeAsImage`)

[`RenderTargetCache::End()`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/engine/src/flutter/impeller/entity/render_target_cache.cc#L23-L36):

```cpp
for (RenderTargetData& td : render_target_data_) {
  if (td.used_this_frame) {
    retain.push_back(td);
  } else if (td.keep_alive_frame_count > 0) {
    td.keep_alive_frame_count--;   // decremented once per Canvas, not per frame
    retain.push_back(td);
  }
}
```

## Expected

Cached render targets should survive `keep_alive_frame_count` **onscreen frames**, no matter how many snapshots run in between.

## Actual

Each snapshot `Canvas` that doesn't use a cached entry decrements that entry's keep-alive. Here `S` is the number of snapshots between two onscreen frames:

| Snapshots between frames | Effect on onscreen `saveLayer` targets |
|---|---|
| S ≤ 4 | Kept (the keep-alive resets to 4 whenever an entry is used) |
| S ≥ 5 | Evicted before the next frame, then reallocated |

The snapshots get no benefit in return: they can only reuse an entry whose size and config match exactly.

## Steps to reproduce

The Dart sample from #193941 almost reproduces this. That sample's `layer` and `snapshot` modes need to be combined, so that one frame has both onscreen `saveLayer`s and ≥5 `toIma
