title: [native assets] iOS: two code assets that map to the same framework name are silently renamed (Foo1.framework) instead of failing like duplicate file names do
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Use two packages whose build hooks each bundle a dynamic library that ends up with the same framework name on Apple, but with different file names. A real case:
   - `flutter_edge_ai_litertlm` emits `libLiteRtLm.dylib`;
   - `llamadart` 0.11.1 (default runtimes) emits `LiteRtLm`.
2. Add both to an app and run `flutter build ios --simulator --debug` (Flutter 3.47.3; the same code is on master).
3. List `build/ios/iphonesimulator/Runner.app/Frameworks`.

### Expected results

The build fails with an error naming both asset IDs, as it does on Android. The same app fails there with:

```
Application asset verification failed
- Duplicate dynamic library file name "libLiteRtLm.so" for the following asset ids: "package:flutter_edge_ai_litertlm/src/native/LiteRtLm", "package:llamadart/litert_lm_LiteRtLm".
```

This matches the direction taken in dart-lang/native#1425 and flutter/flutter#158214: duplicates are an error, not renamed.

### Actual results

The build succeeds, with no warning:

```
LiteRtLm.framework    <- llamadart's library
LiteRtLm1.framework   <- flutter_edge_ai_litertlm's library, renamed
```

The duplicate check compares file names, and `libLiteRtLm.dylib` and `LiteRtLm` differ. But `frameworkUri` (`packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/isolated/native_assets/macos/native_assets_host.dart`) strips `lib` and `.dylib`, so both become `LiteRtLm`. When names collide, it then appends a counter without telling anyone.

Install names are rewritten, so lookups that go through the asset ID still resolve. But a framework name is a stable path, and a library that opens itself or its companions as `@executable_path/Frameworks/LiteRtLm.framework/LiteRtLm` now silently gets the other package's binary. In our case that is a different, ABI-incompatible build of the same runtime. Which package gets the plain name depends on asset order.

### Suggestion

Validate on the derived framework name on Apple targets, and fail the same way as for duplicate file names. If renaming has to stay, print a warning that names both asset IDs and the framework each one ended up in.

[Google3 Bug]: [web] FragmentShader.getImageSampler throws UnsupportedError on CanvasKit and Skwasm
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an app with `flutter create bug`.
2. Add the shader from the code sample as `shaders/sampler.frag` and register it in `pubspec.yaml` (see code sample).
3. Replace `lib/main.dart` with the code sample.
4. Run it on web with either renderer:
   - CanvasKit: `flutter run -d chrome`
   - Skwasm: `flutter run -d chrome --wasm`
5. Observe the exception thrown from `SamplerPainter.paint`.

### Expected results

`shader.getImageSampler('uTexture')` returns an `ImageSamplerSlot`, and `slot.set(image)` binds the image to the `uTexture` sampler, equivalent to `shader.setImageSampler(0, image)`. The 200x200 square renders the image (left half red, right half blue).

This is how the API behaves on mobile and desktop, where `FragmentShader.getImageSampler` is implemented in [`lib/ui/painting.dart`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/b1a73f83d9cfefcaadca0a93ff71c1c07c3e787c/engine/src/flutter/lib/ui/painting.dart#L6473-L6484) (added in #176749).

### Actual results

On both web renderers, `getImageSampler` throws immediately:

```
Unsupported operation: getImageSampler is not supported on the web.
```

Both web backends stub the method out:

- CanvasKit: [`CkFragmentShader.getImageSampler`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/b1a73f83d9cfefcaadca0a93ff71c1c07c3e787c/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/canvaskit/fragment_shader.dart#L314-L317)
- Skwasm: [`SkwasmFragmentShader.getImageSampler`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/b1a73f83d9cfefcaadca0a93ff71c1c07c3e787c/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/skwasm/skwasm_impl/shaders.dart#L477-L480)

Every other uniform type can already be bound by name on web (`getUniformFloat`, `getUniformVec2`, ..., `getUniformMat4Array`), and `ShaderData.fromBytes` already parses `SampledImage` uniforms. Samplers are the only uniform type that can't be bound by name on web. So cross-platform code that uses the by-name API has to special-case web and fall back to index-based `setImageSampler`.

#### Proposed fix (I have a patch and will send a PR referencing this issue)

1. Add `_getImageSamplerIndex(String name)` to `CkFragmentProgram` and `SkwasmFragmentProgram`, mirroring [`FragmentProgram._getImageSamplerIndex`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/b1a73f83d9cfefcaadca0a93ff71c1c07c3e787c/engine/src/flutter/lib/ui/painting.dart#L5527-L5551). The index is the number of `SampledImage` uniforms declared before `name`. It throws `ArgumentError` if `name` doesn't exist or isn't a sampler.
2. Return an `ImageSamplerSlot` from `CkFragmentShader.getImageSampler` and `SkwasmFragmentShader.getImageSampler` instead of throwing.
3. In `EngineFragmentShader.getImageSampler`, wrap the backend slot so that `set()` goes through `EngineFragmentShader.setImageSampler`. That keeps the `BackendImageShader` it creates attached to the shader finalizer and tracked in `samplerImages`, the same as the index-based path.
4. Add coverage to `lib/web_ui/test/ui/fragment_shader_test.dart

title: Let apps read the max texture size
body:
### Use case

impeller shrinks any decoded image bigger than the max texture size, and the limit is different per device and backend. on a pixel 7 its 32768 with vulkan and 16383 when a debug build forces opengl es. a pixel 5 has 16384.

apps that show big images need this number. in immich we hardcode 16384 on ios and android so long images dont squish (immich-app/immich#29367, immich-app/immich#32213). on a pixel 7 that cuts the resolution by up to half. the only way i found to read the real limit today is decoding a 1x65536 image and checking the height that comes back.

split out from #194060 as asked there.

### Proposal

a getter on PlatformDispatcher:

```dart
int? get maxTextureSize;
```

it returns the limit impeller uses when it decodes images, or null when impeller is not in use or the limit is not known yet. if this sounds ok, i can send a pr.

body:
Three flutter/packages iOS example apps crash at launch when their native tests run on the iOS 27 simulator with Xcode 27, so the `native test` step of `ios_platform_tests` fails for them:

- `google_maps_flutter_ios_sdk9/example` — shard 2: https://ci.chromium.org/b/8668086846834062161
- `google_maps_flutter_ios_sdk10/example` — shard 2: same build
- `webview_flutter_wkwebview/example` — shard 5: https://ci.chromium.org/b/8668086842838050321

(Both are staging.shadow led replays with `sdk_version: 27a266a`; the earlier Xcode 27 runs behind #194019 never reached this step because `xcode analyze deprecation` failed first.)

```
Application failed to launch: UIScene life cycle is required for apps built with this SDK. See "Transitioning to the UIKit scene-based life cycle" in the UIKit documentation for more information on migration.
The test runner crashed before establishing connection: Runner
```

For the two google_maps examples all four `GoogleMapsUITests` fail with `dev.flutter.plugins.googleMobileMapsExample crashed`, then the unit-test host hits the same error. For webview_flutter_wkwebview the UI tests pass but the unit-test `Runner` host fails to launch.

Cause: these are the only iOS example apps in the repo whose `example/ios/Runner/Info.plist` has no `UIApplicationSceneManifest`. iOS 27 requires the scene-based life cycle for apps built against its SDK (same root cause as #187870 on the framework side). The other iOS examples (google_maps_flutter_ios, google_sign_in_ios, in_app_purchase_storekit, camera_avfoundation, image_picker_ios, url_launcher_ios, video_player_avfoundation, …) already have the manifest and launch fine on iOS 27.

Related: #194019, #187870

title: [web] CanvasKit: downscaled images now generate mipmaps (kFast_SrcRectConstraint), blacking out ChromeOS on PowerVR Rogue GPUs
body:
**Summary** Since Flutter 3.47, CanvasKit draws downscaled images with mipmaps. On ChromeOS devices with a PowerVR Rogue GPU, this makes the whole screen, including the system UI, flash black, and the app crashes. It started when #186914 / the Skia roll in #186949 switched CanvasKit's `drawImageRect` to `kFast_SrcRectConstraint`. That change was meant to make downscaled images sharper (#186569). Since then, every image drawn smaller than its size with the default `FilterQuality.medium` gets a GPU-generated mipmapped copy of its texture. For a 3840×1980 background that is about 39 MB extra. On an Asus C202XA (PowerVR Rogue GX6250) and a Lenovo N23 Yoga (also PowerVR GX6250): - Flutter 3.47.5 crashes. - Flutter 3.41.7 runs fine. - Flutter 3.47.5 also runs fine when CanvasKit's `drawImageRectOptions` is patched to pass `MipmapMode.None`. Live repro: https://bvg-gynzy.github.io/flutter_powervr_mipmap_repro/ We would like a supported way to opt out of mipmaps on web. **Steps to reproduce** 1. Open https://bvg-gynzy.github.io/flutter_powervr_mipmap_repro/3.47.5/ (the app first generates six 3840×1980 PNG backgrounds, so it takes a while to load, longer on a slow Chromebook), or build https://github.com/BvG-Gynzy/flutter_powervr_mipmap_repro with Flutter 3.47.5 (`flutter build web`, or `./build.sh` for all variants). 2. Open it in Chrome on a ChromeOS device with a PowerVR Rogue GPU (we used an Asus C202XA, PowerVR Rogue GX6250). 3. Leave it running while it cycles through its 3840×1980 backgrounds. **Expected results** The app keeps rendering, as it does with Flutter 3.41.7. **Actual results** The whole ChromeOS screen, including the system UI, flashes black and the app crashes. - The same app built with 3.41.7 works. - With 3.47.5 it also works when `drawImageRectOptions` is patched to pass `MipmapMode.None` (`?noMipmaps=1`). **Code sample** The full app is https://github.com/BvG-Gynzy/flutter_powervr_mipmap_repro ([`lib/main.dart`](https://github.com/BvG-Gynzy/flutter_powervr_mipmap_repro/blob/main/lib/main.dart), [`web/flutter_bootstrap.js`](https://github.com/BvG-Gynzy/flutter_powervr_mipmap_repro/blob/main/web/flutter_bootstrap.js)). It generates six 3840×1980 PNG backgrounds and shows one full-screen, switching every second. The part that matters: ```dart Image.memory( pngBytes, // 3840×1980 PNG fit: BoxFit.cover, // downscaled to the 1366×768 screen filterQuality: FilterQuality.medium, // the default; becomes MipmapMode.Linear gaplessPlayback: true, ) ```
Workaround used for ?noMipmaps=1 (web/flutter_bootstrap.js) ```js const canvasKit = await window.flutterCanvasKitLoaded; const drawImageRectOptions = canvasKit.Canvas.prototype.drawImageRectOptions; canvasKit.Canvas.prototype.drawImageRectOptions = function (image, src, dst, filterMode, mipmapMode, paint) { return drawImageRectOptions.call(this, image, src, dst, filterMode, canvasKit.MipmapMode.None, paint); }; ```

[Xcode 27] flutter/packages "Swift format" repo check fails (swift-format moves `@preconcurrency @testable import`)
body:
"Swift format" in `Mac_arm64 macos_repo_checks` fails when the bots run Xcode 27.

https://ci.chromium.org/b/8668494649107525137 (staging.shadow run of the Xcode 27 CI experiment, flutter/packages#13158, `sdk_version: 27a266a`)

The step runs `xcrun swift-format -i` over every Swift file and then diffs. With the swift-format bundled in Xcode 27, exactly one file comes out different:

```
diff --git a/packages/video_player/video_player_avfoundation/darwin/RunnerTests/VideoPlayerTests.swift b/packages/video_player/video_player_avfoundation/darwin/RunnerTests/VideoPlayerTests.swift
@@ -4,9 +4,10 @@
 import AVFoundation
 import Testing
-@preconcurrency @testable import video_player_avfoundation
 import video_player_avfoundation_objc

+@preconcurrency @testable import video_player_avfoundation
+
 #if os(iOS)
   import Flutter
 #else
```

The new formatter moves the attributed import (`@preconcurrency @testable import …`) out of the sorted import block into its own group. The current Xcode 26.2 (17c52) formatter leaves it in place, so the file is correctly formatted today and will stop being correctly formatted the moment the bots move to Xcode 27.

Options:
- reorder that one import in `VideoPlayerTests.swift` so both formatter versions accept it (needs checking that Xcode 26.2's swift-format doesn't move it back), or
- land the reformat together with the Xcode 27 roll.

Related: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/194019 (the other Xcode 27 failures in the same experiment runs).

title: [packages] Raise iOS min version for deprecation checks
body:
There's an analyze run in flutter/packages that's meant to avoid introducing new deprecated code (other than within an availability-gated fallback path), and the idea is that it's supposed to be set to a higher min iOS version than our actual minimum, so that dropping old iOS versions doesn't suddenly give a bunch of deprecation warnings, and they can instead be addressed proactively.

Currently, for iOS it's [still set to iOS 14](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/c63648d6ab6c69a141fa71361979eea159a7c452/.ci/targets/ios_platform_tests.yaml#L21), which is now lower than our minimum supported version. I ran into this in https://github.com/flutter/packages/pull/13197 where CI tried to block me from removing deprecated code paths that we no longer need, because it's analyzing for iOS 14 instead of 15. I can bump it to 15 there (if that doesn't cause issues in other packages, TBD), but ideally it should be raised to something relatively recent, and any warnings that show up in that process addressed with new codepaths.

title: [Impeller] Unified Vulkan transient attachment caching in Impeller core
body:
When Impeller renders into a Vulkan render target, it requires 4x MSAA color and depth-stencil transient attachments. On mobile GPUs with lazy memory allocation or Apple Metal memoryless attachments, these buffers reside in on-chip tile memory with no host RAM footprint. On desktop Linux, Wayland/DRM-KMS embedders, and embedded GPUs like Raspberry Pi Broadcom VideoCore (V3D 4.2), lazy allocation is unsupported. Benchmarks from @jwinarske on V3D 4.2 show that allocating these buffers per frame on scanout rings creates ~60 MB of allocation churn per frame (at 1280x1440 with 4x MSAA) and drops framerates from 58.8 fps to 23.5 fps.

An earlier iteration of https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/193003 explored caching these transient textures directly inside `embedder.cc`. While that benchmark proved the necessity of caching on embedded scanout rings, the embedder shell is the wrong architectural home for managing GPU texture lifecycles. Caching at the shell layer duplicates the transients cache already present in `GPUSurfaceVulkanImpeller`, and textures held in shell closures cannot respond to engine memory pressure notifications or cache trimming.

Directionally, we should consolidate transient texture caching into Impeller's core Vulkan backend rather than maintaining separate caches across the shell.

I propose moving transient texture memoization into `impeller::ContextVK`, keyed by `TextureDescriptor`. Cached instances can hold a `std::weak_ptr<DeviceHolderVK>` so they drop cleanly if the context or device is destroyed. Both `embedder.cc` and `GPUSurfaceVulkanImpeller` can then share this single caching mechanism and participate in engine-level memory trimming.

title: [Impeller] Support configurable Vulkan image layout handoff for embedder backing stores
body:
In https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/193003, Impeller returns Vulkan backing stores in `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_GENERAL`. Skia returned them in `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_COLOR_ATTACHMENT_OPTIMAL`.

This difference means that switching from skia vulkan to impeller vulkan will break an embedder which previously used skia with backingstores expecting the layout Skia uses. The form of the breakage would be synchronization and validation failures (`VUID-vkCmdPipelineBarrier-oldLayout-01181`).
Also, `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_GENERAL` can disable hardware framebuffer compression on tile-based mobile GPUs.

The reason that PR uses `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_GENERAL` is because that PR uses a shortcut to create its render target for the backingstore. It calls `SurfaceVK::WrapSwapchainImage` with a dummy present callback. This leads to them being treated as onscreen swapchains, which uses `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_GENERAL`.

We should provide a contract for embedders to request a particular image layout.

I propose adding a `presentation_layout` field to `FlutterVulkanBackingStore` in `embedder.h`. We can keep the default on `VK_IMAGE_LAYOUT_GENERAL`.
We should also extract a dedicated helper for wrapping offscreen render targets to get rid of the `SurfaceVK::WrapSwapchainImage` shortcut.

title: [macOS] flutter_desktop_darwin_unittests: ResponseAfterEngineDied frees the engine inside EmbedderEngine::RunTask, corrupting the heap for later tests
body:
`flutter_desktop_darwin_unittests` corrupts its own heap in some shuffled orders. The process then aborts with `BUG IN CLIENT OF LIBMALLOC: memory corruption of free block` in whichever later test allocates next, usually a `FlutterTextInputPluginTest` case. It reproduces on master in both `host_debug_unopt_arm64` and `host_profile_arm64`.

### Steps to reproduce

On master `b314ad53146`, macOS 26.4 (arm64, Apple M5 Max), Xcode 26.6:

```
cd engine/src
flutter/bin/et build -c host_debug_unopt_arm64 //flutter/shell/platform/darwin/macos:flutter_desktop_darwin_unittests

# Guard Malloc shows the first invalid access deterministically:
env DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES=/usr/lib/libgmalloc.dylib \
    DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=out/host_debug_unopt_arm64 FLUTTER_BUILD_DIRECTORY=out/host_debug_unopt_arm64 \
    out/host_debug_unopt_arm64/flutter_desktop_darwin_unittests \
    --gtest_shuffle --gtest_repeat=2 --gtest_random_seed=64654

# Without Guard Malloc the same seed aborts in iteration 2 in roughly half of the runs:
env DYLD_LIBRARY_PATH=out/host_debug_unopt_arm64 FLUTTER_BUILD_DIRECTORY=out/host_debug_unopt_arm64 \
    out/host_debug_unopt_arm64/flutter_desktop_darwin_unittests \
    --gtest_shuffle --gtest_repeat=2 --gtest_random_seed=64654
```

The same seed aborts in `host_profile_arm64` (through `testing/run_tests.py --variant host_profile_arm64 --type engine --engine-filter flutter_desktop_darwin_unittests`, or the binary directly), in 3 of 8 runs.

### Expected results

The suite passes in any shuffle order.

### Actual results

With Guard Malloc, the run stops at test 99 of iteration 1, `FlutterEngineTest.ResponseAfterEngineDied`, with `EXC_BAD_ACCESS (KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS)`:

```

flutter::EmbedderEngine::RunTask
FlutterEngineRunTask
__block for -[FlutterEngine postMainThreadTask:targetTimeInNanoseconds:]

title: [web] Cover Skwasm font loading from Dart and JavaScript byte views
body:
Skwasm font loading accepts a `Uint8List`, which may be a view into a larger buffer or backed by a JavaScript `Uint8Array`. Focused engine tests should preserve this behavior when the font-data copy path changes.

Proposed coverage:
- A Dart-allocated `Uint8List` and `JSUint8Array.withLength(...).toDart`.
- A font view starting at byte offset 0 and at byte offset 13.

Each case places a valid Ahem font into a larger buffer, takes a `Uint8List.sublistView` of the font bytes, verifies that `SkwasmFontCollection.loadFontFromBytes` succeeds, and checks that the entire source buffer remains unchanged, including sentinel bytes outside the view.

[All four cases](https://github.com/yexuan910812/flutter/blob/96d296c73487975c4e8dbbe7017973e404fc68af/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/test/skwasm/font_data_test.dart) already pass at `b314ad53146b1bde55b60197a35183fb530aac0a` in the `chrome-coi-dart2wasm-skwasm-skwasm` suite. This tracks additional coverage for existing behavior, requires no production change, and makes no performance claim.

title: [web] SkwasmFontCollection.clear retains registered typeface references
body:
`SkwasmFontCollection.clear()` recreates the native font collection but leaves `registeredTypefaces` populated. Loading named fonts appends wrappers to this map, so repeated load/clear cycles retain references from previous collections.

Reproduced at `b314ad53146b1bde55b60197a35183fb530aac0a` with the Chrome dart2wasm/skwasm engine test suite.

### Reproduction

Copy [this standalone engine regression test](https://github.com/yexuan910812/flutter/blob/96821e42481e37ec00a3c2ac21a132259135fa51/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/test/skwasm/font_collection_test.dart) onto that revision, without the implementation change, then run from `engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui`:

```sh
dev/felt test --gcs-prod --offline --suite chrome-coi-dart2wasm-skwasm-skwasm test/skwasm/font_collection_test.dart
```

The test loads Ahem twice under one family, clears the collection, and repeats the cycle. The first clear fails:

```text
Expected: empty
Actual: {'TestFont': [Instance of 'SkwasmTypeface', Instance of 'SkwasmTypeface']}
```

Expected: clearing the collection also removes its registered typeface references. Adding `registeredTypefaces.clear()` makes all three cycles pass.

This is a reference-retention regression test, not a measurement of process memory or GC timing. No public font-unloading API is proposed.

title: [Linux] Wayland subsurface renderer negates its own zero-copy benefit: synced subsurface forces a full-window CPU clear on every frame
body:
### Summary

The new Wayland subsurface view renderer (flutter/flutter#191389, landed 2026-08-24, first shipped in beta 3.49.0-0.2.pre) creates the view's subsurface with `wl_subsurface_set_sync()` hard-coded. In synced mode, every commit of the subsurface requires the parent surface to be committed too, so the embedder calls `gtk_widget_queue_draw()` on the whole `GtkWindow` for every frame. GTK then redraws the parent window — including a full-window CPU clear via pixman — once per Flutter frame.

The result: the "zero-copy" presentation that the subsurface renderer was built for is paid for by an equal amount of per-frame CPU memory traffic (W×H×4 bytes written by pixman each frame). Measured end-to-end CPU usage is essentially identical to the old stable path, whose cost is a full-window CPU readback copy via `gdk_cairo_draw_from_gl()`. Two different mechanisms, same bill.

### Measured impact

Test app: a terminal emulator (continuous PTY output, frame rate capped at 30 fps), same window size/position, same deterministic workload, `perf record` on the UI/platform thread. Linux x64, Wayland session (GTK 3).

| Configuration | Process CPU | Dominant CPU consumer (perf samples) |
|---|---|---|
| beta 3.49.0-0.2.pre, default opaque black window background | **65.3%** | GTK parent-window clear path |
| beta 3.49.0-0.2.pre, transparent window background | **38.3%** | `pixman_fill` ≈ 55% of all samples (~21 CPU points) |
| stable 3.47.5 (GTK3 path), transparent window background | **38.9%** | `memmove` ≈ 37% of samples, call chain through `gdk_cairo_draw_from_gl()` |

Notes:

- On the stable path the cost is a full-window CPU copy of the GL framebuffer contents (`gdk_cairo_draw_from_gl`).
- On the beta subsurface path the GPU presents the frame without a copy, but the *parent* GTK window repaints every frame because the subsurface is synced, and that repaint does a full-window pixman fill on the CPU.
- The two totals match within measurement noise (38.3% vs 38.9%) — both are dominated by a per-frame full-window CPU memory write.
- Removing the pixman fill would bring the beta path down to roughly ~17% CPU for this workload (extrapolation from the sample shares), which is in the same range as a native GPU terminal (Ghostty) running the identical workload at ~18%.

### Root cause (source references)

1. The subsurface is unconditionally created in synced mode — `wl_subsurface_set_sync` with no desync anywhere:
   https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/linux/fl_subsurface.cc#L43
   (unchanged since the initial commit of #191389)

2. Because the subsurface is synced, every new frame requires the parent surface to commit, so the renderer redraw-callback queues a full-widget redraw of the `GtkWindow` every frame:
   https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/774a76734848e38c908681d752e465b2a1595adb/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/linux/fl_view_renderer_subsurface.cc#L133
   (`redraw_cb` → `gtk_widget_queue_draw(GT

title: [go_router] Root-navigator redirect page is omitted when restoring a StatefulShellRoute branch
body:
### What package does this bug report belong to?

go_router

### Summary

When a `StatefulShellRoute` branch redirects to a child route displayed on the root navigator, switching away and restoring the branch with `goBranch()` can omit the redirect page. The cached branch `RouteMatchList` contains the branch matches but still has the URI of the root-navigator child that was removed from those matches.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Configure two branches, `/a` and `/b`, in `StatefulShellRoute.indexedStack`.
2. Redirect `/b` to `/b/welcome`. Configure `welcome` as a child of `/b` with `parentNavigatorKey` set to the root navigator key. The redirect remains required on every entry.
3. Start at `/a`, then select branch B using `navigationShell.goBranch(1)`. The welcome page appears.
4. On the welcome page, cancel by calling `context.go('/a')`.
5. Select branch B again using `navigationShell.goBranch(1)` with the default `initialLocation: false`.

### Expected results

The welcome page appears again because the redirect condition has not changed. The restored branch cache should have a URI and path parameters consistent with its remaining route matches.

### Actual results

On the second entry, the branch page is displayed without the welcome page. The cached list excludes the root-navigator child, but its URI still points to `/b/welcome`. The restore parser can therefore retain the cached list instead of the newly matched redirect destination.

title: [camera] Support separate resolution presets for photo and video capture
body:
### Use case

The `camera` plugin currently uses a single `ResolutionPreset` for both still image capture and video recording. Some applications need high-resolution photos while recording videos at a lower resolution to reduce file size, upload time, memory usage, and encoding load.

### Proposal

Allow photo capture and video recording resolution to be configured independently. For example:

```dart
final controller = CameraController(
  camera,
  ResolutionPreset.high,
  photoResolutionPreset: ResolutionPreset.max,
  videoResolutionPreset: ResolutionPreset.high,
);
```

The existing `resolutionPreset` can remain the default for both modes to preserve backward compatibility. When an optional mode-specific preset is provided, the platform implementation should apply it only to the corresponding capture pipeline:

- `photoResolutionPreset` for `takePicture()`
- `videoResolutionPreset` for `startVideoRecording()`

This would let applications balance still-image detail and video size/performance without rebuilding the controller or interrupting the preview.

title: Add optional `isSelected` toggle state support to `ButtonStyleButton`
body:
### Use case

In Material 3 and Material 3 Expressive (see #168813, #184936, #184937), common buttons (`FilledButton`, `FilledButton.tonal`, `ElevatedButton`, `OutlinedButton`, `TextButton`) and custom `ButtonStyleButton` subclasses support toggleable selected/unselected states (updating `WidgetState.selected` for color/shape resolution and setting `Semantics.selected` for accessibility).

Currently, `ButtonStyleButton` does not expose an `isSelected` parameter. As a result:
1. Even inside Flutter's own Material library (`icon_button.dart`), `_IconButtonM3 extends ButtonStyleButton` has to be wrapped in a separate 100-line `_SelectableIconButton extends StatefulWidget` solely to allocate a `WidgetStatesController`, synchronize `WidgetState.selected` in `initState`/`didUpdateWidget`, and wrap the child in `Semantics(selected: isSelected)`.
2. Every custom `ButtonStyleButton` subclass or toggleable Material button must duplicate that boilerplate `StatefulWidget` wrapper to manage `WidgetStatesController` lifecycle and `Semantics(selected: ...)`.

### Proposal

Add an optional `bool? isSelected` property directly to `ButtonStyleButton`:
- In `_ButtonStyleState.initStatesController()`, if `widget.isSelected != null`, call `statesController.update(WidgetState.selected, widget.isSelected!)`.
- In `_ButtonStyleState.didUpdateWidget()`, if `widget.isSelected != oldWidget.isSelected`, call `statesController.update(WidgetState.selected, widget.isSelected ?? false)`.
- In `_ButtonStyleState.build()`, pass `selected: widget.isSelected` to the outer `Semantics` widget.
- Optionally simplify `_IconButtonM3` in `icon_button.dart` by passing `isSelected` directly to `ButtonStyleButton` and removing `_SelectableIconButton`.

title: [macOS] With semantics enabled, the first composing keystroke into an empty TextField loses its composition and the field stops repainting
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create --platforms=macos repro`, replace `lib/main.dart` with the code sample, and add the Swift snippet to `macos/Runner/MainFlutterWindow.swift`. The snippet's channel posts `NSApplicationDidChangeAccessibilityEnhancedUserInterfaceNotification` with `AXEnhancedUserInterface = YES`. AppKit posts the same notification when another process sets that attribute on the app through `AXUIElementSetAttributeValue`, as assistive apps do. The engine enables semantics when it arrives (`FlutterEngine.mm`, `onAccessibilityStatusChanged:`). Setting the attribute from another process has the same effect on a release build.
2. `flutter run -d macos`, with the ABC keyboard layout.
3. Click the first field and type ⌥E, then `e`, then `x`. It reads `éx`.
4. Click "Enable semantics, as an assistive app does".
5. Click the second field and type ⌥E, then `e`, then `x`.

### Expected results

The second field behaves like the first: ⌥E shows the accent as marked text, `e` turns it into `é`, and the field reads `éx`.

### Actual results

- The second field shows an underlined `´` and stops repainting; even the caret stops blinking. No frame runs until something unrelated schedules one, such as hovering the button or the window resigning key.
- Its controller ends up holding `ex`: the pending accent is discarded, so `é` never forms.
- With an input method that composes with marked text (tested with Sogou Pinyin 6.25.3), typing `ceshi` leaves the field at an underlined `c`. The input method commits `c` on its own and starts a new composition at `e`, so choosing a candidate yields `c` followed by the candidate for `eshi`.
- Typing into the field again, after it has been edited once, works.
- With `FLTEnableMergedPlatformUIThread` set to `false`, the field repaints normally, but the first composition is still lost.

Mechanism, from the logs below and from method swizzling on `FlutterTextInputPlugin` and `FlutterTextField`:

1. The first keystroke arrives as marked text (`setMarkedText:`), and the framework applies composing `0..1`.
2. The next frame's `flushSemantics` sends the field's new value. `Shell::OnEngineUpdateSemantics` uses `RunNowOrPostTask`, so with merged threads `AccessibilityBridgeMac` handles the update synchronously inside the frame. Its `VALUE_CHANGED` branch calls `[FlutterTextField startEditing]`, which calls `selectText:`. `FlutterTextInputPlugin` resigns first responder and becomes the field editor of the `NSTextField` while the composition is still pending, so the composition ends. The ABC dead key is discarded; Sogou Pinyin commits its letter with `insertText:`.
3. The plugin reports the change through `updateEditState`. `Shell::OnPlatformViewDispatchPlatformMessage` uses `RunNowAndFlushMessages`, so the framework's `TextInput` handler runs immediately, still inside the frame (`SchedulerPhase.persistentCallbacks`). `EditableText` applies the value and marks itself dirty. `ensureVisualUpdate` does not schedule a fr

title: [camera_web] availableCameras throws cameraNotReadable when one video device cannot be opened (e.g. OBS Virtual Camera)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Windows 10 with a working webcam and OBS Studio installed (it registers a DirectShow filter `OBS Virtual Camera`). Do not start OBS or its virtual camera. Any other camera that is listed by the browser but cannot be opened behaves the same way.
2. Create an app that depends on `camera: ^0.11.0+2` and run it in Chrome (`flutter run -d chrome`).
3. Call `availableCameras()` and grant the camera permission.

### Expected results

`availableCameras()` returns the cameras that can be used (here: the integrated webcam). A device that cannot be opened is skipped.

### Actual results

`availableCameras()` throws `CameraException(cameraNotReadable, The camera is not readable due to a hardware error that prevented access to the device.)`. No camera is returned, although the integrated webcam works.

### Cause

In `camera_web` `availableCameras()` calls `getUserMedia({video: {deviceId: {exact: id}}})` for every video input device (`_getVideoStreamForDevice`, in the `for (final videoInputDevice in videoInputDevices)` loop). The only `try`/`catch` surrounds the whole method. In Chrome the OBS Virtual Camera device rejects with `NotReadableError: Could not start video source`. This becomes a `CameraWebException` that exits the loop, so one unreadable device hides all the others.

The structure is the same in every version I checked (0.3.1+3, 0.3.1+4, 0.3.2+3, 0.3.3, 0.3.4, 0.3.5, 0.3.5+6).

A page with plain `navigator.mediaDevices.getUserMedia` confirms it, without Flutter:

- `getUserMedia({video: true})` succeeds (`Integrated Webcam`);
- `getUserMedia({video: {deviceId: {exact: <integrated webcam id>}}})` succeeds;
- `getUserMedia({video: {deviceId: {exact: <OBS Virtual Camera id>}}})` fails with `NotReadableError: Could not start video source`.

### Suggested fix

Handle a failure per device inside the loop and continue with the next device; throw only when no device could be opened (or return an empty list).

### Environment

- `camera_web` 0.3.5+6 via `camera` 0.11.x, Flutter 3.44.9 (stable), Windows 10, Chrome 154.0.8037.98.

title: [Flutter GPU] A render target with two color attachments aborts the process on OpenGL ES
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. On the OpenGL ES backend, create a `RenderTarget` with two color attachments.
2. Bind a pipeline whose fragment shader writes `layout(location = 0)` and `layout(location = 1)`, and draw.
3. Submit the command buffer.

`RenderPassGLES` asks the pipeline for its one legacy-compatible color attachment (`impeller/renderer/backend/gles/render_pass_gles.cc`):

```cpp
const auto* color_attachment =
    pipeline.GetDescriptor().GetLegacyCompatibleColorAttachment();
if (!color_attachment) {
  VALIDATION_LOG
      << "Color attachment is too complicated for a legacy renderer.";
  return false;
}
```

`PipelineDescriptor::GetLegacyCompatibleColorAttachment()` returns null for anything but exactly one color attachment, so this backend renders into one color attachment only. The `false` goes back to the reactor callback, which checks it:

```cpp
FML_CHECK(result)
    << "Must be able to encode GL commands without error.";
```

### Expected results

Either the draw renders into both attachments, or Flutter GPU tells the app beforehand that this backend takes one color attachment: a capability on `GpuContext` it can check, next to `doesSupportOffscreenMSAA` and `doesSupportFramebufferRenderMipmap`, and a Dart exception from `createRenderPass` or `bindPipeline` that names the limit.

### Actual results

The process aborts with SIGABRT (exit code 134). No Dart exception is thrown and nothing in the Dart API mentions the limit beforehand. The abort comes from `FML_CHECK`, which stays in release builds too, so I'd expect a release app to crash the same way. I ran it only on a debug engine, though.

<details open><summary>Program output (flutter_tester_opengles, debug engine, the whole log)</summary>

```console
[ERROR:flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/gles/render_pass_gles.cc(607)] Break on 'ImpellerValidationBreak' to inspect point of failure: Color attachment is too complicated for a legacy renderer.
[FATAL:flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/gles/render_pass_gles.cc(1010)] Check failed: result. Must be able to encode GL commands without error.
```

</details>

### Suggested fix

Expose the limit as a capability (a `maxColorAttachments`, or a boolean like the existing `doesSupport…` getters) that reports 1 on the GLES backend. Then Flutter GPU can refuse a render target with more color attachments when the render pass is created, with a message that names the limit, before anything reaches the reactor. Lifting the limit on GLES 3 contexts with `glDrawBuffers` would be a separate change.

I hit this while testing #194154, where a pipeline gave every color attachment the format of attachment 0. Its Dart test skips OpenGL ES for this reason.

I ran it as a test in `testing/dart/gpu_test.dart`, built the same way as the existing "Can render into color attachments with different formats" test there, which skips OpenGL ES: two 100x100 RGBA8 textures with render target usage as the two color attachments of one `RenderTarget`, a

title: [Flutter GPU] GpuContext.defaultColorFormat returns PixelFormat.unknown with wide gamut on Metal
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an iOS app with `flutter_gpu` as a dependency, and set both `FLTEnableFlutterGPU` and `FLTEnableWideGamut` to `true` in `ios/Runner/Info.plist`.
2. Paste the code sample below into `lib/main.dart`.
3. `flutter run --profile` on a device with a P3 display (I used an iPad on iOS 27.2).

The sample reads `gpuContext.defaultColorFormat` and creates a texture with it before the first frame, right after it, and again one and three seconds later.

### Expected results

`defaultColorFormat` is a format Flutter GPU can create textures in, for the whole life of the app, and `createTexture` with it succeeds every time.

### Actual results

It is `b8g8r8a8UNormInt` before and right after the first frame, then `PixelFormat.unknown` from about a second in, and `createTexture` with it fails from then on. The layer is `MTLPixelFormatBGRA10_XR` throughout.

Why: on Metal the default color format changes at runtime. `IOSSurfaceMetalImpeller::CreateGPUSurface` calls `ContextMTL::UpdateOffscreenLayerPixelFormat` with `layer_.pixelFormat`, which recomputes the capabilities with that format as the default color format. With wide gamut it is `kB10G10R10A10XR` (or `kB10G10R10XR`), and `FromImpellerPixelFormat` in `lib/gpu/formats.h` maps the extended-range formats to `kUnknown`:

```cpp
case impeller::PixelFormat::kB10G10R10XR:
case impeller::PixelFormat::kB10G10R10XRSRGB:
case impeller::PixelFormat::kB10G10R10A10XR:
  // Apple-only extended-range formats, not exposed by the Flutter GPU API.
  return FlutterGPUPixelFormat::kUnknown;
```

`GpuContext.createImageSurface` without an explicit format uses `defaultColorFormat` too, so it fails the same way. The embedder calls `UpdateOffscreenLayerPixelFormat` when it wraps a Metal backing store, so the same can happen there.

body:
### Steps to reproduce

Pass any of these to `RenderPass` (code sample below):

1. An attachment texture created with `enableRenderTargetUsage: false`.
2. Color and depth-stencil attachments with different sample counts.
3. A color format (for example `r8g8b8a8UNormInt`) as the `DepthStencilAttachment` texture, or a depth-stencil format as a color attachment.
4. `mipLevel > 0` on a backend where `GpuContext.doesSupportFramebufferRenderMipmap` is false (OpenGL ES).
5. `bindVertexBuffer` / `bindIndexBuffer` with a `BufferView` that ends past its buffer, or has a negative offset. (`bindUniform` already rejects this natively.)

8. `setScissor` with a rectangle larger than the render target.
9. A `RenderTarget` with no attachments at all.

`RenderTarget._validateAttachments` (`lib/gpu/lib/src/render_pass.dart`) checks mip levels, slices and attachment sizes, and `ColorAttachment._validate` checks MSAA resolve setups, but nothing checks the cases above. On the engine side their checks are missing or only debug validation logs.

### Expected results

Each call throws in Dart with a message that names the problem, in debug and release builds alike.

### Actual results

Dart doesn't throw, and in a release build these are undefined behavior. [Flutter GPU] RenderPass.draw() before bindPipeline() crashes the process
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a render pass on any render target.
2. Bind a vertex buffer, but don't call `bindPipeline()`.
3. Call `draw()` or `drawIndexed()`.

`flutter::gpu::RenderPass::Draw` (`lib/gpu/render_pass.cc`) builds the pipeline through `GetOrCreatePipeline`, which calls

```cpp
if (!render_pipeline_->BindToPipelineDescriptor(*context.GetShaderLibrary(),
                                                pipeline_desc)) {
```

Only `bindPipeline` sets `render_pipeline_`, and neither the Dart nor the native side checks that it was called.

### Expected results

A Dart exception that says the pass has no pipeline bound. It's an easy mistake while learning the API, or when a pipeline is created asynchronously and the first draw runs before it is ready.

### Actual results

The process dies on a null `fml::RefPtr<RenderPipeline>`. A debug engine stops on the check below and gets SIGABRT; without that debug check it is a null pointer dereference, and the C++ unit test I wrote for it gets SIGSEGV. I reproduced it with `flutter_tester` on Metal and Vulkan (SwiftShader) and with `flutter_tester_opengles`; I haven't run a release engine.

<details open><summary>Program output (flutter_tester, debug engine)</summary>

```console
[FATAL:flutter/fml/memory/ref_ptr.h(125)] Check failed: ptr_.
```

</details>

### Suggested fix

In native code, `RenderPass::Draw` returns false when no pipeline is bound, before it touches the context or the pipeline; the Dart side already turns a false into an exception. In Dart, `RenderPass` remembers whether `bindPipeline` was called, and `draw` / `drawIndexed` throw a `StateError` that says what is missing.

Related: #186768 is about passing native error detail back to Dart; this check stops the draw before it reaches native code at all. #193867 (pass lifecycle) may touch the same files. #192396 is about bindings that survive a pipeline change; this issue is only about drawing with no pipeline bound.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>The relevant part</summary>

```dart
final gpu.CommandBuffer commandBuffer = gpu.gpuContext.createCommandBuffer();
final gpu.RenderPass renderPass = commandBuffer.createRenderPass(
  gpu.RenderTarget.singleColor(gpu.ColorAttachment(texture: colorTexture)),
);
renderPass.bindVertexBuffer(vertices);
renderPass.draw(3); // no bindPipeline() before this
```

</details>

### Flutter Doctor output

Found in an engine built from source: macOS arm64, `host_debug_unopt_arm64`. On current main `RenderPass::Draw` has moved (#190400), but the unchecked `render_pipeline_->BindToPipelineDescriptor(...)` is still there.

<details open><summary>Doctor output</summary>

```console
[✓] Flutter (Channel stable, 3.47.0, on macOS 27.2 26B5091g darwin-arm64)
    • Framework revision 4cf2416426, 2026-08-11
    • Engine revision 5f77625673
    • Dart version 3.13.0
[!] Xcode - develop for iOS and macOS (Xcode 27.0)
```

title: [Flutter GPU] DeviceBuffer.flush() with default arguments flushes a range of SIZE_MAX bytes
body:
### Steps to reproduce

`DeviceBuffer.flush` (`lib/gpu/lib/src/buffer.dart`) documents that a `lengthInBytes` of -1, the default, flushes the entire buffer:

```dart
void flush({int offsetInBytes = 0, int lengthInBytes = -1}) {
  ...
  _flush(offsetInBytes, lengthInBytes);
}
```

The native side (`lib/gpu/device_buffer.cc`) passes the value straight into an `impeller::Range`, whose fields are `size_t`:

```cpp
bool InternalFlutterGpu_DeviceBuffer_Flush(
    flutter::gpu::DeviceBuffer* device_buffer,
    int offset_in_bytes,
    int size_in_bytes) {
  device_buffer->GetBuffer()->Flush(
      impeller::Range(offset_in_bytes, size_in_bytes));
  return true;
}
```

1. Create a host-visible `DeviceBuffer`, write vertices into it with `overwrite`, and call `flush()` with no arguments.
2. Bind it as a vertex buffer and draw a triangle with any unlit pipeline.
3. Run with Impeller on OpenGL ES.

### Expected results

The whole buffer is flushed and the triangle is drawn, on every backend.

### Actual results

`flush()` becomes `Flush(Range{0, SIZE_MAX})`, and each backend does something different with it:

- On OpenGL ES, `DeviceBufferGLES::Flush` stores `{offset, SIZE_MAX}` as the dirty range, and the next bind calls `glBufferSubData(target, offset, SIZE_MAX, ...)`. `SIZE_MAX` as a `GLsizeiptr` is -1, so GL returns `GL_INVALID_VALUE` and uploads nothing. A debug engine aborts on the GL error check.
- On Metal (macOS, managed storage), `didModifyRange:` gets `NSMakeRange(offset, SIZE_MAX)`, a range that runs past the end of the buffer.
- On Vulkan, `vmaFlushAllocation(..., offset, SIZE_MAX)` happens to work, because `SIZE_MAX` equals `VK_WHOLE_SIZE`.

I reproduced the abort with `flutter_tester_opengles` on macOS; Metal and Vulkan (SwiftShader) draw the triangle. Android runs the same `DeviceBufferGLES` path, but I haven't run it on a device, and I haven't run a release engine, where the upload would be skipped without the abort.

<details open><summary>Program output (flutter_tester_opengles, debug engine)</summary>

```console
[FATAL:flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/gles/proc_table_gles.h(44)]
Fatal GL Error GL_INVALID_VALUE(1281) encountered on call to glBufferSubData
```

</details>

### Suggested fix

Normalize -1 in one place. On the native side, treat a negative length as "to the end of the buffer", and reject offsets and lengths outside the buffer (with the same offset bound as the Dart checks) instead of building an oversized `Range`. That also covers callers that reach the native entry point without going through the Dart checks. The native call already returns a bool, but Dart declares it as returning void, so a refusal is lost; it should be `Bool`, and `flush` should throw on false, as `overwrite` does.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>The relevant part</summary>

```dart
final ByteData vertices = Float32List.fromList(
    <double>[-0.5, 0.5, 0.0, -0.5, 0.5, 0.5]).buffer.asByteData();
final gpu.DeviceBuffer buffer = gpu.gpuContext.cr

[Impeller] GLES: copying a wrapped texture to a buffer reads the default framebuffer
body:
### Steps to reproduce

`ConfigureFBO` in `engine/src/flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/gles/blit_command_gles.cc` decides how a texture is bound for a blit:

```cpp
if (TextureGLES::Cast(*texture).IsWrapped()) {
  // The texture is attached to the default FBO, so there's no need to
  // create/configure one.
  gl.BindFramebuffer(fbo_type, 0);
  return 0;
}
```

`IsWrapped()` is true for two different kinds of texture. `TextureGLES::WrapFBO` wraps a framebuffer: the onscreen surface, where binding framebuffer 0 is what the comment describes, or a caller's own FBO, where it binds the wrong one. `TextureGLES::WrapTexture` wraps an existing GL texture name, as `ImpellerTextureCreateWithOpenGLTextureHandleNew` in the interop toolkit does; such a texture has no framebuffer at all, and `GetFBO()` returns `std::nullopt`. The blit binds framebuffer 0 for both.

This can't be reproduced from Dart today: Flutter GPU doesn't take a GL texture it didn't create, so a wrapped texture name never reaches it. On main the path is open through the interop toolkit (`ImpellerTextureCreateWithOpenGLTextureHandleNew`) and skwasm (`images_impeller.cc`), and from Dart it opens with texture import (#194142), which is where I ran into it. So the repro is at the HAL level:

1. Wrap a GL texture name with known contents with `TextureGLES::WrapTexture` (same share group).
2. Encode a texture-to-buffer copy from it into a host-visible buffer and submit.
3. Read the buffer.

The code sample below does this at the HAL level. With the mock GL proc table in `impeller_unittests` the same thing shows as `glBindFramebuffer(GL_FRAMEBUFFER, 0)` followed by `glReadPixels`, with no `glFramebufferTexture2D` for the texture name.

### Expected results

The buffer holds the wrapped texture's pixels: the texture name is attached to a temporary framebuffer and read from there, as for any texture the engine made. A wrapped framebuffer other than 0 is read from that framebuffer.

### Actual results

The buffer holds the pixels of whatever is bound as framebuffer 0, and the copy reports success, with no error or validation message. A texture-to-texture blit with a wrapped texture name as source or destination reads or writes framebuffer 0 the same way. `RenderPassGLES` has the same confusion: with a wrapped texture name as its color attachment it binds no framebuffer, turns off the y flip and draws into whatever is bound.

### Suggested fix

Tell the two apart with a `TextureGLES::IsWrappedFBO()`. A wrapped framebuffer binds the FBO it wraps, and the caller's FBO is never deleted; a wrapped texture name is read through a temporary FBO.

I'd keep it read-only. Uploads and `SetContents` already refuse wrapped textures, so a blit into a wrapped texture name, or a render pass that uses one as its color attachment, should be refused too, with a validation error, instead of writing into the wrong framebuffer. Writing into textures the caller owns is what #192059 is about, and this issue doesn't try to
[truncated]

title: [Flutter GPU] FlutterGpuCommandBufferTest aborts in debug builds: CommandBuffer is created on the stack
body:
## Problem

The three tests in `lib/gpu/command_buffer_unittests.cc` (`FlutterGpuCommandBufferTest.*`) abort in an unoptimized debug build:

```
[ RUN      ] FlutterGpuCommandBufferTest.RejectsCompletionCallbacksAfterSubmit
[FATAL:flutter/fml/memory/ref_counted_internal.h(97)] Check failed: !adoption_required_.
[ERROR:flutter/fml/backtrace.cc(108)] Caught signal SIGABRT during program execution.
...
Frame 4: fml::internal::RefCountedThreadSafeBase::~RefCountedThreadSafeBase()
```

Each test builds the `flutter::gpu::CommandBuffer` on the stack:

```cpp
CommandBuffer command_buffer(context, impeller_command_buffer);
```

`CommandBuffer` is ref-counted, and an fml ref-counted object has to be adopted (created through `fml::MakeRefCounted`) before it is destroyed. A stack instance is never adopted, so its destructor trips the debug check. The check is debug-only, which I assume is why CI doesn't see it.

## Steps to reproduce

macOS arm64, an existing `host_debug_unopt_arm64` build. The test file is the same on current `main`.

```
cd engine/src
ninja -C out/host_debug_unopt_arm64 flutter/lib/gpu:gpu_unittests
out/host_debug_unopt_arm64/gpu_unittests --gtest_filter='FlutterGpuCommandBufferTest.*'
```

All three tests abort as above. The other `gpu_unittests` suites pass.

## Proposed fix

Create the command buffer with `fml::MakeRefCounted<CommandBuffer>(...)` in the three tests and use it through the returned `fml::RefPtr`. No engine code changes.

I ran into this while testing a few Flutter GPU fixes locally; until it's fixed I leave `FlutterGpuCommandBufferTest.*` out of the `gpu_unittests` filter in those PRs.

title: [native assets] Respect app deployment targets on iOS and macOS
body:
## Use case

Native code assets may need a newer Apple deployment target than Flutter's baseline. The consuming app can already set `IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET` or `MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET`, but those values do not reach the corresponding native asset hook configuration.

Flutter currently supplies [iOS 15](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/71e4717a61786faab4c7aa39825989305ed29e8a/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/isolated/native_assets/ios/native_assets.dart#L14) and [macOS 13](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/71e4717a61786faab4c7aa39825989305ed29e8a/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/isolated/native_assets/macos/native_assets.dart#L14) through [`IOSCodeConfig` and `MacOSCodeConfig`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/71e4717a61786faab4c7aa39825989305ed29e8a/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/isolated/native_assets/targets.dart#L312). In `code_assets` 2.1.0 both target-version fields are integers, so targets such as iOS 16.4 or macOS 13.3 cannot be represented accurately.

There is also a reproduced iOS packaging mismatch. With an app targeting 16.4 and a hook-provided binary requiring 16.4, Flutter generates a native framework plist declaring 15.0:

| Artifact | Minimum OS version |
| --- | --- |
| Runner.app/Info.plist | 16.4 |
| Native binary LC_BUILD_VERSION / minos | 16.4 |
| Generated native framework Info.plist | **15.0** |

This was reproduced in successful unsigned release builds on stable 3.47.6 (`5fc346839b`) and master 3.49.0-0.2.pre (`a381eea6b1`) using a small C function, without a third-party native runtime or model download. The same reduced sample's device and simulator framework plists become 16.4 with an iOS packaging patch. This evidence does not establish an App Store rejection or a runtime failure.

A workaround in llamadart is a separate Flutter companion package linking an XCFramework through SwiftPM. Hook packages cannot set the generated framework's plist themselves. The hook in this use case downloads prebuilt libraries, so fixing iOS packaging can help independently of changing the compiler hook input.

macOS's fixed hook configuration is confirmed in source, but an equivalent packaging or runtime failure has **not** been reproduced. macOS has a different framework layout, and its app uses `LSMinimumSystemVersion` rather than the iOS `MinimumOSVersion` path.

## Proposal

- Pass the consuming app's iOS/macOS deployment target into native asset configuration, preserving major, minor, and patch versions. Full hook-version support will need coordination with `dart-lang/native`.
- Keep iOS framework metadata consistent with the app deployment target rather than a fixed baseline. Preserve Flutter's supported floor and a documented fallback when no app target is available.
- Take settings from the app build context; dependency packages should not need their own `ios/` or `macos/` directories.
- Invalidate affected cached output when the deployment target changes, and test defaults, malformed/unsupported values, iOS

title: [Flutter GPU] Read textures created by another graphics API without a copy
body:
## Problem

Flutter GPU can only use textures it created itself (`GpuContext.createTexture`) or took from a `ui.Image` (`Texture.fromImage`, PR #188605 for issue #188246). An image that another GPU API in the same process produced can't be used at all.

Where this comes up:

- Compute or simulation in another library. wgpu-native running in the same process writes its results into a texture, and the only way to get them into Flutter GPU today is a CPU readback followed by `Texture.overwrite`.
- Video and camera frames that arrive as IOSurfaces, `AHardwareBuffer`s or GL textures.
- Engines and runtimes that hand out images they own.

Impeller already wraps external images internally: `TextureMTL::Wrapper`/`WrapTextureMTL` for embedder backing stores, `TextureGLES::WrapTexture`, `AHBTextureSourceVK`, and `WrapTextureSourceVK` from the #187525 series (PR #193001). Flutter GPU can't reach any of them.

## Scope

This proposal covers **reading** external images: sampling them, using them as storage textures in compute, and copying to and from them in blit passes. An imported texture can't be a render pass attachment.

**Rendering into externally owned targets (OpenXR swapchain images, embedder surfaces) is #192059**, where @adrian-moisa has a working `GpuExternalSurface` prototype. That work needs a frame acquire/present protocol and probably scheduling changes, as discussed there, and I'm keeping this proposal out of it. If it's useful, the import primitive here could sit under that surface: a surface frame would be an imported image plus the acquire/present rules.

## Proposal

### Impeller

One entry point on `impeller::Context` that doesn't depend on the backend:

```cpp
struct ExternalTextureDescriptor {
  ExternalTextureType type;      // kMTLTexture, kIOSurface, kVkImage,
                                 // kAHardwareBuffer, kGLTexture, kEGLImage
  void* handle;                  // borrowed for the call
  uint64_t param;                // IOSurface plane, VkImageLayout, GL target
  TextureDescriptor desc;        // what the caller says it is
  std::function<void()> release_proc;  // after Impeller's last reference
};

absl::StatusOr<std::shared_ptr<Texture>> Context::ImportTexture(
    ExternalTextureDescriptor external);   // non-virtual: null handle, desc.Validate()
virtual absl::StatusOr<std::shared_ptr<Texture>> OnImportTexture(...);
                                           // ContextMTL, ContextVK, ContextGLES
```

`SurfaceContextVK` forwards to its parent. A type the backend doesn't handle fails with `kFailedPrecondition`.

### What each backend checks

The caller describes the texture the same way as for `createTexture`: format, size, sample count, mip count, storage mode and usage. The backend checks that description against the native object wherever the object can be queried. Usages are requirements, not hints.

- **Metal, `id<MTLTexture>`.** The handle has to conform to `MTLTexture` and belong to the context's device. Type, pixel f

title: [Android] A display density change leaves devicePixelRatio stale because onConfigurationChanged does not resend viewport metrics
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Split out of #193770, where this was asked for as a separate issue. That one is about platform views being drawn at a stale ratio; this one is about the frame itself.

It also reproduces #142905, open since 2024-02 and confirmed by triage on Android 12 only, where changing Display Size in Settings is not reflected in the app and the next change shows the previous one's value. No mechanism was ever posted there. I believe it is this defect, and the evidence is below.

`flutter create density_probe`, replace `lib/main.dart` with the sample below, and `flutter run` on an emulator whose physical density is 420 dpi. I used a Pixel 7 AVD, 1080x2400 at 420 dpi, arm64-v8a, at API 31, 34 and 36.

All of this is emulator work — I have no Android handset to hand. #142905's reporter saw the symptom on two physical Android 12 devices.

**The permanent case — Android 12 only.** This is #142905's own sequence, with `wm density` standing in for the Settings slider.

1. Press Home, so the app is in the background.
2. `adb shell wm density 520`
3. Return to the app.
4. Watch the log, and the two numbers on screen. They disagree and stay that way.
5. Repeat with `adb shell wm density reset`. The app now shows the ratio from step 2, one change behind, and stays there.

**The transient case — every version I tried.** With the app in the foreground, `adb shell wm density 520`, then `adb shell wm density reset`. The two numbers disagree for a few frames each time and then agree again.

The sample runs a repeating animation so that frames keep being produced and the log is a continuous record. An ordinary app still draws here — a metrics change schedules a frame — but it would draw fewer, and a transient state is easier to miss.

### Expected results

The sample prints two numbers: `ui.FlutterView.devicePixelRatio`, the ratio the frame is built with and the one `MediaQuery` reports, and `ui.Display.devicePixelRatio`. `dart:ui` documents them as one number, from both sides. On master `c2362b30d1`, in `engine/src/flutter/lib/ui/window.dart`:

- `FlutterView.devicePixelRatio`, line 141 — "The value here is equal to the value exposed on `[display]`."
- `Display.devicePixelRatio`, line 26 — "This value is the same as the value of `[FlutterView.devicePixelRatio]` for all view objects attached to this display."

Neither doc describes a window in which the two can differ. After a display density change the first frame Flutter draws should be built with the new ratio.

### Actual results

#### On Android 12 the ratio never catches up

After the backgrounded change, `ui.Display` reads 3.25 and the frame is still built at 2.625 — and stays there. [gen_l10n] Make generated localization code more extensible and configurable
body:
### Use case

Flutter's built-in localization tool (`gen_l10n`) generates Dart classes and message accessors from ARB files and `l10n.yaml`. In large applications, modular architectures (e.g. monorepos or multi-package feature modules), or codebases with existing localization infrastructure, teams frequently run into architectural constraints with the current generator:

1. **Tight coupling to `package:intl`**: Generated code hardcodes `import 'package:intl/intl.dart' as intl;` and direct references to `intl.NumberFormat`, `intl.DateFormat`, and `intl.Intl.pluralLogic`/`selectLogic`. Applications wrapping `intl` with custom formatting policies, caching, telemetry, or custom localization pipelines cannot use `gen_l10n` without post-generation script workarounds.
2. **Inability to attach mixins to generated classes**: When domain-specific helper logic, interfaces, or mixins need to be shared across all generated locale classes (or attached to specific locale subclasses), developers currently have no way to instruct `gen_l10n` to apply mixins.
3. **Strict runtime failure on unsupported locales**: When an application encounters a runtime `Locale` not explicitly covered by the generated resources, `gen_l10n` unconditionally throws `FlutterError` in `lookupAppLocalizations(Locale locale)` unless callers wrap and catch errors manually. A declarative fallback locale mechanism would allow graceful degradation.
4. **No exclusion mechanism for draft or internal ARB keys**: When working with external translation vendors or draft resources, developers need a way to ignore specific ARB keys during code generation without manually stripping them from version-controlled ARB files.
5. **Single-directory ARB limitation**: In modular applications where different features define their own localized resources, ARBs cannot currently be merged from multiple directories across modules into a unified localization interface without custom build pre-processing.

None of these capabilities can be addressed purely as standalone pub.dev packages because they pertain to Flutter's native localization code generator in `flutter_tools`.

### Proposal

We propose extending `gen_l10n` with declarative configuration options in `l10n.yaml`, while remaining **100% backward-compatible** and **strictly opt-in**.

The proposed capabilities under consideration:

#### 1. Configurable Localization Runtime (`localization-runtime`)
Allow declaratively configuring the imported package URI, import alias, and underlying runtime symbols, preserving `package:intl/intl.dart` and `intl` by default:
```yaml
localization-runtime:
  package: package:core/core.dart
  alias: coreTr # Optional, can be empty for unaliased imports
  symbols:
    canonicalized-locale: CustomLocale.canonicalize
    plural-logic: CustomPlural.choose
    select-logic: CustomSelect.choose
    date-format: CustomDateFormatter
    number-format: CustomNumberFormatter
```
- Completely decouples the generator from hardcoded `intl` s

body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create view_repro && cd view_repro`
2. Replace `lib/main.dart` with the code sample below.
3. `flutter build web --release`, serve `build/web` locally, and open it in:
   - Firefox: bug. (Firefox has `ImageDecoder`, but the engine only uses it on Blink, see `_isBrowserImageDecoderStable` in `safe_browser_api.dart`, so Firefox takes the fallback path.)
   - Safari: same fallback path, expected bug (not tested directly).
   - Chrome: works (the control; Blink uses `ImageDecoder`).

The app decodes the same valid 2x2 red PNG twice: once from a `Uint8List.sublistView` at offset 8 inside a larger buffer (like an image embedded in a .glb's BIN chunk), and once from a copy of those bytes.

### Expected results

Both decodes succeed in every browser: `OK 2x2, first pixel RGBA [255, 0, 0, 255]`, and both `Image.memory` widgets show the red 2x2 image. A `Uint8List` view is a normal `Uint8List`; its `offsetInBytes`/`lengthInBytes` should be honoured.

### Actual results

On every browser that takes the non-`ImageDecoder` fallback, decoding the **view** fails and decoding the **copy** works. Chrome is fine.

**Flutter master** 3.49.0-0.2.pre (framework 78052b8c6c, 2026-10-09), `flutter build web --release`:
- **Firefox 157**: `view (offset 8): FAILED InvalidStateError: The image could not be decoded`; `Image.memory(view)` shows `error: InvalidStateError: The image could not be decoded`; `copy: OK 2x2, first pixel RGBA [255, 0, 0, 255]`.
- **Chrome 154**: view and copy both `OK 2x2, first pixel RGBA [255, 0, 0, 255]`.
- `--wasm`: Chrome 154 (skwasm) OK; Firefox 157 fell back to CanvasKit/JS and fails the same way.

**Flutter stable 3.47.5** (framework 6a19cca564): same result, with the older message `ImageCodecException: Failed to load image: blob:http://localhost:…` in Firefox 157 and 156.

Real-world impact: textures embedded in `.glb` files are decoded from `Uint8List.sublistView(glbBin, …)`. In Firefox every one of them failed (27 decode errors in one level), and the 3D library fell back to a white placeholder.

### Root cause

When `browserSupportsImageDecoder` is false (every non-Blink browser, because of `_isBrowserImageDecoderStable => browserEngine == blink` in `safe_browser_api.dart`), the engine builds the `Blob` from `list.buffer`, the whole backing `ByteBuffer`, and ignores the view's `offsetInBytes`/`lengthInBytes`. The format sniff reads the view correctly, so the PNG is detected, but the browser then decodes a blob that starts with the 8 junk bytes, and the decode fails.

**master**, `engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/image_decoder.dart`, line 343 (the fallback decoder shared by the renderers):

```dart

      final DomBlob blob = createDomBlob(<ByteBuffer>[list.buffer]);
      final DomImageBitmap originalBitmap = await createImageBitmap(blob);
```

title: Proposal:Let apps read which Impeller backend the engine is using
body:
### Use case

On Android the engine picks Vulkan or OpenGL ES at startup, and some devices try Vulkan and end up on OpenGL ES. An app has no API to read which one it got. The engine prints it in a log line, and the impellerEnabled service extension only says on or off, in debug and profile builds.

That matters for bug reports, and it can change between releases: in #179268 an app went from Vulkan in 3.27 to OpenGL ES in 3.38.3 ("we became more aggressive falling back to OpenGL ES because of Vulkan driver stability").

We hit this in immich with long images. On a Pixel 7 the engine shrinks them to 32768 with Vulkan and 16383 when a debug build forces OpenGL ES. We had to check logcat on each phone to know which. An app can already read the limit itself by decoding a 1x65536 image.

### Proposal

A getter on PlatformDispatcher:

```dart
enum ImpellerBackend { metal, opengles, vulkan }

// on PlatformDispatcher
ImpellerBackend? get impellerBackend;
```

It returns the backend in use after any fallback, or null when Impeller is not in use (Skia, web). It doesn't wait for the engine to choose, so it can be null early in startup. After the first frame has been rasterized it no longer changes.

If you'd rather not expose the backend name, a max texture size getter would at least save apps the 1x65536 decode.

I have a patch with tests ready if this sounds ok.

title: [web] Focus traversal from _ViewState.didChangeViewFocus reads the FocusScopeNode of a route popped in the same frame (semantics enabled): "Cannot get renderObject of inactive element"
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. `flutter create --platforms web bug` and replace `lib/main.dart` with the code sample below (no packages beyond the SDK).
2. `flutter build web --release`, serve `build/web` (e.g. `python3 -m http.server --directory build/web 8765`) and open it in Chrome. (`flutter run -d chrome` shows the debug assertion instead.)
3. Enable the semantics tree the way a screen reader does: run `document.querySelector('flt-semantics-placeholder').click()` in DevTools, or Tab to the "Enable accessibility" placeholder and activate it.
4. Click **Open form**.
5. Click **Save**. The button's child becomes a `CircularProgressIndicator`; ~300 ms later the app pops back to **List**.

Each of these is required (verified in isolation): the semantics tree is on; the popped route has a zero-duration transition; the app uses `MaterialApp.router` (`MaterialApp(home:)` hides it, see below); the page is wrapped in `Semantics(scopesRoute: true, explicitChildNodes: true)`, as `MaterialPageRoute.buildPage` does; the button is disabled while loading (`onPressed: null`). Typing in the `TextField` is not needed.

### Expected results

No exception. The form pops and the list is shown.

### Actual results

Every time, one error is reported through `FlutterError.onError` while dispatching `WidgetsBindingObserver.didChangeViewFocus`:
- release: `Null check operator used on a null value`, from `RenderObject.getTransformTo` (`rendering/object.dart:3687`, the `owner!`);
- debug: `Cannot get renderObject of inactive element. … The findRenderObject() method was called for the following element: _FocusScopeWithExternalFocusNode`.

The app keeps working; the error is caught in `WidgetsBinding.handleViewFocusChanged`.

#### Mechanism (Flutter 3.44.0 sources)

1. Clicking **Save** gives DOM focus to the button's `<flt-semantics role="button">`. When its child becomes a spinner, the spinner's `SemanticsRole.loadingSpinner` is merged into the button's node (`semantics/semantics.dart:6808`), so the engine role changes button → loadingSpinner. `SemanticsObject._updateRole()` (engine `semantics/semantics.dart:2314-2358`) creates a new DOM element and removes the old one without moving focus → `focusout` with `relatedTarget: null`, `activeElement: <body>` → `ViewFocusBinding` emits `ViewFocusEvent(unfocused)`. (A button that stays enabled is re-focused by the engine because the merged node is still `isFocused`, which hides the bug — hence `onPressed: null` while loading, the common pattern.)
2. The pop with `transitionDuration: Duration.zero` completes synchronously; the popped `OverlayEntry` is removed in a post-frame callback, so in the next frame the list route comes back onstage and the form route's elements are deactivated in the same build.
3. In that frame, `flushSemantics` → engine `updateSemantics` creates the list route's `SemanticRoute`, whose one-time post-update callback (`semantics/route.dart:26-48`, run from `EngineSemanticsOwner._finalizeTree`, `semantics.dart
[truncated]

title: Multiple PlatformViews display incorrectly when showing and hiding
[Linux] liveRegion, SnackBar, AlertDialog and route changes produce no AT-SPI announcement; only explicit `SemanticsService.sendAnnouncement` does
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. flutter create a11y_repro, replace `lib/main.dart` with the code sample below, and run
   `flutter build linux --release`.
2. Start any AT-SPI event listener registered for `object:announcement`,
   `object:children-changed`, `object:state-changed`, `object:text-changed`,
   `object:property-change`, `window:` and `focus:`. I used `pyatspi.Registry.registerEventListener`
   (Accerciser's event monitor shows the same thing).
3. Run the bundle with `NONCE=<random string>` and `MARKFILE=<path>` in the environment. The app
   drives itself and needs no input:
   - SnackBar, then AlertDialog open and close.
   - `MaterialPageRoute` push and pop.
   - A text change inside `Semantics(liveRegion: true)`.
   - `SemanticsService.sendAnnouncement(...)` as a positive control.

   It writes one timestamped `MARK` line per step to `MARKFILE`, so the events can be windowed per
   step. Every string it shows carries the nonce, so no other source can produce a match.

### Expected results

As on Android and web, a live-region change and a SnackBar should produce a spoken announcement, and
an AlertDialog or a route push should be surfaced so Orca speaks it. On AT-SPI that means
`object:announcement` (ATK `notification`/`announcement`), or at least a `window:` or `focus:` event,
or an event from an alert/dialog-role source.

### Actual results

Flutter 3.44.8, atk 2.52.0 (runtime), at-spi2-core 2.52, Ubuntu 24.04, X11.

Two runs gave identical counts. The listener reported 0 errors and 0 dropped events.

| step | events from the app | `object:announcement` | alert/dialog/notification role source |
|---|---|---|---|
| quiet floor | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| SnackBar shown | 2 (children-changed) | **0** | 0 |
| AlertDialog open | 14 | **0** | **0** |
| AlertDialog close | 4 | 0 | 0 |
| route push | 11 | **0** | 0 |
| liveRegion text change | **0 (no event of any kind)** | **0** | 0 |
| `sendAnnouncement` (positive control) | 1 | **1**, text matches nonce | 0 |

The embedder's announcement path works: `sendAnnouncement` → `fl_view_accessible` → ATK
`notification` → `object:announcement`. But nothing the framework marks as `isLiveRegion`, and no
`scopesRoute`/`namesRoute` node, ever reaches that path. The liveRegion change emits no event at all,
not even `text-changed`. Orca is silent for every step except the positive control.

**Where it drops (master `7633739`, unchanged from 3.44.8 and 3.47.7):**

- The embedder API delivers the flags:
  [`embedder.h` L331, L333, L339](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/7633739168babd360765f528f634e3ba4b6a2626/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/embedder/embedder.h#L331-L339)
  carries `scopes_route`, `names_route` and `is_live_region`.
- [`fl_view_accessible_handle_update_semantics`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/7633739168babd360765f528f634e3ba4b6a2626/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/linux/fl_view_accessible.cc#L157-L182)
  copies flags, label and value onto each `FlAccessibleNode` and never compares

title: [material_ui] Tooltip(message:) is not hoverable by default (ignorePointer: true), failing WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.13 on web and desktop
body:
### Summary

`Tooltip` resolves `ignorePointer` as `widget.ignorePointer ?? _tooltipTheme.ignorePointer ?? widget.message != null` (`packages/material_ui/lib/src/tooltip.dart`), so a plain-`message` tooltip is invisible to hit testing. On any mouse platform, when the tooltip does not overlap its trigger (true for every ≤48 px `IconButton`, including `AppBar`'s `BackButton` and `DrawerButton`), moving the pointer from the trigger onto the tooltip fires the trigger's `onExit`, and `RawTooltip` dismisses it after `exitDuration` (100 ms).

WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.13 *Content on Hover or Focus* (Level AA) — **Hoverable**: "If pointer hover can trigger the additional content, then the pointer can be moved over the additional content without the additional content disappearing." The only exception is content whose presentation is controlled by the user agent (e.g. HTML `title`); Flutter's tooltip is author-drawn, so it is in scope.

Verified with a widget test (material_ui @ 5d34573, flutter master): hover trigger → move pointer onto tooltip → `pumpAndSettle` → dwell 2 s:

| `ignorePointer` | 40 px trigger (4 px gap) | 48 px trigger (0 px gap) | 200 px trigger (overlaps) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `null` (default) | **dismissed** | **dismissed** | stays (pointer never exits) |
| `true` | **dismissed** | **dismissed** | stays |
| `false` | stays, no flicker | stays, no flicker | stays, no flicker |

Same result for an `AppBar` `BackButton` on linux/macOS/windows: 40×40 button, tooltip box starts 4 px below it, tooltip dismissed on hover with the default.

### History

- #75885 → #83830 (2021): `Tooltip` was deliberately made hoverable and dismissible for exactly this requirement.
- #126207 (2023): overlay `IgnorePointer` removed so `richMessage` gesture recognizers work.
- #142465 → #161363 (Feb 2025): tooltips were blocking hover on neighbouring toolbar items; the fix added `ignorePointer` defaulting to `message != null`. Reviewed as "ok with this default behavior change"; neither the PR nor the issue mentions accessibility or #75885. This is where hoverability for plain messages was lost.
- #177678 (3.41) accidentally re-enabled hoverability; #182468 reported that as a regression; #182527 restored `ignorePointer` semantics via `RawTooltip.ignorePointer` and added a test asserting the tooltip disappears when hovered. The default was not revisited.
- flutter/packages#12918 (material_ui 1.5.0) added `TooltipThemeData.ignorePointer` as a global opt-in to hoverable plain tooltips. Default unchanged.

### Impact

Six open VPAT findings against `packages/material_ui/test_apps/a11y_assessments` (web, Chrome/Firefox/Safari): `#/date-picker`, `#/navigation-bar`, `#/check-box-list-tile`, `#/drawer`, `#/app-bar`, `#/navigation-drawer`. Those are the routes the auditors sampled; the defect reproduces on any route with an `AppBar` back button, i.e. nearly all of them. Internal refs: b/463913706, b/463912499, b/463910116, b/463900105, b/462283112, b/462276641.

The assessment app
