title: [Impeller][Vulkan][flutter_gpu] Pixel 10 (PowerVR DXT, driver 25.3): LoadAction.load of a color attachment stored by a previous render pass yields nothing; with MSAA the app SIGSEGVs in vulkan.powervr.so (CmdBeginRenderPass2)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Minimal app: https://github.com/iamspartacus66/flutter_gpu_powervr_repro (one Dart file + two tiny shaders).

1. `flutter run -d <pixel 10> --profile` (Impeller selects Vulkan on this device: driver 25.3 passes the ≥ 25.1 gate in `driver_info_vk.cc`).
2. Leave mode `two` (pass 1: clear + store, draws a gold ring; pass 2: `LoadAction.load` color + depth/stencil, draws a green tube) and switch AA to `no AA`.
3. The gold ring disappears. Switch back to `MSAA` and it returns. `single` mode (no load) is always correct.

Each pass is its own `CommandBuffer`; attachments are `StorageMode.devicePrivate`, `enableShaderReadUsage: false` for the depth/stencil and MSAA color; the presented texture is a `devicePrivate` r8g8b8a8 texture returned via `asImage()`.

### Expected results

Pass 2 loads the color/depth that pass 1 stored, so both objects render (as on Metal, on the same phone with the OpenGL ES backend forced, and on Adreno/Mali Vulkan devices).

### Actual results

On the Pixel 10 Vulkan backend the loaded color comes back empty (no AA). In our full renderer (same two-pass structure with 4× MSAA + `multisampleResolve`, plus a depth pre-pass and textures) the process instead crashes inside the vendor driver within seconds to a minute, every time a scene with the second pass is shown; the MSAA form has not yet been reduced to the minimal app (the minimal app with MSAA renders for 2+ minutes).

Crash backtrace from the full app (profile build, Flutter 3.47.5; identical on 3.47.6 and on master 3.49.0-1.0.pre-368):

```
Fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 1 (SEGV_MAPERR), fault addr 0x796eedd7b2
Build fingerprint: 'google/frankel/frankel:17/CP3A.260905.009/16091614:user/release-keys'
#00 pc 0000000000087ae8  /vendor/lib64/hw/vulkan.powervr.so (CmdBeginRenderPass2+2824)
#01 pc 0000000000181114  /vendor/lib64/hw/vulkan.powervr.so (IMG_vkCmdBeginRenderPass+52)
#02 pc 000000000087e9b8  libflutter.so
#03 pc 00000000007c7cc8  libflutter.so
#04 pc 0000000000932a28  libflutter.so (InternalFlutterGpu_RenderPass_...)
```

(An earlier variant with depth-store + stencil-dontCare split faulted in the driver's `SetupZLSState` instead; making the stencil actions follow the depth actions moved the fault to `CmdBeginRenderPass2`.)

The fault address is identical across processes/runs, which suggests an out-of-bounds read of a fixed driver table rather than a use-after-free.

Not reproducible on: the same phone with `ImpellerBackend=opengles` (profile build — everything renders, no crash); macOS/iOS Metal; Adreno/Mali Vulkan devices.

### Code sample

https://github.com/iamspartacus66/flutter_gpu_powervr_repro

### Screenshots or Video

<summary>Screenshots / Video demonstration</summary>

[Upload media here]

</details>

### Logs

## Device

- Google Pixel 10 (`frankel`), Android 17, build `CP3A.260905.009`

title: [material_ui] Assign SemanticsRole.option to Autocomplete option items
body:
`Autocomplete`'s option items never get `SemanticsRole.option`, so on web the options popup is exposed as `button` children (with `aria-current` for the highlighted one) rather than `option` children with `aria-selected`.

flutter/flutter#192971 adds `SemanticsRole.listBox` / `SemanticsRole.option` to the framework and engine. It cannot assign `option` to the items: `RawAutocomplete` only sees the opaque widget returned by the caller's `optionsViewBuilder`, and the default item builder lives in `material_ui` (`flutter/packages`), which is tested against stable and can't reference the new enum yet.

**Follow-up (this issue), in `flutter/packages/packages/material_ui`:**

- `lib/src/autocomplete.dart` `_AutocompleteOptions`: wrap the options view in `Semantics(role: SemanticsRole.listBox, container: true, explicitChildNodes: true)`.
- `lib/src/autocomplete.dart` `_AutocompleteOptionsList`: add `role: SemanticsRole.option` to the per-item `Semantics(button: true, selected: highlight, ...)` wrapper (`selected:` landed in flutter/packages#12918). The web engine resolves the explicit role before the `button` flag, and the framework's `option` check only requires a `listBox` *ancestor*, so the `ListView` scroll wrappers between them are fine.
- `lib/src/dropdown_menu.dart`: entries are `MenuItemButton`s inside a `MenuAnchor` with no `listBox` container, and `DropdownMenu` is a combobox pattern, so this needs a design decision (listbox vs. menu popup) rather than a one-liner. Evaluate separately.
- Re-verify `#/auto-complete` in `packages/material_ui/test_apps/a11y_assessments` (Chrome `Accessibility.getFullAXTree` should show `role=listbox` > `role=option` with `aria-selected`).

Blocked on #192971 shipping in a stable Flutter release; `material_ui` then needs a min-Flutter bump to that version (cf. #192839 for why it can't reference master-only APIs under the current `>=3.47.0` constraint).

Related VPAT: b/464138739, b/460080184. Related: #156371.

title: [in_app_purchase_storekit] Data race on productsCache / requestHandlers in StoreKit 1 product request completion (EXC_BAD_ACCESS)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

This is a data race we see in production crash reports; we do not have a deterministic reproduction.

1. Use `in_app_purchase` on iOS with StoreKit 1 (`InAppPurchaseStoreKitPlatform.enableStoreKit1()`).
2. Call `InAppPurchase.instance.queryProductDetails(...)` from more than one place around the same time (e.g. two screens loading products), and/or start a purchase while a product request is still in flight.

### Expected results

No crash. `productsCache` and `requestHandlers` in `InAppPurchasePlugin` are only touched from one thread.

### Actual results

The app occasionally crashes with `EXC_BAD_ACCESS (KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS)` inside `-[__NSDictionaryM setObject:forKey:]`, called from the completion of `startProductRequestProductIdentifiers(_:completion:)`. We also see a related `NSHashTable count underflow` crash.

`FIAPRequestHandler` calls its completion directly from the `SKProductsRequestDelegate` / `SKRequestDelegate` callbacks, which StoreKit delivers on a background dispatch queue (see the stack trace below: `_dispatch_worker_thread2` → `-[SKProductsRequest _start]_block_invoke_2`). Inside that completion, `InAppPurchasePlugin.swift` mutates shared state without synchronization:

- `startProductRequestProductIdentifiers(_:completion:)`: `self.productsCache[product.productIdentifier] = product` (`NSMutableDictionary`) and `self.requestHandlers.remove(handler)` (`NSHashTable`)
- `refreshReceiptReceiptProperties(_:completion:)`: `self?.requestHandlers.remove(handler)`

The same objects are accessed on the main thread elsewhere: `requestHandlers.add(handler)` in the Pigeon API entry points, `getProduct(productID:)` from `addPaymentPaymentMap`, and `productsCache[...] = product` in `paymentQueue(_:shouldAddStorePayment:for:)`. Neither collection is thread-safe, so overlapping requests (or a request racing with a purchase) can corrupt them.

This is present in 0.4.11+2 and unchanged in 0.4.13 and on `main` as of 2026-10-08.

A minimal fix that worked for us is to hop back to the main queue at the top of both completions, so that the cache write, the `completion` call and the handler removal all run on main:

```swift
handler.startProductRequest { [weak self] response, startProductRequestError in
  DispatchQueue.main.async { [weak self] in
    guard let self = self else { return }
    // ... existing body unchanged ...
  }
}
```

and the same for the `refreshReceiptReceiptProperties` completion.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

```dart
// StoreKit 1 is enabled before InAppPurchase.instance is first used.
await InAppPurchaseStoreKitPlatform.enableStoreKit1();

// Two independent callers query products concurrently.
await Future.wait([
  InAppPurchase.instance.queryProductDetails({'consumable_a', 'consumable_b'}),
  InAppPurchase.instance.queryProductDetails({'subscription_monthly'}),
]);
```

</details>

### Screenshots or Video

N/A

### Logs

<details open><summary>Logs</summary>

```cons

title: [flutter_tools] Deduplicate legacy JS interop errors in --wasm builds
body:
`flutter build web --wasm --no-deprecated-js-interop` prints three separate legacy JS interop error blocks for a single `dart:html` import, and `--wasm-dry-run` warning suppression will break when Dart 3.15 makes `--no-deprecated-js-interop` the default ([dart-lang/sdk#64523](https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64523)). - **Tri-state default bug**: [`build_web.dart#L164`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/d454b1b841d223f28bb725bb2928e2ac337b5611/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/commands/build_web.dart#L164) checks `deprecatedJsInterop == false`. When `--[no-]deprecated-js-interop` is omitted (`null`), this evaluates to `false` and will re-enable duplicate `--wasm-dry-run` warnings once the SDK default flips unless changed to `deprecatedJsInterop != true`. - **Redundant `--wasm` migration note**: `Dart2WasmTarget._checkForLegacyWebImports` appends `Note: WebAssembly compilation failed due to legacy web imports` even when `Dart2JSTarget` already printed the CFE deprecation error (and can be retired once [dart-lang/sdk#64527](https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64527) lands native CFE guidance on `dart2wasm`). - **Dual CFE dumps in `WebReleaseBundle`**: `Dart2WasmTarget` and `Dart2JSTarget` run concurrently via `Future.wait` and both log CFE errors on legacy web imports. Related: [flutter/flutter#193877](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/193877), [dart-lang/sdk#64523](https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64523), [dart-lang/sdk#64527](https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64527)
Detailed code trace & affected targets (AI-assisted) ### Steps to Reproduce & Observed Output 1. Add `import 'dart:html' as html;` to `lib/main.dart`. 2. Run `flutter build web --wasm --no-deprecated-js-interop` (which matches default `flutter build web --wasm` once [dart-lang/sdk#64523](https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/64523) flips `--deprecated-js-interop` to `false`). ```text Compiling lib/main.dart for the Web... lib/main.dart:2:8: Error: Import of deprecated JS interop library 'dart:html' is not allowed. Deprecated JS interop libraries are planned for removal in Dart 4.0. Migrate to 'package:web' and 'dart:js_interop' (see https://dart.dev/interop/js-interop/past-js-interop), or temporarily enable the 'deprecated-js-interop' option. import 'dart:html' as html; ^ Info: Deprecated JS interop libraries are imported through: main library └── package:web_test/main.dart └── dart:html Error: Compilation failed. lib/main.dart:2:8: Error: Dart library 'dart:html' is not available on this platform. import 'dart:html' as html; ^ Context: The unavailable library 'dart:html' is imported through these packages: main.dart => package:web_test => dart:html Detailed import paths for (some of) these imports: main.dart => package:web_test/main.dart => dart:html lib/main.dart:5:8: Error: Undefined name 'window'. html.window.console.log('Hello from legacy web'); ^^^^^^ Note: [truncated]

title: Provide an opt-in for CocoaPods
body:
Once you can [no longer opt-out of SwiftPM](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/193978), we can provide a way to opt-in to still use CocoaPods. This should include a disclaimer that Flutter no longer supports CocoaPods and to proceed at your own risk.

## Proposal

### Introduce a `--force-cocoapods` flag

This can be passed to a command to allow CocoaPods to be used for plugins that haven't migrated to SwiftPM yet

e.g. `flutter build ios --force-cocoapods`, `flutter run --force-cocoapods`

### Introduce a `--force-cocoapods-only` flag
* This must be passed for every command to disable SwiftPM and only use CocoaPods
* e.g. `flutter build ios --force-cocoapods-only`, `flutter run --force-cocoapods-only`

---
Both of these must be passed for each command and not saved to the config. We'll want to validate that they work appropriately for `flutter build ios-framework`, `flutter build macos-framework`, `flutter build swift-package`

We could also print a log saying "Please leave on comment on https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/xxx explaining why you still need to use CocoaPods."

title: No longer allow SwiftPM to be disabled globally or per project
body:
Once we stop actively supporting CocoaPods, the SwiftPM feature flag should be removed/deprecated so that it is always enabled.

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/c97791db7632d1a35eb8ed15b4a9ac3dc892304d/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/features.dart#L240-L249

body:

title: Style guide changes for package-private APIs and enums
body:
https://github.com/flutter/rfc/pull/30

Currently, the styleguide suggest no package private, but in practice, it is not followed. Some of the examples are experimental APIs or just something that can change frequently and is not meant to be consume publicly.

Instead of forcing them public and without any guardrail for consumption and breaks people. We should think about whether we should change the guideline to be permissive in this matter while adding guardrail so consumer won't accidentally use these classes without knowing they can breaking frequently.

As part of this, we should also thinking about enum in public API as current lint and guideline suggest exhaustive switch case to handle enum, which is not the most appropriate way to consume some the enum API.

This proposal directly contradict https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/108632.

title: [flutter_tools] Support heartbeat / liveness monitoring for long-running tool extension RPCs
body:
In #193748, `ExtensionBuildManager.build` invokes the `build.build` RPC on a tool extension isolate without a wall-clock timeout (`timeout: null` in `ExtensionConnection.sendRequest`) because complex native builds can legitimately run for many minutes.

While `ExtensionConnection` already monitors `Isolate.addOnExitListener` and `Isolate.addErrorListener` to fail in-flight requests immediately if an extension isolate crashes or exits, a silently deadlocked extension isolate during a long-running operation (`build.build`, `artifact.downloadArtifacts`, etc.) will hang indefinitely without a liveness mechanism.

We should consider introducing a heartbeat / progress notification mechanism between `package:flutter_tools_extension` and `ExtensionConnection`:
1. Allow long-running extension RPC handlers (or the extension isolate runner) to emit periodic heartbeat or build progress notifications over the JSON-RPC channel.
2. Support an optional inactivity/heartbeat timeout on `ExtensionConnection.sendRequest` that resets whenever a heartbeat or progress notification is received from the extension, rather than bounding total wall-clock execution time.

On Windows, an unmodified mouse side-button shortcut intermittently stops working after switching windows with Alt+Tab. The application's input diagnostics show an extra Alt modifier even though Alt is physically released. Pressing and releasing Alt restores the shortcut. Some keyboard shortcuts are also affected.

**Confirmed in the original application:** the Alt+Tab / mouse-refocus sequence, the phantom Alt modifier on a mouse back-button press, and recovery after pressing and releasing Alt. The application obtains pointer modifiers directly from `HardwareKeyboard.instance.isAltPressed` / `isControlPressed` / `isShiftPressed` / `isMetaPressed`; it does not map the side button to an Alt key event.

1. Create a standard desktop project:

6. Return to the Flutter window by clicking its body with the mouse. Do not press any keyboard key first.

title: [material_ui] Modal bottom sheets retain obsolete CurvedAnimation status listeners after drags
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Repeated nonclosing drags on a modal bottom sheet leave obsolete `CurvedAnimation` helpers subscribed to the route animation. They accumulate while the sheet is open. After the sheet is dismissed and its state is disposed, the subscriptions also remain if the application keeps its caller-owned `transitionAnimationController` alive.

The affected framework code is [`_ModalBottomSheetState` in bottom_sheet.dart](https://github.com/hangy233/flutter/blob/540676e356949938eff22c70ade2186b1e14bb2b/packages/flutter/lib/src/material/bottom_sheet.dart#L682). The reproduction uses `package:flutter/material.dart` and the framework implementation in that checkout.

A caller-owned controller may be retained for its host widget's lifetime and disposed when that widget is removed. Controller ownership does not require retaining helpers belonging to an already-disposed sheet. If the route owns and eventually disposes its controller, disposal releases these subscriptions; the accumulation while the sheet is open still occurs.

Ordinary usage that triggers the problem passes a host-owned controller and repeatedly performs short drags that return the sheet to its open position:

```dart
showModalBottomSheet<void>(
  context: context,
  transitionAnimationController: controller,
  builder: (BuildContext context) =>
      const SizedBox(height: 300, child: Text('Bottom sheet')),
);
```

## Automated demo

The [single-file demo](https://github.com/hangy233/flutter/blob/540676e356949938eff22c70ade2186b1e14bb2b/dev/manual_tests/lib/bottom_sheet_memory.dart) has one **Run 200 cycles** button. It opens the sheet, runs 200 actual library callback cycles, closes the sheet automatically, and prints numeric readings before, during, and after the run. The application keeps its controller alive after closing and releases it before the next run.

The fast loop invokes the actual `BottomSheet` callbacks:

```dart
for (var i = 1; i <= 200; i++) {
  sheet.onDragStart!(DragStartDetails());
  sheet.onDragEnd!(DragEndDetails(primaryVelocity: 0), isClosing: false);
}
```

This bypasses pointer recognition and gesture animation waiting. These are callback cycles, not 200 simulated user gestures.

To make the retention visible quickly, the demo deliberately attaches a `Uint8List(1000000)` test buffer to each forwarded status subscription. The callback captures and accesses that buffer; unregistering the callback releases the subscription's ownership of it. The printed MB value is the number of registered subscriptions multiplied by 1,000,000 bytes.

**The 1 MB buffers are deliberate amplification. Ordinary drags do not leak 1 MB each.** The readings describe test buffers still owned by registered callbacks; they are not a measured browser heap, total Chrome memory, or proof that garbage collection has already reclaimed released buffers.

### Run the reproduction

title: [Impeller] Picture.toImageSync allocates a new GPU texture on every call; chained offscreen passes spend ~30% of the raster thread creating textures
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the code sample below on an iPhone in release mode (`flutter run --release`).
2. It renders, every frame, a chain of 32 offscreen passes of 256×256 px with `Picture.toImageSync`, each pass drawing the previous pass's image (the pattern a multi-pass effect needs when every pass feeds the next one within the same frame), and draws the last image.
3. Profile the raster thread with Instruments (Time Profiler, attach to the app).
4. Compare with `--dart-define=MODE=layer`, which records the same amount of offscreen work with nested `Canvas.saveLayer` in a single picture (not visually identical — it only serves as a baseline for the cost of offscreen render targets that come from Impeller's render target cache).

### Expected results

Images that are created every frame and disposed right after use should not cost a new GPU texture allocation each time — or there should be a way to opt into reusing the render target of an image that has been disposed (similar to what `RenderTargetCache` already does for `saveLayer`).

### Actual results

Every `toImageSync` call allocates a fresh texture: `DisplayListToTexture` (`impeller/display_list/dl_dispatcher.cc`) creates its render target through a new `RenderTargetAllocator` on the context's resource allocator, bypassing `RenderTargetCache`. On iOS, every allocation goes through `-[AGXTexture initWithDevice:desc:isSuballocDisabled:]` → `IOGPUResourceCreate` (a kernel call).

Raster thread, iPhone 16 Pro Max (iOS 27.0), 32 passes × 256×256 per frame at 120 Hz, 10 s Time Profiler each:

| mode | raster thread CPU | creating textures (`AGXTexture init…` / `IOGPUResourceCreate`) | render pass setup (`renderCommandEncoderWithDescriptor`) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `snapshot` (`Picture.toImageSync` chain) | 41 % of one core | **29 %** of the raster thread (≈ 1.0 ms per frame) | 23 % |
| `layer` (`saveLayer`, render target cache) | 26 % of one core | **0 %** | 32 % |

Note that the cost of the `toImageSync` work does not show up in `FrameTiming.rasterDuration` (snapshot mode reports a raster p50 of 0.27 ms against 2.1 ms for the layer mode), because the snapshots are rasterized as separate tasks on the raster thread. The time is real, though: it delays the next frame's rasterization, and in a larger app with more and bigger offscreen passes we see frames start 0.5–1 s late right after launch, while the first big textures are being allocated.

There is currently no alternative that keeps zero frames of latency: `flutter_gpu`'s `Texture.fromImage` cannot wrap a `toImageSync` image (it is not rasterized yet), and `FragmentShader.setImageSampler` only accepts a `ui.Image` (#136025).

Possible directions (any one would help):
- let a `ui.Image` produced by `toImageSync` return its render target to `RenderTargetCache` when it is disposed, so that the next `toImageSync` of the same size and format can reuse it;
- or an API to render a `Picture` into an existing image/texture of the same size (e.g. a

title: [Impeller] macOS: text smears/ghosts while another Metal process keeps the GPU busy and unified memory nearly full; clean with --no-enable-impeller
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. On an Apple Silicon Mac (here: M5 Max, 128 GB unified memory, macOS 27.0.1), run a Flutter macOS desktop app that shows scrolling text (a chat view) with Impeller enabled (the default; no `FLTEnableImpeller` key).
2. While the app is open, make another process keep the GPU busy and unified memory nearly full. Our app launches KoboldCpp (llama.cpp) with a ~20 GB GGUF model on Metal and sends it a ~17,000-token prompt; any Metal workload of that size should do (e.g. `llama-server` loading a large model and processing a long prompt).
3. Scroll or let the chat view repaint while the prompt is being processed.

The app is open source: https://github.com/linux4life1/front-porch-AI (Flutter desktop, macOS/Windows/Linux). The chat view is a plain `ListView` of `Text`/`RichText` bubbles.

### Expected results

Text renders normally, as it does when the GPU is idle.

### Actual results

Text smears and ghosts: glyphs are drawn stretched or doubled, and remnants of earlier text stay on screen until the next repaint. It happens only while the other Metal process is saturating the GPU/unified memory; when that finishes, text is clean again.

Running the same build with `flutter run --no-enable-impeller` (Skia) makes the smearing disappear completely under the same load, so it is specific to Impeller.

During the same load the engine also prints, once per late frame:

```
[ERROR:flutter/lib/ui/window/platform_configuration.cc(475)] Reported frame time is older than the last one; clamping. 412949971970 < 412949978254 ~= 6284
```

(dozens of lines in a burst while the prompt is read). Reducing the other process's thread count reduces those lines but the smearing persists as long as the GPU is busy.

My guess from the symptoms: the glyph atlas texture update is not synchronised with the GPU reading it when the GPU is slow to schedule the app's work, so a frame samples a partially written atlas. The macOS embedder also does not forward memory-pressure to the engine (#193015), so nothing clears Impeller's caches when unified memory gets tight.

### Code sample

No reduced sample beyond the app above; the trigger is the external GPU load, not specific widgets. A `ListView` of long `Text` widgets while `llama-server` processes a long prompt with a model that fills most of unified memory should reproduce it. I can record a screen video on request.

### Screenshots or Video

Can be provided on request (the smearing is visible for the seconds a long prompt takes to process).

### Logs

See the `Reported frame time is older than the last one; clamping` burst above. No other engine output.

### Flutter Doctor output

```

title: macOS hot restart fails writing DevFS files into a sandboxed app container
body:
# macOS hot restart cannot write DevFS files into a sandboxed app container

## Summary

A Flutter macOS debug app can launch and connect to the VM service, but hot
restart fails while the tool writes the compiled kernel file (`main.dart.dill`)
under the app's sandbox container. The failure was reproduced in a minimal
Flutter counter app signed for macOS with App Sandbox enabled.

## Environment

- Flutter 3.47.6, framework revision
  `5fc346839b5d0eef006ed8404392afb4dfae428d`
- macOS 27.0.1 and Xcode 27.0 (27A266a). These versions were measured on the
  same host after the original failure; they were not printed in that failure
  log.
- Apple Development-signed arm64 macOS app. For both runs the bundle identifier,
  signing authority/team, and effective entitlements were the same. The
  effective entitlements included `app-sandbox`, `cs.allow-jit`,
  `get-task-allow`, and `network.server`. The app was rebuilt/re-signed for the
  patched run, so its code-signature hash and signing timestamp changed.

## Minimal reproduction

1. Create a macOS Flutter app using the default counter-app source.
2. Enable the App Sandbox for the Debug configuration and retain the JIT,
   debugger, and VM-service network entitlements needed for a debug run. Sign
   with an Apple Development identity.
3. From the project root, run `flutter run -d macos --verbose`.
4. After the app launches and the VM service connects, press uppercase `R`
   once to request a hot restart.

## Expected

The tool writes the updated kernel and other DevFS entries and restarts the app.

## Observed before the change

The app launches and connects to the VM service, then hot restart exits while
creating `main.dart.dill` beneath a path of the form
`<sandbox-container>/Data/tmp/<run>/<app>/main.dart.dill`, followed by Flutter's
generic read/write-permissions guidance. A complete raw stack trace and errno
were not retained. Inspection of the Flutter 3.47.6 code shows macOS selecting
`LocalDevFSWriter`; its direct filesystem write path reaches
`File.copySync`/`createSync` for that container URL.

## Candidate change

In the isolated checkout based on the revision above, `MacOSDevice` overrides
`createDevFSWriter` and returns a small adapter that delegates to the existing
VM-service HTTP writer passed by `DevFS.update`. Other desktop platforms retain
`DesktopDevice`'s local writer. The adapter does not catch or mask transfer
errors.

```dart
@override
DevFSWriter createDevFSWriter(ApplicationPackage? app, String? userIdentifier) {
  return MacOSHttpDevFSWriter();
}

class MacOSHttpDevFSWriter implements DevFSWriter {
  @override
  Future<void> write(Map<Uri, DevFSContent> entries, Uri baseUri, DevFSWriter parent) {
    return parent.write(entries, baseUri, parent);
  }
}
```

Changed files:

- `packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/macos/macos_device.dart`
- `packages/flutter_tools/test/general.shard/macos/macos_device_test.dart`

The focused tests cover macOS writer selection, delegation, and propagati

        depend on it to compile against version 37 or later of the Android APIs.
        :google_mobile_ads is currently compiled against android-36.
```

Starting AGP 9, a module's compileSdk must be >= the `minCompileSdk` of each of its dependencies declared in its AAR metadata. Admob is hardcoded at `compileSdk 36` and consumes `webview_flutter_android` whose metadata requires compileSdk 37 or later. So this fails with a build error.

title: [Impeller] `Canvas.drawVertices` with an image shader ignores the paint's colour filter
[Impeller] A colour filter on the `drawRawAtlas` paint turns off edge anti-aliasing: sprites snap to whole pixels
[Impeller][OpenGL ES][Android] Flutter GPU pipeline creation with no onscreen surface deadlocks the main and raster threads
body:
### Steps to reproduce

The app (all files in the code sample below): `flutter_gpu` only, a one-triangle shader bundle built by a `flutter_gpu_shaders` build hook, `EnableFlutterGPU` on and `ImpellerBackend` set to `opengles` in the manifest. `main` draws one triangle into an offscreen texture before `runApp`, after an optional delay (`DELAY_MS`). `launch.sh` (also below) cold starts the app and reports `pass` when `repro: first frame` reaches the device log within 30 s, else `hang` and a `debuggerd -b` dump.

1. Android emulator, API 35, x86_64 (Impeller selects OpenGL ES; the device's GLES is SwiftShader). On an arm64 emulator or device, build with `--target-platform android-arm64` instead of `android-x64`. On the emulator `debuggerd -b` needs `adb root`.
2. Pipeline creation at the top of `main`:
   ```sh
   cd repro_app && flutter build apk --profile --target-platform android-x64
   adb install -r build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-profile.apk
   cd .. && ./launch.sh on runs/main_on1.log
   ```
3. Pipeline creation 1 s after `main` starts, display on, then display off at launch and on after 4 s:
   ```sh
   cd repro_app && flutter build apk --profile --target-platform android-x64 --dart-define=DELAY_MS=1000
   adb install -r build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-profile.apk
   cd .. && ./launch.sh on runs/delay_on1.log && ./launch.sh off-wake runs/delay_offwake1.log
   ```

### Expected results

`RenderPass.draw` returns, the app draws its first frame and stays responsive, whether or not the activity has a surface when the pipeline is created.

### Actual results

| Build | Launch | Result |
|---|---|---|
| no delay | cold, display on | hang, 3 of 3 |
| `DELAY_MS=1000` | cold, display on | pass, 3 of 3 (first frame within 2 s) |
| `DELAY_MS=1000` | cold, display off, on after 4 s | hang, 3 of 3 |

In every hang the log ends at `repro: drawing before the first frame`, the launch screen stays, and the main and raster threads both wait in `pthread_cond_wait` for the whole 30 s, after the display is back on. Every dump has the same two stacks.

Cause, from the stacks and the source at engine `af7e796e16`: on OpenGL ES, `flutter::gpu::RenderPass::GetOrCreatePipeline` posts a task to the raster thread and blocks the calling thread on its future:

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/af7e796e161ae0bb1ff0758c71a7105418bd9ded/engine/src/flutter/lib/gpu/render_pass.cc#L154-L177

The raster task calls `PipelineLibraryGLES::GetPipeline`, which queues the pipeline build on `ReactorGLES` and returns a future, and waits on it with `PipelineFuture::Get()`:

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/af7e796e161ae0bb1ff0758c71a7105418bd9ded/engine/src/flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/gles/pipeline_library_gles.cc#L268-L312

The reactor runs operations only on a thread where the onscreen or offscreen EGL context is current:

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/af7e796e161ae0bb1ff0758c71a7105418bd9ded/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/android_context_gl
[truncated]

title: Share the PageStorageKey lookup used by PageStorageBucket and Expansible
body:
### Use case

`Expansible` builds its own `PageStorage` identifier from the `PageStorageKey`s above it (#192195). To do that, `_ExpansibleState._computeStorageIdentifier` repeats the key lookup in `PageStorageBucket._allKeys`, because the two are in different libraries and cannot share a private method. If one changes and the other does not, `Expansible` reads an empty slot.

### Proposal

As @Mairramer suggested in #192195, add one shared helper that returns the `PageStorageKey`s for a context, for example a static method on `PageStorage`, and migrate both `PageStorageBucket` and `Expansible` to it.

Related: #193699

title: [pigeon] Stop binding HostApi interfaces with jnigen: they're unused and make up 35% of the `.jni.dart` file
[pigeon] Swift FFI (`swift_use_ffi`) generates code that doesn't compile for files with event channels or ProxyApis
body:
Found while investigating #193195.

## Summary

Pigeon accepts Swift FFI mode for pigeon files that contain event channels or ProxyApis, but the Swift it generates doesn't compile. Users get a wall of Swift errors instead of a clear message at generation time.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Write a pigeon file with a `@HostApi()` and an `@EventChannelApi()`, or use pigeon's own [`pigeons/event_channel_tests.dart`](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/e18a54144e0541b9bfbc4b7cb9837bc224d9bbb7/packages/pigeon/pigeons/event_channel_tests.dart) or [`pigeons/proxy_api_tests.dart`](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/e18a54144e0541b9bfbc4b7cb9837bc224d9bbb7/packages/pigeon/pigeons/proxy_api_tests.dart).
2. Generate Swift with FFI enabled (`--swift_use_ffi`, or `SwiftOptions(useFfi: true)`).
3. Type-check the generated file against the SDK, the way swiftgen compiles it:
   ```sh
   xcrun swiftc -typecheck -sdk "$(xcrun --show-sdk-path --sdk macosx)" Generated.swift
   ```

## Expected results

Either pigeon rejects the input with a clear error, or the generated Swift compiles.

## Actual results

Pigeon writes the file without complaint, and it fails to type-check:

| Input | Result |
| :--- | :--- |
| Host API only | Compiles |
| `pigeons/native_interop_tests.dart` | Compiles |
| Host API + 1 event channel | 56 errors; 34 are missing Flutter types (`FlutterEventSink`, `FlutterStandardReader`/`Writer`, `FlutterError`) |
| `pigeons/event_channel_tests.dart` | 208 errors |
| `pigeons/proxy_api_tests.dart` | 1,118 errors |

## Cause

- In FFI mode the Swift generator skips `import Flutter`/`import FlutterMacOS` ([swift_generator.dart L318](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/e18a54144e0541b9bfbc4b7cb9837bc224d9bbb7/packages/pigeon/lib/src/swift/swift_generator.dart#L318)).
- It uses the FFI codec only when the file has no event channels and no ProxyApis. Otherwise it falls back to the channel codec, which is built on `FlutterStandardReader`/`Writer` ([L530](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/e18a54144e0541b9bfbc4b7cb9837bc224d9bbb7/packages/pigeon/lib/src/swift/swift_generator.dart#L530)). The event channel and ProxyApi code also uses Flutter types directly.
- Swift FFI validation checks only `@TaskQueue` and package dependencies ([pigeon_lib_internal.dart L603–620](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/e18a54144e0541b9bfbc4b7cb9837bc224d9bbb7/packages/pigeon/lib/src/pigeon_lib_internal.dart#L603-L620)), so nothing stops the combination.
- Adding the Flutter import wouldn't fix it. swiftgen compiles the file with `swiftc` against the bare SDK, without a Flutter framework search path.

The Kotlin JNI side doesn't have this compile problem: in JNI mode the Kotlin generator imports the Flutter embedding for files with event channels or ProxyApis.

## Proposed fix

1. **Now:** in Swift FFI validation, reject files that contain event channels or ProxyApis, with a message such as: *"Event channels and ProxyApis are not supported with Swift FFI
[truncated]

title: [pigeon] Native interop (JNI) calls fail with ClassNotFoundException in minified Android release builds
body:
Found while investigating #193195.

## Summary

Flutter's Gradle plugin enables R8 for Android release builds by default. R8 renames or removes classes that pigeon's JNI native interop looks up by name, so most native interop calls fail in a default release build. Debug and profile builds aren't affected, which makes this easy to miss until shipping.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Generate a pigeon file with `kotlin_use_jni` (for example pigeon's own [`pigeons/native_interop_tests.dart`](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/e18a54144e0541b9bfbc4b7cb9837bc224d9bbb7/packages/pigeon/pigeons/native_interop_tests.dart)).
2. Build the app in release mode with default settings (`flutter build apk --release` or `flutter run --release`).
3. Call native interop methods that take or return a data class or an enum, are `@async`, throw an error, or go through a FlutterApi.

## Expected results

All calls behave as in debug builds.

## Actual results

In a release build of pigeon's test plugin, **15 of 25 probe calls fail** with `ClassNotFoundException`.

- **Pass:** `getInstance`, `noop`, and echoes of `int`, `double`, `bool`, `String`, `Uint8List`, `List`, `List<int>` and `Map`.
- **Fail:** everything that touches an enum, a data class, an async method, an error, or the FlutterApi.
- 14 of the 15 failures name the generated error class instead of the class that actually went missing. The generated error handling looks the error class up by name too, and that lookup fails first, which hides the original failure.

## Cause

`mapping.txt` from the release build shows R8:
- renamed the data classes and enums (for example `NativeInteropAllTypes` → `eg`);
- removed the FlutterApi interface and its Registrar;
- inlined the generated error class away;
- renamed `kotlin.Unit`, `kotlin.Result`, `kotlin.Result$Failure`, `kotlin.coroutines.Continuation` and `kotlin.coroutines.intrinsics.CoroutineSingletons`, which `package:jni` and the generated Dart look up by name.

Only `@Keep` classes survived intact. The generated Kotlin has exactly three `@Keep` annotations: the HostApi interface ([L1005](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/e18a54144e0541b9bfbc4b7cb9837bc224d9bbb7/packages/pigeon/platform_tests/test_plugin/android/src/main/kotlin/com/example/test_plugin/NativeInteropTests.gen.kt#L1005)), its Registrar ([L1625](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/e18a54144e0541b9bfbc4b7cb9837bc224d9bbb7/packages/pigeon/platform_tests/test_plugin/android/src/main/kotlin/com/example/test_plugin/NativeInteropTests.gen.kt#L1625)) and `getInstance` ([L1642](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/e18a54144e0541b9bfbc4b7cb9837bc224d9bbb7/packages/pigeon/platform_tests/test_plugin/android/src/main/kotlin/com/example/test_plugin/NativeInteropTests.gen.kt#L1642)). `package:jni`'s consumer rules keep only its own package.

Re-running with the generated classes kept, plus six Kotlin classes (the five above and `kotlin.coroutines.intrinsics.IntrinsicsKt`), made **all 25 calls pass**
[truncated]

title: [iPhone Duo Support] Support adaptive landscape sidebar positioning for Scaffold and Cupertino navigation components
body:
### Use case

On wider viewports and landscape orientations (specifically foldable devices, dual-screen form factors, and iOS landscape adaptations), bottom navigation bars and top app bars consume critical vertical screen real estate.

Native system UI (such as iOS landscape docks and adaptive app bars) moves these controls into a vertical right-hand bar. Developers building cross-platform Flutter applications targeting wider displays currently have no built-in way to allow Scaffold, CupertinoTabBar, or CupertinoNavigationBar to automatically adapt to side-mounted edge alignments without completely abandoning Scaffold and writing custom Row layouts from scratch.

### Proposal

Introduce adaptive positioning options to Scaffold and Cupertino navigation components (CupertinoTabBar, CupertinoNavigationBar) that allow navigation bars and app bars to dock vertically along the right or left edge on wide viewports or landscape orientations.

Key Enhancements Requested:

Scaffold / CupertinoTabScaffold Alignment Support: Allow specifying side alignment parameters (e.g., NavigationSide.right) or automatic OS-level side adaptation for bottomNavigationBar and appBar.

CupertinoTabBar Vertical Mode: Enable CupertinoTabBar to render vertically with properly aligned icons, labels, and safe area insets when positioned on the side edge.

Adaptive Breakpoints: Provide native material/cupertino layout delegate behavior that automatically transitions bottom navigation bars into side-docked bars based on aspect ratio or device posture.

title: [Flutter GPU] Hot reloading a compute shader dereferences a null render pipeline entry point
body:
Part of #188474.

Hot reloading a shader bundle evicts the pipelines that used each changed shader through `PipelineLibrary::RemovePipelinesWithEntryPoint`. On Metal, Vulkan and OpenGL ES that function dereferences `GetEntrypointForStage(function->GetStage())` for every cached pipeline. Render pipelines have no compute entry point, so reloading a compute shader dereferences a null pointer, and compute pipelines are never evicted at all.

Nothing reaches this today because Flutter GPU cannot create compute pipelines yet. It will crash as soon as #188480 lands.

## Changes

- Skip pipelines that have no entry point for the reloaded shader's stage.
- Evict compute pipelines that use the reloaded compute shader.

## Testing

A unit test that reloads a compute shader while render and compute pipelines are cached, on Metal and Vulkan.

## Dependencies

None.

title: [Impeller] OpenGL ES command buffer completion waits for the GPU
body:
Part of #188474.

On OpenGL ES, a command buffer's completion callback fires when the reactor consumes its commands on the raster thread, not when the GPU finishes them (`CommandBufferGLES::OnSubmitCommands`). That is enough for buffer reuse, which GL synchronizes implicitly, but not for readback: a readback Future completed at that point could hand the app bytes before the GPU has written them.

## Changes

- After a command buffer's commands are encoded, insert a `glFenceSync` and report completion once it signals.
- Check pending fences from a task on the raster thread rather than only when frames are drawn, so completion arrives even when the app renders nothing further.
- Keep the existing reactor-granularity tracking for internal buffer reuse if it is cheaper there.

## Testing

On the OpenGL ES backend, a completion callback fires only after the GPU finished the work, and still fires when no further frames are drawn.

## Dependencies

None. Needed by the Flutter GPU readback API on #188474.

title: [Impeller] HAL support for GPU-to-CPU readback
body:
Part of #188474.

The readback API decided on #188474 (`CommandBuffer.readBuffer` and `CommandBuffer.readTexture` returning `Future<ByteData>`) needs backend support that does not exist yet:
- There is no buffer-to-buffer copy in the HAL, so a device-private result cannot reach host-visible memory.
- On Vulkan, nothing makes GPU writes visible to the host: no host barrier after a copy into a readback buffer, and no invalidate for non-coherent memory.
- On Intel Macs, host-visible buffers use Managed storage and nothing calls `synchronizeResource`, so the CPU may read stale data.

## Changes

- `BlitPass` buffer-to-buffer copy on Metal and Vulkan, and on OpenGL ES 3.0+ through `glCopyBufferSubData`.
- Vulkan: a transfer-to-host barrier after copies into readback buffers, and `vkInvalidateMappedMemoryRanges` before the CPU reads non-coherent memory.
- Metal: `synchronizeResource` on a blit encoder for Managed buffers and textures before completion.
- Pooled host-visible staging buffers for readback, reused across reads.

## Testing

Buffer and texture round trips on Metal and Vulkan: write on the GPU, copy to a staging buffer, and read the expected bytes on the CPU after completion.

## Dependencies

None.

title: [Impeller] Automatic compute synchronization on Metal and Vulkan
body:
Part of #188474.

The #188474 contract makes synchronization automatic: a write by an earlier dispatch or pass is visible to every later dispatch, draw, copy and readback without user action. Today it is not.

- The Metal compute encoder is created with `MTLDispatchTypeConcurrent`, so dependent dispatches in one pass race unless the caller adds barriers. Hazards across encoders are already handled, since Metal resources are tracked.
- On Vulkan the only automatic barrier is at the end of a compute pass, and it targets vertex input and index reads only. Fragment, uniform, sampled-texture, transfer, host and indirect consumers are not covered, and neither are render to compute or copy to compute.

## Changes

- Metal: create the compute encoder with `MTLDispatchTypeSerial`.
- Vulkan: a compute-to-compute memory barrier between dispatches in a pass, and a barrier at the end of a compute pass whose destination covers vertex input, index and indirect reads, vertex, fragment and compute shader reads, transfer and host.
- Vulkan: render and copy pass exits include the compute stage in their destination scope.
- Keep `AddBufferMemoryBarrier` and `AddTextureMemoryBarrier` as the manual override.

## Testing

On Metal and Vulkan, with Vulkan synchronization validation enabled:
- Two dependent dispatches in one pass with no manual barrier.
- A compute pass writing a vertex buffer that a later render pass draws.
- A render pass writing a texture that a later compute pass reads.

## Dependencies

None.

title: [Impeller] Compute dispatch contract cleanup: literal workgroup sizes, device limits, persistent bindings
body:
Part of #188474.

#188601 moved compute dispatch to 3D workgroup counts, but several backend differences remain in the dispatch contract that the Flutter GPU compute API will expose.

## Changes

- Remove the Vulkan specialization constant that overrides `constant_id = 0` with `maxComputeWorkGroupSize[0]` on every compute pipeline. It silently clobbers any user constant with that id. Convert `prefix_sum_test.comp` to a literal `local_size`.
- Validate the workgroup size against device limits when a compute pipeline is created, on Metal (the pipeline's `maxTotalThreadsPerThreadgroup` and the device's per-dimension maximum) and on Vulkan (`maxComputeWorkGroupSize` and `maxComputeWorkGroupInvocations`), and fail with a clear error.
- Expose the limits on `Capabilities`: max workgroup invocations, max workgroup size, max workgroup count, max shared memory and the minimum storage-buffer offset alignment.
- A dispatch with a zero count is a no-op on every backend instead of an error.
- Bindings persist across dispatches within a pass on every backend. Vulkan currently resets the pipeline and bindings after each dispatch.
- Fix the Metal compute pass pushing a debug group whose pop only happens in debug builds.

## Testing

`compute_unittests` on Metal and Vulkan: a literal-size prefix sum, an oversized workgroup rejected at pipeline creation, a zero-count dispatch, and two dispatches sharing one set of bindings.

## Dependencies

None.

title: [Flutter GPU] Pass lifecycle: one recording pass per command buffer, ended by the next command
body:
Part of #188474.

A Flutter GPU pass never ends until `submit()`. lib/gpu creates the backend pass when the Dart pass is created and encodes every pass at submit, so on Metal two passes in one command buffer have two command encoders open at once, which Metal does not allow. Apps work around this today with one command buffer per render pass, and compute passes (#188480) would hit the same limit.

This implements the pass lifecycle decided on #188474. It changes render passes as well as compute, so it lands on its own.

## Changes

- A command buffer records one pass at a time, and passes execute in the order they are created.
- Creating the next pass, or recording a copy or readback on the command buffer, ends the current pass. `submit()` ends the last one.
- When a pass ends, its Metal or Vulkan encoder ends at that point, so a command buffer can hold any number of passes. OpenGL ES keeps encoding at submit, in the same order.
- `RenderPass.end()` ends a pass explicitly and is harmless to call twice.
- Any call on an ended pass throws a `StateError` naming what ended it, for example "RenderPass was ended when createRenderPass() was called on the same CommandBuffer".

## Testing

`gpu_test.dart` on Metal, Vulkan and OpenGL ES:
- Two render passes in one command buffer both render correctly.
- Using a pass after the next pass was created, after a copy, or after `end()` throws.
- Calling `end()` twice is harmless.

## Dependencies

None.

title: newDsl Flutter Fix is shown alongside the "unsupported AGP version" error
body:
If a project uses an existing Android Gradle Plugin (AGP) version newer than Flutter supports, the Flutter Gradle Plugin fails the build with an error telling the user to downgrade AGP.

The Flutter tool also prints the `android.newDsl` Flutter Fix message for the same failure. That message tells the user to update Flutter or opt out of android.newDsl, while the Gradle error tells them to downgrade AGP. Seeing both at once suggests two separate problems, and the user can't tell which fix to apply.

```
$ flutter build apk

     Alternatively, use the flag "--android-skip-build-dependency-validation" to bypass this check (unsupported; your build may fail).

title: [Windows] Plugins registration failure should not prevent app from start like on Android
body: On Windows, Flutter app does not launch at all when a single plugin DLL cannot be loaded. On Android the same kind of failure is caught per plugin and logged, and app starts. Some plugins are not that important to block launch of whole process and are better to caught with `MissingPluginException` on Dart side instead of fail that can not be bypassed without removing whole plugin for every user/platform. DLL plugin can become unloadable on user's machine for reasons app developer does not control. In my production app Smart App Control blocked `audioplayers_windows_plugin.dll` by blue-fire team https://pub.dev/packages/audioplayers, added from their [git repo](https://github.com/bluefireteam/audioplayers) with latest bug-fixes, while the executable itself was allowed to run. I reported the file to Microsoft on Oct 4, 2026, and the analyst answered: > After review, one or more files from submission were confirmed to be incorrectly blocked by Smart App Control. This has now been remediated, and the file(s) will no longer be blocked So the block was a false positive, and it is fixed for this file and **can no longer be reproduced with it**. But until Microsoft reacted, the app did not work on affected machines and nothing in app code could change that. The same can happen again to any plugin DLL of any Flutter Windows app: Smart App Control, a WDAC policy, a missing or damaged file. The Flutter tool already had the same error code 4551 in #190232 (impellerc, a top 10 crasher in 3.44.8) and #191899 (dartaotruntime.exe, 16.9% of the top 10 crashes in 3.47.1). ### Why one plugin stops the app The generated Windows registrant runs each registration directly and checks nothing. `_cppPluginRegistryImplementationTemplate` in `packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/flutter_plugins.dart`: ```cpp void RegisterPlugins(flutter::PluginRegistry* registry) { {{#methodChannelPlugins}} {{class}}RegisterWithRegistrar( registry->GetRegistrarForPlugin("{{class}}")); {{/methodChannelPlugins}} } ``` `generated_plugins.cmake` links each plugin as a load-time import of the runner: ```cmake target_link_libraries(${BINARY_NAME} PRIVATE ${plugin}_plugin) ``` With this Windows does not start the process at all when it cannot load one of the plugin DLLs. I use delay-load for plugins DLL in runner so that the process at least can start, but same problem happens with default flutter app. Then the app crashed in `RegisterPlugins` before the first frame, at the call of the function that was not loaded. WinDbg on affected machine: ``` (2db0.2dac): Unknown exception - code c06d007e (first chance) (2db0.2dac): Unknown exception - code c06d007e (!!! second chance !!!) KERNELBASE!RaiseException+0x8a: 00007ff9`349141ca 0f1f440000 nop dword ptr [rax+rax] 0:000> g (2db0.2dac): Access violation - code c0000005 (first chance) First chance ex [truncated]

title: [iOS 26] EXC_BAD_ACCESS in OSThread::~OSThread / Log::~Log: OSThread::log_ always has exactly bit 40 set (byte +0x85 == 0x01), about 5 s after the app reconfigures the audio route
body:
Follow-up to #192369 (closed for lack of a repro), #190021 and #190023. I have no standalone repro yet, but the production data now has a deterministic signature that I think rules out random corruption and points at a single one-byte store. I am filing it so the data is in one place and to ask for help narrowing down the writer.

## Environment

- Flutter 3.47.5 (framework 6a19cca564), Dart 3.13.4 (dart-lang/sdk b530c21f7d), iOS release (AOT, PRODUCT) builds.
- iOS 26.6.1, 26.6.2 and 27.0. 58 events from 21 users since 2026-07-22. None on iOS 18.
- Devices: iPhone 12 to iPhone 16 class (iPhone13,2 / 14,x / 15,x / 16,1 / 17,x), iPad A16 (iPad15,7), iPad Air 3 (iPad11,3), iPad mini 6 (iPad14,6).
- Microphone capture with `record` 7.1.1 / `record_ios` 2.1.1 (AVAudioEngine input tap, `echoCancel: true`, so voice processing is enabled on the input node). AVAudioSession switches between `.playback` and `.playAndRecord` around each capture.

## Crash

Crashed thread (a Dart thread pool worker: named `DartWorker` in 4 of 31 events, unnamed like the other idle workers in the rest):

```
_pthread_start
_pthread_exit
_pthread_tsd_cleanup
dyld::ThreadLocalVariables::finalizeList
dart::OSThreadPtr::~OSThreadPtr
dart::OSThread::~OSThread          (os_thread.cc, delete log_)
dart::Log::~Log
dart::MallocGrowableArray<char>::~MallocGrowableArray
dart::BaseGrowableArray<char>::~BaseGrowableArray
EXC_BAD_ACCESS / KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS
```

There are no app frames, and the app was in the foreground in every event.

## The datum: bit 40, every time

In all 31 events with a fault address (30 of 30 in my first pass, 31 of 31 now), the fault address is a normal 16-byte-aligned heap pointer with bit 40 set:

| fault address | x20 (= log_) | x20 & ~(1<<40) | x19 (= this, OSThread) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0x10157953d10 | 0x10157953cf0 | 0x157953cf0 | 0x15b414a80 |
| 0x10119ac5640 | 0x10119ac5620 | 0x119ac5620 | 0x119808480 |
| 0x1012b343e90 | 0x1012b343e70 | 0x12b343e70 | 0x12c7f8a80 |
| 0x101392bccb0 | 0x101392bcc90 | 0x1392bcc90 | 0x1333f6b80 |

title: Investigate migrating basic plugins from CocoaPods to SwiftPM on the fly
body:
We should investigate if it's possible to migrate basic CocoaPod-only plugins to SwiftPM on the fly.

This would likely only work for plugins that meet the following criteria:
* No dependencies
* No modulemap
* No custom podspec settings 

See manual migration instructions: https://docs.flutter.dev/packages-and-plugins/swift-package-manager/for-plugin-authors

We'd also want a way to disable this as it could cause errors if migration is done incorrectly.

Expose iOS/macOS System Font variants (Rounded, Serif, Monospaced) natively to prevent ITMS-91182 App Store rejection
body:
### Use case

## Problem description:
Apple recently introduced a new App Store Connect validation rule: ITMS-91182: Disallowed font. Starting October 1, 2027, Apple will strictly reject app uploads that physically embed Apple-provided system fonts (such as SF Pro Rounded, SF Mono, New York, etc.) into the app bundle.

The warning message developers are currently receiving states:

"ITMS-91182: Disallowed font - The font named “SFProRounded-Bold” at “Runner.app/Frameworks/App.framework/flutter_assets/fonts/sf-pro-rounded-bold.otf” is an Apple-provided font. App uploads containing these embedded font files will be rejected starting October 1, 2027... Instead of embedding fonts, utilize standard system-provided APIs to reference and render Apple system fonts."

Currently, Flutter handles the default system font (standard sans-serif SF Pro) on iOS automatically. However, if a developer wants to use Apple's highly popular system font variants—like SF Pro Rounded or New York (serif)—the only way to do it in Flutter is to download the .otf files from Apple, bundle them in the assets/fonts folder, and declare them in pubspec.yaml.

This exact workflow is what triggers the ITMS-91182 warning and will soon cause hard rejections for Flutter apps on iOS.

## Alternative solutions considered:

Abandoning the fonts: Falling back to the default standard SF Pro sans-serif font to comply with Apple's guidelines, which ruins the intended UI/UX design (especially for apps relying heavily on rounded typography).

Native Platform Views: Using a UiKitView to render a native UILabel configured with UIFont.systemFont(ofSize: 16, weight: .bold, design: .rounded). This is highly impractical, terrible for performance, and impossible to integrate seamlessly within standard Flutter text spans and widgets.

## Is there a package on pub.dev?
No. Because Flutter uses its own text rendering engine (Impeller/Skia) which relies on assets defined in pubspec.yaml or byte data, a standard pub.dev package cannot cleanly hook into the low-level text layout engine to extract and render unbundled OS-level fonts.

### Proposal

I would like Flutter's engine to be updated to natively access OS-level system font variants (Rounded, Serif, Monospaced) using Apple's system-provided APIs, entirely removing the need to bundle .otf/.ttf files.

At the API level, I propose allowing developers to specify the system font design directly within a TextStyle. This could be implemented similarly to how CSS handles extended system fonts (ui-rounded, ui-serif, ui-monospace).

## Code Samples:

```Dart
Text(
  'Welcome to the app',
  style: TextStyle(
    fontSize: 24,
    // Option A: Special font family fallback strings recognized by the Flutter Engine
    fontFamily: 'SystemRounded', 
    
    // Option B: A dedicated new property (Similar to SwiftUI's .fontDesign)
    // fontDesign: FontDesign.rounded,
  ),
)
```

title: [Impeller] Vulkan: a LoadAction.load render pass clears the texture after an earlier LoadAction.clear pass into it
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a package with `flutter_gpu` and `vector_math` dependencies (pubspec below) and add the test file below as `test/load_action_test.dart`.
2. Run it on a Vulkan device: `flutter test --enable-impeller --enable-flutter-gpu test/load_action_test.dart`.

The first test renders two passes into one texture through Flutter GPU: a pass with `LoadAction.clear` (clear value red), then a pass with `LoadAction.load` (clear value green, no draws). The second test is a control: a single `LoadAction.load` pass into a texture filled with `Texture.overwrite`.

### Expected results

Both tests pass: a `LoadAction.load` pass keeps the texture's contents, so the texture stays red.

### Actual results

On Vulkan the first test fails at its second `expect`: the load pass clears the texture with its own (green) clear value.

```
00:00 +0 -1: a load pass after a clear pass keeps the cleared contents [E]
  Expected: [255, 0, 0, 255]
    Actual: [0, 255, 0, 255]
     Which: at location [0] is <0> instead of <255>
  test\load_action_test.dart 46:5                     main.<fn>
00:00 +0 -1: a first load pass into a texture keeps its contents
00:00 +1 -1: Some tests failed.
```

The control passes, so `LoadAction.load` works when the texture has had no earlier clearing pass. The result is the same on every run.

Cause, from the Impeller source (permalinks at current master `53d381d906`):

- `RenderPassVK::RenderPassVK` reads `TextureVK::GetCachedFrameData` and stores the pass and framebuffer back with `SetCachedFrameData`. The cache is per texture and keyed by sample count, mip level and slice only, not by the attachments' load or store actions: [render_pass_vk.cc#L177-L208](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/53d381d9067f16b1d4132f5b8f059a9cc5ddb9ec/engine/src/flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/vulkan/render_pass_vk.cc#L177-L208).
- `RenderPassVK::CreateVKRenderPass` returns the cached `VkRenderPass` whenever one exists, before `RenderPassBuilderVK` would apply the current `load_action` / `store_action`: [render_pass_vk.cc#L95-L101](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/53d381d9067f16b1d4132f5b8f059a9cc5ddb9ec/engine/src/flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/vulkan/render_pass_vk.cc#L95-L101).

So the second pass reuses the first pass's `VkRenderPass`, whose color attachment has `loadOp = CLEAR`, and the clear value of the second render target is applied. The same applies to store actions and to depth/stencil load and store actions.

On Metal the result is correct by construction: `RenderPassMTL` builds a fresh `MTLRenderPassDescriptor` from the render target for every pass, with `loadAction` taken from the attachment ([render_pass_mtl.mm#L65](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/53d381d9067f16b1d4132f5b8f059a9cc5ddb9ec/engine/src/flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/metal/render_pass_mtl.mm#L65), [#L148](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/53d381d9067f16b1d4132f5b8f059a9cc5ddb9ec/engine/src/flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/metal/rende

title: Interpolated stadium and rounded borders inset inner paths too far
body:
### Steps to reproduce

On flutter/flutter master `53d381d9067f16b1d4132f5b8f059a9cc5ddb9ec`, interpolate a stadium border into a rounded rectangle with a 10-pixel inside stroke and inspect its inner path.

### Expected results

The inner path is inset by 10 pixels for an inside stroke, 5 pixels for a centered stroke, and zero for an outside stroke. Intermediate shapes preserve the same stroke geometry as their endpoints.

### Actual results

The stadium-to-rounded-rectangle and rounded-shape-to-circle helpers use the stroke alignment (-1 to 1) directly as a linear-interpolation parameter. Their inner paths are inset by 20 pixels for an inside stroke and 10 pixels for a centered stroke, which clips an unnecessarily large region. The same root cause affects rounded rectangles and rounded superellipses interpolated with circles.

### Code sample

```dart
const side = BorderSide(width: 10.0);
final shape = ShapeBorder.lerp(
  const StadiumBorder(side: side),
  const RoundedRectangleBorder(side: side),
  0.5,
)!;
const rect = Rect.fromLTWH(0.0, 0.0, 100.0, 100.0);
// Expected Rect.fromLTRB(10, 10, 90, 90); actual Rect.fromLTRB(20, 20, 80, 80).
final bounds = shape.getInnerPath(rect).getBounds();
```

Not required for the deterministic path-geometry reproduction.

### Logs

Nine new regression cases cover three public shape interpolations and inside/center/outside alignment. The unchanged production code passes 3 cases and fails 6. Tests check both path bounds and inside/outside point containment across interpolation progress. A two-line fix reuses `side.strokeInset`; a draft PR with the regressions will follow.

Semantics: node nested in a scrollable keeps isHidden after its modal sheet settles (ExpansionTile headers missing for TalkBack on Android)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Put a `ListView` inside a modal bottom sheet, where each item is a semantics node nested inside another semantics node. A plain `ExpansionTile` on Android is enough, because its header sits inside the "Collapsed" live-region `Semantics` node (`accessibilityFocusBlockType: blockNode`).
2. Open the sheet.
3. After the sheet has finished opening, look at the semantics tree (or with TalkBack / UiAutomator connected before the sheet opened).

The code sample below is a self-contained widget test (`flutter test`) and needs no device.

### Expected results

Every item that is on screen once the sheet has settled has `SemanticsFlag.isHidden == false`.

### Actual results

The first several items keep `isHidden == true` even though they are fully on screen. With the sample (9 items on a 1080×2400 @ 2.625 view, `pumpAndSettle`'s 100 ms frames), 8 of the 9 are hidden.

On Android this makes the items disappear for assistive technology: `AccessibilityBridge.createAccessibilityNodeInfo` skips children flagged `IS_HIDDEN`, so TalkBack and UiAutomator only see the bare "Collapsed" wrapper of each `ExpansionTile` header. A *new* accessibility connection made after the sheet is open sees every item, because the framework then rebuilds the whole tree.

How many items stay hidden depends on frame timing. In widget tests it reproduces with frames of 20 ms or longer, which a debug build's first frames after pushing a route easily hit on a device. Neither `liveRegion` nor `blockNode` is required; any node-forming wrapper around a node-forming child reproduces it (see the first test). iOS `ExpansionTile` (no wrapper node) and a bare `ListTile` don't reproduce it.

#### Cause

Tracing `rendering/object.dart` (`_RenderObjectSemantics`):

1. On the sheet's first frame the list is below the screen edge, inside the viewport's cache extent. Its nodes get a non-empty rect from the viewport's semantics clip but an empty paint clip, so wrapper and child are both built with `hidden = true`.
2. On a later frame, a rebuild of the child (`Semantics.updateRenderObject` → `markNeedsSemanticsUpdate`) dirties parent data up to the boundary, so `updateChildren()` runs on the wrapper. Its `configProvider.reset()` discards the wrapper's effective config, including the `isHidden = true` written by the last build.
3. In the same frame the wrapper moves on screen. `_updateGeometry` computes `isSemanticsHidden = false` and compares it with `configProvider.effective.isHidden`, which the reset turned into `false`. It sees no visibility change, size is unchanged, so it returns early **without calling `_updateChildGeometry()`**.
4. The child's geometry is never recomputed. It is then rebuilt (`built == false` from step 2) with its geometry from step 1, so its `SemanticsNode` keeps `hidden = true`. Once the sheet stops moving nothing touches it again.

#### Possible fix

Also treat a change in the geometry's own `hidden` as a visibility change in `_updateGeometry`:

Android: a platform view is drawn at the wrong scale after the display size changes, because FlutterMutatorView keeps the density it was created with
body:
## Steps to reproduce

An Android platform view drawn through hybrid composition keeps the display density it was created
with, so it is drawn at the wrong scale after the display size changes while the app runs.

A reproduction is below: a `flutter create` app with one platform view and no dependencies. The
native view fills its own bounds and draws an inset border and both diagonals; Flutter lays it out in
a box of 240 x 120 logical pixels and draws a red frame of the same size on top of it, so the two
agree only while the view is drawn at the right scale.

1. `flutter run --release` on an Android device whose density is 420.
2. `adb shell wm density 520` while the app stays in the foreground.
3. Tap **Recreate the platform view**, which gives the platform view a new key.

## Expected results

The platform view follows the new display size, as the rest of the Flutter UI does.

## Actual results

After step 2 the native content is drawn too large and clipped to the bounds the Flutter side gives
it: the diagonals no longer meet the corners of the red frame, and the right and bottom sides of the
inset border are cut off. The Flutter content around it is laid out correctly — the red frame is
780 px wide, which is 240 logical pixels at the new ratio of 3.25.

Measured from screenshots, at the point where the rising diagonal meets the right edge of the frame:

| Density | Platform view | Native content drawn at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 420 | as created | 1.000x |
| 520 | the same one | **1.239x** |
| 520 | created again (step 3) | 1.000x |

520 / 420 = 1.238, which is the factor the analysis below predicts.

## Analysis

`FlutterMutatorView` stores the density once, in its constructor, and divides by it on every draw:

```java
// engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/embedding/engine/mutatorsstack/FlutterMutatorView.java
private float screenDensity;                                   // line 34 on main

public FlutterMutatorView(
    @NonNull Context context,
    float screenDensity,                                       // line 48 on main
    @Nullable AndroidTouchProcessor androidTouchProcessor) {
  super(context, null);
  this.screenDensity = screenDensity;                          // line 51 on main
  ...
}

private Matrix getPlatformViewMatrix() {
  Matrix finalMatrix = new Matrix(mutatorsStack.getFinalMatrix());
  // Reverse scale based on screen scale.
  finalMatrix.preScale(1 / screenDensity, 1 / screenDensity);  // line 162 on main
  ...
}
```

The field has no setter, and `screenDensity` appears nowhere else in the Android embedding. Both
places that create the view read the density at that moment and never revisit it:

```java
// PlatformViewsController.java and PlatformViewsController2.java
final FlutterMutatorView parentView =
    new FlutterMutatorView(
        context, context.getResources().getDisplayMetrics().density, androidTouchProcessor);
```

### Steps to reproduce

On flutter/flutter master c035b6f25c9dc7692b581539db9e6bccc3f67b72, clamp a system TextScaler with a minimum scale factor, leave the maximum at its default infinity, and scale a zero font size.

### Expected results

});
```

The regression fails with an assertion in dart:ui/math.dart clampDouble, called by _ClampedTextScaler.scale. This uses the system scaler rather than TextScaler.linear, which has a specialized clamp implementation. A focused fix and regression test will follow in a draft PR.

body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Create an app with `flutter create`, replace `lib/main.dart` with the code sample below, and add the following `<style>` block to the `<head>` of `web/index.html`. The CSS lets the page scroll, which is what makes iOS collapse the browser toolbar. Nothing else in the app changes.

   ```html
   <style>
     /* Let the page scroll, so iOS collapses its toolbar when you swipe.
        html overflow stops body's overflow: hidden from applying to the page. */
     html { overflow: auto; }
     body { touch-action: pan-y !important; }
     html::after { content: ""; display: block; height: 1000vh; }
   </style>
   ```

2. Build with `flutter build web` and open the app in Safari or Chrome on an iPhone.
3. Swipe up until the browser toolbar collapses, then stop.

Deployed repro: https://flutter-demo-71-before.web.app

### Expected results

The Flutter view grows to fill the area the toolbar gave up, as it does on Android and desktop.

### Actual results

The Flutter view keeps its toolbar-expanded height. The page behind it shows through as a white strip at the bottom of the screen.

| Browser, toolbar collapsed | Flutter view height | `window.innerHeight` | `visualViewport.height` | `documentElement.clientHeight` |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Safari, iOS 27 | 775 | 815 | 815 | 775 |
| Chrome, iOS 27 | 745 | 853 | 853 | 745 |

With the toolbar expanded, all four values match and there is no strip.

Note: in Chrome on iOS, swiping all the way to the end of the page can also shift the whole page up, revealing white below. That is a separate Chrome behavior with `position: fixed` content, it happens with the current engine too, and it is not this bug. Stop swiping once the toolbar collapses.

### Cause

On iOS, `FullPageDimensionsProvider.computePhysicalSize` in `lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/view_embedder/dimensions_provider/full_page_dimensions_provider.dart` sizes the view from `documentElement.clientHeight` instead of `visualViewport.height`. That branch was added in flutter/engine#25895 to fix #81430, where Chrome on iOS reported a wrong `visualViewport.height` after rotating.

When the toolbar collapses because the page scrolled, iOS grows `innerHeight` and `visualViewport.height` but leaves `documentElement.clientHeight` at the toolbar-expanded value, so the view never grows.

`computeKeyboardInsets` has the same iOS branch: it reports the keyboard inset as the view height minus `documentElement.clientHeight`. Growing only the view height turns the difference into a fake keyboard inset, 40px in Safari and 108px in Chrome, and `Scaffold` shrinks its body for a keyboard that is not there. Both functions need the same height.

Collapsing the toolbar from Safari's page menu with Hide Toolbar does not reproduce this, because that path also updates `documentElement.clientHeight`. A default Flutter app cannot scroll the page, so today the bug only shows once the page itself scrolls, which is what #69529 asks for. Any fix for #69529, suc

title: [Linux] Use-after-free of FlTaskRunner on app shutdown: timeout source outlives the task runner
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run a Flutter Linux desktop app that uses the `window_manager` plugin (observed with FluffyChat, Flathub Flatpak `im.fluffychat.Fluffychat`).
2. Use the app normally.
3. Close the main window.

The app crashes with SIGSEGV very often (not every time) during shutdown.

### Expected results

The app exits cleanly.

### Actual results

On exit the following is logged, followed by a segfault:
```
embedder.cc (2603): 'FlutterEngineRemoveView' returned 'kInvalidArguments'. Remove view info was invalid. The implicit view cannot be removed.
```

The crash happens on the main thread while `g_application_run()` is still iterating the main loop: a GLib timeout source fires and its callback in `libflutter_linux_gtk.so` casts its `user_data` to `FlTaskRunner`, but that object has already been finalized.

Note that `user_data` of the timeout source and `type_instance` in the failed cast are the same address (`0x55c78106db20`).

`fl_task_runner_tasks_did_change_locked()` schedules
`g_timeout_add(..., fl_task_runner_on_expired_timeout, self)` without holding a reference to `self`. If the `FlTaskRunner` is disposed/finalized during engine shutdown while this timeout is still pending, the source is not removed and `fl_task_runner_on_expired_timeout()` runs on freed memory (`FL_TASK_RUNNER(data)` → `g_type_check_instance_cast` → SIGSEGV).

Possible fixes: remove `timeout_source_id` in `fl_task_runner_dispose()`, or let the timeout source hold a strong or weak reference to the task runner.

Make google_maps_flutter_ios_sdk9 default iOS implementation for google_maps_flutter
body:
## Current

Currently we have three implementations of Google Maps for iOS

* [google_maps_flutter_ios](https://github.com/flutter/packages/tree/main/packages/google_maps_flutter/google_maps_flutter_ios) - Only supports CocoaPods
  * Cannot be converted to SwiftPM because SwiftPM does not resolve dependencies with the minimum deployment target. It resolves to the latest. If your package has a dependency that has the possibility of resolving to a version that requires a higher iOS version than your package does, your package also can only support the higher version. Basically would force our package and therefore everyone to iOS 16+. And would continue to increase every time we added a new Maps SDK version.
* [google_maps_flutter_ios_sdk9](https://github.com/flutter/packages/tree/main/packages/google_maps_flutter/google_maps_flutter_ios_sdk9) - supports SwiftPM, requires iOS 15
* [google_maps_flutter_ios_sdk10](https://github.com/flutter/packages/tree/main/packages/google_maps_flutter/google_maps_flutter_ios_sdk10) - supports SwiftPM, requires iOS 16

google_maps_flutter_ios is currently the [default implementation package](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/7368361bb18a852e1401a241395cbaa3c8a427dd/packages/google_maps_flutter/google_maps_flutter/pubspec.yaml#L17) for google_maps_flutter.

Flutter CLI warns the package doesn’t support SwiftPM and people file issues. @stuartmorgan-g has been closing and instructing to see the [README](https://github.com/flutter/packages/blob/main/packages/google_maps_flutter/google_maps_flutter/README.md#platform-setup) to pin an SDK package.

## Proposal

* Freeze google_maps_flutter_ios - it will no longer receive updates since we now support iOS 15+ and people should migrate to SwiftPM
* Make google_maps_flutter_sdk9 the default

Side effect: CocoaPods users who were resolving to sdk10 will suddenly be on sdk9 instead. 

There were some changes between the two SDKS:
 * Compass button size/style change
 * Dark mode made automatic
 * See https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/ios-sdk/release-notes#May_19_2025

[WebParagraph] Line metrics diverge from SkParagraph: kTextHeightNone, leadingDistribution default, StrutStyle, TextHeightBehavior, placeholders
body:
WebParagraph's line metrics diverge from SkParagraph (CanvasKit / Skwasm) in several independent ways. All of them are visible through `Paragraph.height`, `Paragraph.alphabeticBaseline`, `computeLineMetrics()`, `getBoxesForRange()` and `getBoxesForPlaceholders()`; the reference behavior is `Run::calculateMetrics`, `InternalLineMetrics`, `TextWrapper::breakTextIntoLines`, `ParagraphImpl::computeEmptyMetrics` and `TextLine::getRectsForRange` in `modules/skparagraph`.

### 1. `kTextHeightNone` is treated as a height multiplier of `0.0`

- `ChildStyleNode._height` maps `TextStyle(height: kTextHeightNone)` to `null` and then falls back to the parent's height, so a child span cannot opt out of a `ParagraphStyle(height: 3.0)`.
- `LineBlock` and the empty-paragraph branch of `TextLayout.wrapText` only check `height != null`, so `ParagraphStyle(height: kTextHeightNone)` multiplies the line metrics by `0.0`.

Expected: `kTextHeightNone` disables the multiplier and the line is laid out at the font's own ascent + descent.

### 2. The default `TextLeadingDistribution` is `even`, and `TextHeightBehavior.leadingDistribution` is ignored

- `LineBlock` treats `leadingDistribution == null` as `even` (half-leading). SkParagraph's default is `proportional` (`fHalfLeading == false`), i.e. ascent and descent are scaled by the same factor. The total line height is the same, but the baseline position differs for every paragraph that sets `height` without an explicit `leadingDistribution`.
- `WebParagraphStyle` doesn't pass `textHeightBehavior.leadingDistribution` to its root text style and `RootStyleNode._leadingDistribution` always returns `null`, so `TextHeightBehavior(leadingDistribution: even)` has no effect.

### 3. `StrutStyle` does not affect line metrics

- `StrutStyle` has no effect on line metrics: `WebStrutStyle.calculateMetrics` computes `strutAscent` / `strutDescent` / `strutLeading`, but their only consumer is `getBoxesForRange(boxHeightStyle: BoxHeightStyle.strut)`. `TextLine` starts from `0` / `0` and only accumulates block metrics, so a strut never sets a minimum line height, `forceStrutHeight` is a no-op (for text and placeholders alike) and `leading` is lost. E.g. `StrutStyle(fontFamily: 'Arial', fontSize: 20, height: 1.0, leading: 1.5, forceStrutHeight: true)` + `'Hello'` should give a 50px line (20 + 30 of leading); WebParagraph gives the font's natural height.
- `WebStrutStyle.calculateMetrics` also bails out when `fontSize` is `null` (SkParagraph falls back to the default font size, 14), ignores the paragraph's `TextHeightBehavior.leadingDistribution` as a fallback (`dart:ui` resolves `strutStyle.leadingDistribution ?? textHeightBehavior.leadingDistribution`), and accepts a negative `leading`.
- An empty paragraph ignores `height`, `StrutStyle` and `TextHeightBehavior` entirely: `paragraph.height` is just the height of the empty cluster, and both baselines are set to that height.

### 4. `TextHeightBehavior.applyHeightToFirstAscent` / `applyHeight
