title: [web_paragraph] TextWrapper.breakLines misdetects a trailing newline (hardLineBreak is read from the wrong cluster)
body:
### Where

WebParagraph (the experimental web text layout engine), [`TextWrapper.breakLines`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/web_paragraph/wrapper.dart) in `engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/web_paragraph/wrapper.dart`.

### What happens

After the main loop `hardLineBreak` is used as "the text ends with a line feed" to decide whether to append the synthetic empty last line (the one Flutter expects after a trailing `\n`):

```dart
    var hardLineBreak = false;
    for (var index = 0; index < _layout.allClusters.length - 1; index += 1) {
      final WebCluster cluster = _layout.allClusters[index];
      hardLineBreak = _isHardLineBreak(cluster);
      ...
    }
    ...
    if (hardLineBreak) {
      // Flutter wants to have another (empty) line if \n is the last codepoint in the text
      line._top += _layout.addLine(emptyClusterRange, emptyClusterRange, false, line._top);
    }
```

But the variable holds the flag of the **last visited cluster**, which means "there is a mandatory break *before* this cluster". The segmenter puts the `hardLineBreak` flag on the position *after* the `\n`, and the loop stops at `allClusters.length - 1`, so the last position (`text.length`, the empty cluster) is never visited. The two meanings only coincide by accident.

Observed line counts (`computeLineMetrics().length`):

| text | expected (SkParagraph) | actual |
|---|---|---|
| `'x\n'` | 2 | **1** |
| `'\n'` | 2 | **1** |
| `'x\ny'`, `'a\nb'`, `'abc\nd'` | 2 | **3** (the last text line is also marked as `hardBreak`) |
| `'xx\nyy'`, `'abc\nde'` | 2 | 2 (by accident: the last visited cluster has no flag) |
| `'x\n\n'`, `'\n\n\n'` | 3, 4 | correct by accident |
| `'a\nb\nc\n'` with `maxLines: 2` | 2 | **3** (the synthetic line is added although `maxLines` is reached; SkParagraph resets `fHardLineBreak` on the last line, `TextWrapper.cpp` ~L420) |

### Expected

Same as SkParagraph / CanvasKit: exactly one extra empty line iff the text ends with `\n`, never beyond `maxLines`, and `LineMetrics.hardBreak` only on lines that actually end with a hard break.

### Proposed fix

After the loop take the flag from the last (empty) cluster — "there is a mandatory break before the end of the text" is exactly "the text ends with a line feed":

```dart
    hardLineBreak = _isHardLineBreak(_layout.allClusters.last);
    ...
    if (hardLineBreak && !line.reachedMaxLines()) {
```

Verified locally: with this change all tests in `test/webparagraph/` pass and every string above produces the expected number of lines.

### Why it matters

- `TextHeightBehavior.applyHeightToLastDescent` must apply to the empty line after a trailing `\n` (as in SkParagraph); the test `TextHeightBehavior treats the empty line after a trailing newline as the last line` added in #193403 is skipped until this is fixed.

title: [web][Firefox] Platform view content never composites on first construction (fixed by a widget rebuild)
body:
## Summary

On Flutter Web (CanvasKit renderer), a platform view whose native content lives
inside a library's own Shadow DOM — projected into Flutter's platform-view `<slot>`
via the standard mechanism — renders a fully correct, non-zero-sized, visible DOM/CSS
tree in **Firefox**, but the content is never actually painted to the screen. The
screen shows only the app's background color. **Chrome and Edge never reproduce this,
every time, with the identical build.** A manual browser-level layout change (resizing
the window) reliably reveals the correctly-rendered content afterward, which is the
strongest clue that this is a compositing-step bug, not a DOM/CSS/application-logic bug.

This matches the bug category described in #105485 and #193223, but neither of those
threads has a confirmed fix or workaround that applies here (both are CanvasKit;
`--wasm`/skwasm was checked and documented as reproducing the same category in
#193223, and `--web-renderer` no longer exists as a build flag to test the old HTML
renderer as an A/B).

- Flutter 3.41.1 • channel stable
- Framework revision `582a0e7c55`
- Engine revision `3452d735bd` (hash `cc8e596aa65130a0678cc59613ed1c5125184db4`)
- Dart 3.11.0
- Renderer: CanvasKit (default; `--wasm`/skwasm not usable as an A/B since
  `--web-renderer` has been removed as a flag in this Flutter version)

  fixed a *different*, now-resolved worker-serialization error that existed under

- OS: Windows 11 (dev machine); bug reproduces for the end user on their own Windows

title: Add a namespace to PageStorageBucket readState and writeState
body:
### Use case

`PageStorageBucket` picks the slot for `readState` and `writeState` from the `PageStorageKey`s above the context. Two different widgets under the same keys end up in the same slot and overwrite each other. For example an `Expansible` saves a `bool` and a `Scrollable` in its body saves a `double`, which caused the crashes in #192184.

#192195 works around this in `Expansible` by building its own identifier from the same keys and passing it as `identifier`. That repeats the key lookup in `PageStorageBucket._allKeys`, and any other widget that needs its own slot would have to do the same.

### Proposal

Add a namespace to `PageStorageBucket`, for example `readState(context, {identifier, namespace})` and `writeState(context, data, {identifier, namespace})`, so a widget can keep its state apart from other widgets under the same `PageStorageKey`s without computing the keys itself. `Expansible` can then drop its own identifier.

title: [web] SkwasmRenderer.renderScene drops FrameTimingRecorder on queue
body:
### Summary

In multi-threaded `skwasm` and `wimp`, when `DedicatedWorker` rasterization (`_surface_renderPicturesOnWorker`) spans more than one UI frame, `SkwasmRenderer.renderScene` (`engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/renderer.dart:423-430`) queues the incoming scene in `renderQueue.next` before running `Frame.raster`. This causes two defects:

1. **Silent `FrameTimingRecorder` Drop When `renderQueue.next` Is Overwritten**:
   When a new scene arrives while `renderQueue.current != null` and `renderQueue.next != null`, `SkwasmRenderer.renderScene` (`renderer.dart:426`) calls `renderQueue.next?.completer.complete()` and overwrites `renderQueue.next` without recording raster timestamps or reporting timings for the replaced frame's `FrameTimingRecorder`.

2. **Premature `SkwasmPicture` Disposal Before Deferred `Frame.raster` Execution**:
   When `renderQueue.current == null`, `_kickRenderLoop` runs `ViewRasterizer.draw` -> `compositorFrame.raster(layerTree, currentFrameSize, recorder)` (`engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/layer/layer_tree.dart:83-94`) synchronously before `await viewEmbedder.submitFrame(recorder)`.
   However, when `renderQueue.current != null`, `renderQueue.next` holds the raw `LayerScene` without running `Frame.raster` (`preroll` -> `measure` -> `paint`). If a subsequent UI frame runs `flushPaint()` / `compositeFrame()` on the main thread before `_kickRenderLoop` pops `renderQueue.next`:
   - `PictureLayer.picture = newPicture` (`packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/layer.dart:844-849`) calls `_picture?.dispose()` on the previous frame's `SkwasmPicture` handles.
   - `Layer.engineLayer = ...` (`packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/layer.dart:449-454`) calls `_engineLayer?.dispose()` (`ContainerLayer.dispose()` in `engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/layer/layer.dart:45-54`), disposing direct `PictureLayer` children of the queued scene's `OffsetEngineLayer`s.
   - When `_kickRenderLoop` subsequently pops `renderQueue.next`, `PrerollVisitor.visitPicture` (`engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/layer/layer_visitor.dart:177-184`) sees `picture.picture.isDisposed == true` and culls the disposed pictures (`picture.paintBounds = ui.Rect.zero; picture.isCulled = true`). If all pictures are culled, `rootLayer.needsPainting` is `false`, `PlatformViewEmbedder._updateDomForNewComposition` (`embedder.dart:482-498`) releases the active `<canvas>` overlay, and `submitFrame` dispatches `surfaceRenderPictures(handle, pictureHandles, 0)` (`picture_count == 0`).

### Summary

In https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/190048 (fixing https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/190039) and https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/191014, `skwasm` enabled `SK_ENABLE_THREADLOCAL_STRIKECACHE` because multithreaded `skwasm` and `wimp` are compiled with `-sWASM_WORKERS=1` (`engine/src/build/config/compiler/BUILD.gn:312`) without `-pthread`, which links single-threaded Emscripten system libraries where POSIX synchronization primitives (`sem_wait`, `pthread_cond_wait`) are no-op stubs.

Making `SkStrikeCache` thread-local did not eliminate shared mutable state between main-thread `$paragraph_layout` and `DedicatedWorker` `_surface_renderPicturesOnWorker`:

title: Mac framework_tests_impeller is too big and flaky
body:
The `Mac framework_tests_impeller` LUCI shard is flaky.

Currently in `dev/bots/suite_runners/run_framework_tests.dart`, `runImpeller` executes the entire `packages/flutter` test suite in a single monolithic invocation:
```dart
Future<void> runImpeller() async {
  printProgress('${green}Running packages/flutter tests $reset in Impeller$reset');
  await runFlutterTest(
    path.join(flutterRoot, 'packages', 'flutter'),
    options: <String>['--enable-impeller'],
  );
}
```
This runs a lot of stuff in one shard. 20,000 tests or so. If one test fails, retrying the shard re-runs all of these, which feels wasteful.

I looked at the last 500 try runs of `Mac framework_tests_impeller`. I noticed that failures spike during peak CI load windows (US midday and evening batch merges), whereas the post-merge builder (`flutter/prod/Mac framework_tests_impeller`) maintains a 100% pass rate over the last 100 runs.

#### Hourly Distribution of Try Failures (Pacific Time)
```text
Hour (Pacific)   | Total Builds | Failures | Failure Rate
-------------------------------------------------------
00:00 - 07:00    |          107 |        4 |         3.7%  ####
08:00 - 11:00    |          155 |        2 |         1.3%  ##
12:00 - 15:00    |          121 |        8 |         6.6%  ########  (Peak US midday)
16:00 - 21:00    |           88 |        3 |         3.4%  ###
22:00 - 23:00    |           27 |        4 |        14.8%  ####      (Late batch merges)
```

From those 500 try runs, failures were found in only four test files. I think these could use some attention, or be split out into their own shard or something.

Here's a report from AI on them:

| Failing Test Suite | Failures | Failure Mode |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `packages/flutter/test/widgets/draggable_scrollable_sheet_test.dart` | **10** | Physics fling/drag animation timing |
| `packages/flutter/test/material/progress_indicator_test.dart` | **4** | Continuous spinning indicator timeout (`did not complete [E]`) |
| `packages/flutter/test/widgets/editable_text_cursor_test.dart` | **2** | Cursor blink animation timing |
| `packages/flutter/test/widgets/transform_test.dart` | **2** | 3D perspective anti-aliasing mismatch |

### Root Causes per Failing Suite
1. **Decoupled Host Clocks (`progress_indicator_test.dart`)**: Progress indicators run infinite `AnimationController.repeat()` loops. Under runner CPU throttling, asynchronous microtasks and timer ticks fall behind real wall-clock time, causing tests to exceed timeouts (`- did not complete [E]`).
2. **Unbounded Fling Decay (`draggable_scrollable_sheet_test.dart`)**: Ballistic fling simulations (`tester.fling`) followed by unbounded `tester.pumpAndSettle()` generate long micro-step settling tails that hit timeouts or fail precision thresholds (`closeTo(.5, precisionErrorTolerance)`) under thread starvation.
3. **Cursor Blink Thresholds (`editable_text_cursor_test.dart`)**: 500ms blink timer periods oscillate close to pump thresholds under CPU throttling.

title: [Android] Update embedding to explicitly support disabling HCPP
body: Currently, the source of truth for engine configuration flags for Flutter Android, [FlutterEngineFlags.java](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/e47fb53953f43e21e914ecc26f9e922fea88d8bb/engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/android/io/flutter/embedding/engine/FlutterEngineFlags.java), does not list the disable option for HCPP. Specifically, it does not support the version of the [`--enable-hcpp-and-surface-control`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/e47fb53953f43e21e914ecc26f9e922fea88d8bb/engine/src/flutter/shell/common/switch_defs.h#L284) flag that takes a boolean value. Thus, the embedding (and the tool as needed) should be updated to do so to (1) allow for the potential of HCPP being enabled by default and (2) enable the rejection of flags that the embedding does not recognize: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/182557

title: [web][Android] View keeps a keyboard-reduced height and reports negative viewInsets after focus moves from an iframe input to a TextField
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a web app from the code sample below (`flutter create`, then `flutter pub add web`). It has a text input inside an iframe (`HtmlElementView`) and a Flutter `TextField`. To see where the Flutter view ends, give the page a background in `web/index.html`, for example `<body style="background:#c62828">`.
2. `flutter build web --release`, serve `build/web`, and open it in Chrome on Android.
3. Tap the iframe input. The numeric keypad opens.
4. Tap the Flutter `TextField`. The keyboard switches to the text keyboard.
5. Close the keyboard with the system Back button or gesture. The `TextField` keeps focus.

The order `TextField` → iframe input → `TextField` → Back gives the same result, which is the usual order on a form that mixes Flutter fields with an embedded payment field.

### Expected results

After the keyboard closes, the Flutter view fills the viewport again and `viewInsets.bottom` is 0.

### Actual results

The Flutter view stays at the height it had while the keyboard was open for the iframe input, and `viewInsets.bottom` is negative. The page background shows below the view.

Measured on the page with the sample (CSS pixels; `<flutter-view>` is its `getBoundingClientRect().height`, the last two columns are what the framework sees through `MediaQueryData.fromView`):

| Step | `visualViewport.height` | `<flutter-view>` height | view size | `viewInsets.bottom` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Start | 692.3 | 692.3 | 384x692 | 0 |
| 3. iframe input focused | 317.9 | 317.9 | 384x318 | 0 |
| 4. `TextField` focused | 381.9 | 317.9 | 384x318 | -64 |
| 5. Keyboard closed | 692.3 | **317.9** | **384x318** | **-374** |

The view stays at 318 after tapping outside the field, and recovers the next time the keyboard opens for a Flutter text field.

Same result with stable 3.47.5 and with master at 4e5a09292c.

Not triggered by:

- Flutter fields only (`TextField` → Back): the view stays at 692.
- The iframe input only (iframe input → Back): the view follows the viewport, 318 and back to 692.

#### Cause

`_handleBrowserResize` keeps `_physicalSize` unchanged and reports the difference as `viewInsets` while `isMobile && textEditing.isEditing`. That relies on the preserved size being the full, keyboard-less size, the expectation #179581 describes:

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/4e5a09292c1c64a38d604c7ec096537f50d69f93/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/window.dart#L334

https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/4e5a09292c1c64a38d604c7ec096537f50d69f93/engine/src/flutter/lib/web_ui/lib/src/engine/window.dart#L352-L366

That assumption does not hold when the keyboard is already open at the moment editing starts:

- Step 3: the iframe input has focus, so Flutter's text editing is not active. The resize caused by the keyboard is handled as a real resize and `_physicalSize` becomes the keyboard-reduced size (318).
- Step 4: the `TextField` gets focus and `isEditing` becomes true. From here `_physicalSize` i

title: Cold Material route resolve allocations on Adreno 750: Impeller/Vulkan investigation
body:
Expected behavior: the normal Material route should avoid long synchronous allocation work that stalls rasterization. The independent sample has modest missed-frame costs and establishes the target mechanism; the severe private-app tail is not reproduced by it.

Test scope: physical Android, profile mode, stock Flutter 3.41.3 and stable 3.47.5. Master-channel testing and a public severe-tail reproducer are not available. No claim is made that latest stable has the severe private-app failure or fixes it.

**Public source/evidence snapshot.** Tested on 2026-10-01. The independent public sample reproduces the offscreen-target mechanism on Flutter 3.41.3 and latest stable 3.47.5. It has **not** reproduced the severe latency tail observed in a larger private application.

## Request

Help identify why synchronous `vkAllocateMemory` for two stable offscreen resolve images varies from a few milliseconds to more than 100 ms on this device. Which diagnostic would distinguish Impeller/VMA allocation policy from driver CPU work? We seek a maintainable fix that preserves normal `MaterialPageRoute` behavior. The pool and optional dedicated-node experiments below did not establish such a fix.

In `reproducer/`, run `flutter pub get`, then `flutter run --profile` on Android with Impeller enabled. Tap **Open details**, go Back, reopen. The sample is independently written, deterministic local reading-workshop content with SDK fonts/icons. It uses normal programmatic `MaterialPageRoute` and a destination `RepaintBoundary`. It has no network/data loading, manual opacity or saveLayer, custom transition, hidden destination, resource warming or readiness gate. `README.md` describes instrumentation and optional descriptor tracing; `REPRODUCTION_RESULT.md` contains all 12 valid physical trials and limitations.

This is a mechanism reproducer, **not a guaranteed severe-stall reproducer**. Its simpler startup and resource history may matter.

title: Table: baseline-aligned cells ignore rowSpan
body:
Follow-up to #177102 (`colSpan` / `rowSpan` support in `TableCell`), tracking the `TODO(hm21)` in the baseline case of `RenderTable.performLayout`. Agreed as a follow-up in the review: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/177102#discussion_r4147241248

### Steps to reproduce

1. Check out the branch of #177102.
2. Build a baseline-aligned `Table` in which a `TableCell(rowSpan: 2)` is taller than the row it starts in (code sample below).
3. Compare the row heights.

### Expected results

A spanning cell is sized like the other alignments: it does not add its height to the row it starts in, and the rows it covers only grow if the cell needs more room than they provide. For baseline alignment, close to HTML's `vertical-align: baseline` on a `rowspan` cell, that means:

- the cell aligns its baseline with the baseline of the first row, so only its ascent counts toward that row's `beforeBaselineDistance`;
- its descent is not added to the first row. Once the first row's baseline is known, the height the cell needs from the top of that row is recorded for the last row it covers, the same way `top`, `middle` and `bottom` rowSpan cells are handled.

In the sample, row 0 is 50 tall (ascent 45 of `T`, descent 5 of `A`) and row 1 is 20 tall. `T` reaches from 0 to 60, into row 1. The table is 70 tall.

### Actual results

The baseline case never looks at `rowSpan`, so the whole height of the cell goes into the row it starts in:

```
row0=60.0 row1=20.0 table=80.0
T=Rect.fromLTRB(0.0, 0.0, 100.0, 60.0)
A=Rect.fromLTRB(100.0, 30.0, 200.0, 50.0)
```

The same applies to a baseline-aligned cell without a real baseline (it is top-aligned, but its height also goes into its first row).

title: [web] Fix --web-content-hash breaking cache when --source-maps is used
body:
When building a Flutter web app with both `--web-content-hash` and `--source-maps` (e.g., `flutter build web --wasm --web-content-hash --source-maps` or `flutter build web --web-content-hash --source-maps`), `build/web/precache_manifest.json` records `"urlHashed": false` and a mismatched `"hash"` for `main.dart.<hash>.js`:

```json
{
  "url": "main.dart.216ed961.js",
  "hash": "fca793b5",
  "size": 6079674,
  "urlHashed": false
}
```

### Root Cause

1. In [`_hashAndRenameWebOutput`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/build_system/targets/web.dart), `flutter_tools` computes `contentHash` (`216ed961`) from the initial `main.dart.js` bytes (when its trailing comment is still `//# sourceMappingURL=main.dart.js.map`), derives `newBasename = 'main.dart.216ed961.js'`, and **then** rewrites the trailing `sourceMappingURL` directive inside `main.dart.js` in-place to `//# sourceMappingURL=main.dart.216ed961.js.map` before renaming the file on disk ( additionally stripping any trailing newline due to `\s*$` matching `\n` before EOF).
2. Later, during `WebReleaseBundle.build`, [`updatePrecacheManifest`](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/web/content_hash.dart) hashes the final `build/web/main.dart.216ed961.js` bytes on disk—which now contain the rewritten `sourceMappingURL` comment—producing a different hash (`fca793b5`).
3. Because `'main.dart.216ed961.js'.contains('.fca793b5.')` is `false`, `updatePrecacheManifest` sets `"urlHashed": false` and `"hash": "fca793b5"`, breaking cache validation and precache manifest consumers that rely on `urlHashed: true` and filename/content hash parity.

### Other Affected Files

- **`main.dart.<hash>.js`** (`Dart2JSTarget` and the JS fallback in `--wasm` builds): **Affected** when `--source-maps` is passed.
- **`main.dart.<hash>.mjs.map`** (`Dart2WasmTarget`): If a `.mjs.map` file is present alongside `main.dart.mjs`, `Dart2WasmTarget` previously derived `jsSupportMapName = '$jsSupportName.map'`.
- **`flutter_service_worker.js` / `worker.<hash>.js`**: Uses `_hashAndRenameWebOutput` with `sourceMapFile` if present.
- **`main.dart.<hash>.wasm`**: **Not affected** (`_hashAndRenameWebOutput` skips `sourceMappingURL` rewriting when `isWasm` is `true` because `.wasm` embeds `main.dart.wasm.map` in a binary custom section).

### Proposed Fix (Hash Inversion)

In `_hashAndRenameWebOutput` (`packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/build_system/targets/web.dart`):
1. Hash `sourceMapFile` **first** (`mapHash`) and rename it via `computeHashedBasename(oldMapBasename, mapHash, file.fileSystem)` (producing `main.dart.<mapHash>.js.map`, `main.dart.<mapHash>.mjs.map`, `worker.<mapHash>.js.map`).
2. Rewrite `//# sourceMappingURL=<newMapBasename>` in `file` (using positive lookahead `(?=\s*$)` so trailing newlines are preserved).
3. Compute `contentHash` from the **final** bytes of `file` and rename `file` to `main.dart.<contentHash>.js` so its filename hash matc

title: [Windows][Skia] OpenGL resource context remains current after engine shutdown
body:
### Steps to reproduce

This is reproducible in the engine's native embedder tests, without an app or plugin.

1. Check out flutter/flutter at 3829a944235cd8e25142d72302dc89db4cd16934 and sync engine dependencies.
2. Add the regression test included below to engine/src/flutter/shell/platform/embedder/tests/embedder_gl_unittests.cc. Leave the production implementation unchanged.
3. From engine/src, configure and build:

```console
python flutter/tools/gn --unoptimized --no-lto
ninja -C out/host_debug_unopt embedder_unittests
out/host_debug_unopt/embedder_unittests.exe --gtest_filter=EmbedderTest.ShutdownReleasesOpenGLResourceContextOnItsThread
```

### Expected results

After synchronous engine shutdown, the resource context has been cleared on the I/O thread that made it current.

### Actual results

The test-only baseline fails at both post-shutdown assertions:

```text
context.resource_released: Actual false, Expected true
context.resource_current:  Actual true,  Expected false
1 FAILED TEST
EXIT=1
```

Applying the Skia release hook makes the same test pass. Validation:

Windows x64, `host_debug_unopt` (`--unoptimized --no-lto`), source `3829a944235cd8e25142d72302dc89db4cd16934`:

- New regression with unchanged production code: failed both expected release assertions (exit 1).
- With the two Skia production changes: the same regression passed (exit 0).
- Full `embedder_unittests`: 180 passed, 8 skipped, 1 pre-existing disabled test; no failures (exit 0).
- Shutdown regression repeated 100 times: all passed (exit 0).
- Changed-line clang-format and `git diff --check`: passed.

The eight skips are five AOT-only checks in this JIT build and three golden checks restricted to Linux. No test was disabled or skip condition changed by this patch. Other platforms remain for upstream CI.


### Cause and proposed fix

Shell teardown already calls PlatformViewEmbedder::ReleaseResourceContext on the I/O thread after releasing the last IO manager. PlatformViewEmbedder forwards this to the surface. EmbedderSurfaceGLSkia does not override the default no-op, so its resource context remains current. EGL can defer destruction while the context remains current on a thread.

Implement the existing release hook in EmbedderSurfaceGLSkia and clear the current context through the existing embedder callback. GLES Impeller already implements analogous cleanup; this report does not claim a new Impeller fix.

The EGL reference specifies that context destruction is deferred until the context is no longer current to any thread: https://registry.khronos.org/EGL/sdk/docs/man/html/eglDestroyContext.xhtml

Related prior investigation: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/138893#issuecomment-1852109576 identified the same EGL thread-binding mechanism on December 12, 2023. The reporter closed the issue on July 18, 2024, and it was locked on August 1, 2024; no fixing PR is linked there. This focused issue provides a standalon
[truncated]

title: [macOS] Accessibility bridge keeps freed AXNodes after a failed AXTree update and crashes on the next AX query
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Release-mode macOS app (engine revision `0cd610717b`, Flutter 3.44.8 stable, framework `058e0af2c2`), accessibility in use (VoiceOver, an AX client such as a screen recorder or a password manager, or just AppKit's own tracking-area collection on a mouse move). The framework commits a semantics update in which a parent claims a child that has MOVED without sending that child in the same update, the OverlayPortal traversal graft shape described in #182444. Two commits later the app crashes on the main thread in the next accessibility query.

A deterministic unit reproduction on the stock engine at this pin, release config, in `accessibility_bridge_unittests.cc`: build the tree `0 > [1 > 3 > 4], 2, 5 > 6`, then send ONE commit with `1` without child `3`, `2` claiming `3`, and `5` without child `6` (nodes `3` and `4` not sent). Then walk every delegate's children.

### Expected results

Either the update is rejected atomically (the tree and the bridge stay at the previous consistent state) or it is applied consistently (delegates and cached child counts match the tree). Later commits keep applying.

### Actual results

1. `AccessibilityBridge::CommitUpdates` first removes the child from its old parent, then applies a second update that passes `AXTree::ComputePendingChanges` but fails in `ValidatePendingChangesComplete` ("Nodes left pending by the update: 3"), AFTER `UpdateNode` has already run `DeleteOldChildren` (nodes freed) and created new nodes.
2. `AXTree::Unserialize` returns false before the observer notifications and before the unignored-child cache refresh. The bridge therefore keeps delegates whose `ax_node_` is freed, has no delegate for the new nodes, and leaves parents whose cached unignored child count exceeds their real children.
3. `CommitUpdates` gates on the sticky `AXTree::error()` string (never cleared) instead of the return value, and its first-update error path is an `assert(false)` that release builds compile out and that returns without clearing the pending updates. Every later commit is refused, so the bridge never recovers.
4. The next AppKit query dereferences the stale state. Two field signatures from a shipping app, symbolized against the release FlutterMacOS:
   - a mouse-moved tracking-area update: `-[FlutterTextField frame]` (FlutterTextInputSemanticsObject.mm:97) into `FlutterTextPlatformNode::GetFrame` (:186) into `AXTree::RelativeToTreeBounds` on a freed `AXNode`.
   - an out-of-process AX query (`NSAccessibilityChildren`): `-[AXPlatformNodeCocoa AXChildrenInternal]` (ax_platform_node_mac.mm:651) into `FlutterPlatformNodeDelegate::ChildAtIndex` (flutter_platform_node_delegate.cc:90), fault address `0x48` (`AXNodeData::id` read through a null child): `GetChildCount()` returned the stale cached count and `GetUnignoredChildAtIndex(index)` returned `nullptr`.

In the unit cell: the bridge logs `Failed to update ui::AXTree, error: Nodes left pending by the update: 3`, the delegate for `6` outlives
[truncated]

title: Bundled native assets are not resolved from the bundle on embedder-API platforms: "relative" resolves against a debug label
Tooltip (OverlayPortal) of a list item parked in the keep-alive bucket is never laid out but still hit-tested, freezing mouse input
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. A lazily built list (`ListView.builder`, default `addAutomaticKeepAlives: true`) whose items contain a `Tooltip` around an `IconButton`, with no relayout boundary between the item root and the `Tooltip` (a loose-height `Column`/`Row`, as in most cards).
2. The mouse enters an item's `IconButton`: the `InkWell` hover highlight makes the item request keep-alive, and the `Tooltip` shows its overlay (a new `_RenderDeferredLayoutBox` is added to the root `_RenderTheater`).
3. In the same frame, the list scrolls so that this item ends up past the trailing cache extent (for example a fast wheel or trackpad flick upwards).
4. Move the mouse.

Two deterministic repros below: a widget test (fails on 3.47.3 and 3.49.0-0.1.pre), and a small web app plus a DevTools console snippet that freezes a release build in Chrome.

### Expected results

The tooltip overlay is either laid out, or not hit-tested/painted while its anchor is parked. Pointer input keeps working.

### Actual results

`RenderSliverList.performLayout` collects the item as trailing garbage without laying it out, and `_destroyOrCacheChild` parks it in the keep-alive bucket, still attached. The new `_RenderDeferredLayoutBox` is only laid out through its layout surrogate (inside the parked item, which is never laid out again) or during the theater's own layout (which `_addDeferredChild` does not dirty), so it never gets a size. `_RenderTheaterMixin.hitTestChildren` still hit-tests it:

- debug: `Cannot hit test a render box that has never been laid out.` With semantics enabled, the semantics flush asserts first: `'!childSemantics.renderObject._needsLayout': is not true.`
- release (dart2js): `Null check operator used on a null value` in `RenderBox.hitTest`.

It throws in `MouseTracker`'s post-frame device update and on every following pointer event, before the hover exit is dispatched. So the `InkWell` never loses its highlight, the item stays kept alive, the tooltip stays on screen, and **the app stops reacting to the mouse until the page is reloaded**. In debug, the tracker then also asserts `'!_debugDuringDeviceUpdate': is not true.`

Not affected: items with a relayout boundary inside (for example `SizedBox(height: …)` + `Align`), because the dirty boundary is still laid out from the dirty list while parked; and leading garbage, because `RenderSliverList` lays those children out before collecting them.

### In production

We hit this in our production Flutter web app (desktop Chrome, Edge and Safari; Flutter 3.45 beta, 3.47 and 3.49 beta), in a side-panel list of cards that each have a delete `IconButton` with a `Tooltip`. Over the last 90 days:

- 37 users hit it at least once, about 1.7 % of the ~2,125 web users who opened that page;
- 14,415 error events, since a frozen tab throws on every mouse move until it is reloaded;
- mostly on low-end laptops (for example a 1358×644 screen with 4 GB of RAM). The hover and a large scroll delta have to land in the same frame,

title: After a three-finger screenshot, Flutter touch handling stays in `accepted` and subsequent touches stop responding
body:
## Problem

On an Android tablet, after using the system three-finger swipe-down screenshot gesture, none of the note cards in our Flutter page respond to taps. The list can still scroll vertically. Restarting the application that provides the Flutter page restores tapping. This happens every time on the current device.

Logging confirms that **after the screenshot, both DOWN and UP from subsequent taps reach Flutter, but the cards' `onTap` callbacks no longer run.** The three old pointers from the screenshot gesture never end. The list's drag recognizer stays in `accepted`, and hit-test paths for subsequent taps no longer include the card subtree.

Here, `accepted` refers to the state of `VerticalDragGestureRecognizer` in the logs: the drag gesture has been recognized and accepted.

## Background and environment

We are developing a Launcher (the device's home-screen application) for an Android tablet. The Launcher is written in **Kotlin with Jetpack Compose**, with several tabs for different pages.

The Notes tab displays a Flutter page written in **Dart**, provided by a separate Android application running in its own process. That application creates a FlutterEngine and FlutterView and uses `SurfaceControlViewHost` to provide a child Surface. The Launcher displays this Surface through a `SurfaceView` hosted in Compose's `AndroidView`.

The Flutter page contains vertically scrollable note cards. The cards are ordinary Flutter widgets that handle taps with `GestureDetector.onTap`.

- Android 15 / API 35
- Flutter 3.44.6
- Release mode
- FlutterView uses the default Surface rendering mode
- The device supports a built-in three-finger swipe-down screenshot gesture

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open the Launcher and switch to the Flutter Notes tab.
2. Tap any card and confirm that its `onTap` callback runs.
3. Swipe down with three fingers over the list to trigger a system screenshot.
4. After the screenshot, tap any card again.

**Expected:** Cards should still respond to taps after the screenshot.

**Actual:** None of the cards' `onTap` callbacks run. The list can still scroll, and other Launcher tabs and native components respond normally. Restarting the application that provides the Flutter page restores tapping.

## What happens to the next tap

### The screenshot gesture never ends on the Flutter side

Android logs show that two `ACTION_POINTER_UP` events and the final `ACTION_UP` reach the `ViewRootImpl` enqueue point in the process providing the Flutter page. However, these events never enter FlutterView's `dispatchTouchEvent` / `onTouchEvent`. Flutter receives neither the corresponding Up events nor a Cancel event.

So far, we have narrowed the gap down to the path between `ViewRootImpl` enqueueing the events and FlutterView's dispatch entry. We have not identified the specific Android function that stops these events from reaching FlutterView.

title: [Android][16 KB] ARM64 release libflutter.so has a misaligned GNU_RELRO end (3.44.2 and 3.47.5)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Inspect the official prebuilt Android ARM64 **release** engine binary from Flutter 3.47.5 (engine `af7e796e161ae0bb1ff0758c71a7105418bd9ded`):

```sh
curl -fL -o arm64_v8a_release.jar \
  https://storage.googleapis.com/download.flutter.io/io/flutter/arm64_v8a_release/1.0.0-af7e796e161ae0bb1ff0758c71a7105418bd9ded/arm64_v8a_release-1.0.0-af7e796e161ae0bb1ff0758c71a7105418bd9ded.jar
unzip -p arm64_v8a_release.jar lib/arm64-v8a/libflutter.so > libflutter.so
llvm-readelf -lW libflutter.so | grep -E 'LOAD|GNU_RELRO'
```

Calculate `(GNU_RELRO VirtAddr + MemSiz) % 0x4000`. The same check can be performed on Flutter 3.44.2's official ARM64 release artifact (engine `77e2e94772b6eb43759e34ed1ad7da4674e19cab`). This does not require application code; the input is the Flutter-distributed engine binary.

### Expected results

The ARM64 release `libflutter.so` should satisfy the 16 KB GNU_RELRO boundary check described in the [Android 16 KB page-size documentation](https://developer.android.com/guide/practices/page-sizes), or there should be an explanation of why the published binary is safe on 16 KB-page ARM64 devices despite the check failing.

### Actual results

The check fails for both official prebuilt ARM64 release artifacts:

| Flutter | GNU_RELRO `VirtAddr` | `MemSiz` | End | End modulo `0x4000` |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 3.44.2 | `0xaba8e0` | `0x05a720` | `0xb15000` | `0x1000` |
| 3.47.5 | `0xae7ef0` | `0x05b110` | `0xb43000` | `0x3000` |

The `LOAD` segment alignments are at least 16 KB. In a Flutter 3.44.2 release AAB, bundletool reported `PAGE_ALIGNMENT_16K`, and the generated APK split's ZIP alignment passed. Thus this report is about the ARM64 release ELF's RELRO boundary, not AAB/APK ZIP alignment. The x86_64 release engine and an ARM64 profile engine inspected in the same investigation did not show this mismatch.

This is a **static binary inspection finding**. I have not reproduced an ARM64 16 KB-page runtime crash, so I am not claiming one.

### Code sample

No Dart sample is needed: the reproduction above uses the official Flutter Maven artifact directly.

### Logs

Relevant `llvm-readelf -lW` fields for the official binaries:

```text
Flutter 3.44.2 arm64_v8a_release: GNU_RELRO VirtAddr=0xaba8e0 MemSiz=0x05a720
Flutter 3.47.5 arm64_v8a_release: GNU_RELRO VirtAddr=0xae7ef0 MemSiz=0x05b110
```

Related issue: #150168 tracks the broader 16 KB page-size support work, but does not appear to cover this release-artifact RELRO boundary check.

### Flutter Doctor output

The local AAB was built with Flutter 3.44.2 stable (framework `c9a6c48423`, engine `77e2e94772`, Dart 3.12.2) on macOS x64 with Android SDK 35.0.0. The 3.47.5 result above comes from inspecting its official artifact directly, not from a locally installed 3.47.5 SDK. Host-specific doctor paths and device names are omitted; I can provide more environment details if needed.

title: [a11y][iOS] VoiceOver scroll move 80% of the viewport, while native iOS moves a full screen
body:
When VoiceOver is on, swiping with 3 fingers only scrolls 80% of the screen length, compared to native iOS, which traverses 100% of the screen height. This value is hardcoded [here](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/29367a5ec5389371bc9825d88ffb5e7cb59598cd/packages/flutter/lib/src/rendering/proxy_box.dart#L4001)
This seems to have be introduced in 2016 [here](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/1309/changes#diff-49ed554236b13596f025c7396911c4dc95da9f6341b0835c2298bfc234667ba2R1415), with no context left behind. 

The problem here is that VoiceOver's page announcements ("page 3 of 6") are based on full-screen pages, so in Flutter apps the swipe count and the page count don't match, it takes more swipes than the announced number of pages which can be quite confusing. 

Here you can see that in Flutter, its takes 4  swipes to get to the bottom, while in native it takes 3 swipes.

| Flutter | Native |
| :-: | :-: |

I'm not sure how Android behaves.

title: [webview_flutter] Recurring flake on `Mac_arm64 macos_platform_tests`: `Failed to load webview_flutter_test.dart: OS Error: Invalid argument, errno = 22`
body:
`webview_flutter`'s macOS integration tests intermittently fail on `Mac_arm64 macos_platform_tests` before any test runs. The app builds and launches, then the test file fails to load with `OS Error: Invalid argument, errno = 22`, and every test is reported as "did not complete".

18 confirmed occurrences since 2026-08-22, on both `master` and `stable` and on unrelated changes (postsubmit commits and PRs from different authors), so this is not caused by any single change. Most recently it failed the flutter -> packages roll https://github.com/flutter/packages/pull/13065; the next roll (https://github.com/flutter/packages/pull/13066, a superset of the same Flutter commits) passed this builder.

title: [iOS][a11y] VoiceOver focus jumps to the first element on screen after a three-finger scroll
[Flutter GPU] Metal shaders cannot opt out of fast math
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. On an M3 or newer Mac on macOS 26+ (or a recent iPhone on iOS 26+), draw with a large Flutter GPU fragment shader. flutter_scene at `f706046e` does this with any lit, shadowed mesh (bdero/flutter_scene#436).
2. Without that hardware, build the reduced shader below with the Xcode 27 Metal toolchain: `metal-tt -arch applegpu_g16s -macos-version-min 26.0` fails with `LLVM ERROR: Failed to encode.` and passes with `-fno-fast-math`.

### Expected results

Flutter GPU shaders can be compiled without fast math.

### Actual results

Impeller compiles Flutter GPU's runtime MSL with `newLibraryWithSource:options:NULL` ([shader_library_mtl.mm](https://github.com/flutter/flutter/blob/master/engine/src/flutter/impeller/renderer/backend/metal/shader_library_mtl.mm#L125-L126)), so fast math is always on. Apple's compiler crashes on this shader under fast math (FB24988821) and builds it with `MTLMathModeSafe`. A shader cannot opt out on its own, since `#pragma METAL fp math_mode(safe)` does not reach the precompiled `metal_stdlib`.

flutter_scene worked around it by shrinking its shaders (bdero/flutter_scene#438), but any large enough shader can hit it again. The segfault that followed the failed pipeline on stable is already fixed on master by #189899.

### Code sample

<details open><summary>Code sample</summary>

Reduced MSL and a standalone Metal probe: https://github.com/kiarina/labs/tree/main/2026/09/29/flutter-scene-m4-metal-crash (`reduced/standard_26678127_reduced.metal`, `probe/main.swift`).

</details>

### Screenshots or Video

<details open>
<summary>Screenshots / Video demonstration</summary>

N/A

</details>

### Logs

<details open><summary>Logs</summary>

```console
Could not create render pipeline for :Compilation failed due to an interrupted connection: XPC_ERROR_CONNECTION_INTERRUPTED. This error occurred after multiple retries.
```

`MTLCompilerService` aborts in `llvm::MCObjectStreamer::emitInstruction` while compiling the fragment shader.

</details>

title: Migrate ContextMenuButtonType to an enum-like class ContextMenuButtonKind
body:
`ContextMenuButtonType` is a public enum in `package:flutter/widgets.dart`. `cupertino_ui` and `material_ui` (and probably other packages and apps) use exhaustive switches over it, so adding a new value is a breaking change. For example, adding `ContextMenuButtonType.translate` breaks the published `cupertino_ui` 1.1.1.

This is blocking the iOS Translate context menu item (#180021). The engine side already landed in #189878, but the framework side can't add a new button type without breaking the decoupled packages.
The Dart team isn't planning to add open enums (https://github.com/dart-lang/sdk/issues/63678#issuecomment-5335706239), so the suggestion from the discussion was to move to an enum-like class, like we did with `FloatingActionButtonLocation`.

Because `cupertino_ui` and `material_ui` support older stable Flutter versions, they can't reference `ContextMenuButtonKind` until it reaches stable and they bump their minimum SDK constraint. To avoid unresolvable deprecation warnings on `master` in the meantime, we're doing a phased migration:
- [x] **1. Add `ContextMenuButtonKind` (without deprecating `ContextMenuButtonType`):** Introduce `ContextMenuButtonKind` (including `translate`) and `ContextMenuButtonItem.kind`, while keeping `ContextMenuButtonType` and `ContextMenuButtonItem.type` undeprecated. (#193528)
- [ ] **2. Migrate `cupertino_ui` and `material_ui`:** Once `ContextMenuButtonKind` reaches stable, bump the minimum Flutter SDK in `cupertino_ui` and `material_ui` and switch them from `item.type` to `item.kind` (including handling `translate`).
- [ ] **3. Deprecate `ContextMenuButtonType` and `ContextMenuButtonItem.type`**

title: [tool_crash] Unhandled ProcessPackageException in DefaultResidentCompiler._compile when dartaotruntime is missing
body:
### Summary
In Flutter 3.47.5 (7 days post-release), `ProcessPackageException` at `LocalProcessManager.start` (`package:process/src/interface/local_process_manager.dart-a1bacf0f`) is the #9 tool crasher, accounting for **61 crashes (4.0% of Top 10 crashes, 2.0% of all crashes)**.

### Stack Trace & Error Message
```text
ProcessPackageException: ProcessException: Failed to find "/Users/.../flutter/bin/cache/dart-sdk/bin/dartaotruntime" in the search path.
  Command: /Users/.../flutter/bin/cache/dart-sdk/bin/dartaotruntime

#0      LocalProcessManager.start (package:process/src/interface/local_process_manager.dart:56)
#1      ErrorHandlingProcessManager.start.<anonymous closure> (package:flutter_tools/src/base/error_handling_io.dart:1284)
#2      _run (package:flutter_tools/src/base/error_handling_io.dart:1052)
#3      ErrorHandlingProcessManager.start (package:flutter_tools/src/base/error_handling_io.dart:1282)
#4      DefaultResidentCompiler._compile (package:flutter_tools/src/compile.dart:1000)
#5      DefaultResidentCompiler._recompile (package:flutter_tools/src/compile.dart:877)
#6      _RecompileRequest._run (package:flutter_tools/src/compile.dart:451)
#7      _CompilationRequest.run (package:flutter_tools/src/compile.dart:424)
#8      DefaultResidentCompiler._handleCompilationRequest (package:flutter_tools/src/compile.dart:928)
```

### Root Cause Analysis
In `DefaultResidentCompiler._compile` (`packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/compile.dart:997`), `_processManager.start(command)` spawns `dartaotruntime` with `frontend_server_aot.dart.snapshot`. If the user's Flutter SDK `bin/cache` directory is corrupted, partially downloaded, or cleaned while a resident session or compilation request is running (or quarantined by antivirus), `LocalProcessManager.start` throws `ProcessPackageException` (`ProcessException: Failed to find ".../dartaotruntime" in the search path`), which is not caught or converted to a `ToolExit` by `ErrorHandlingProcessManager` or `DefaultResidentCompiler._compile`.

### Expected Behavior
`DefaultResidentCompiler._compile` (or `ErrorHandlingProcessManager`) should catch `ProcessException` when spawning the Dart AOT runtime / frontend server and exit cleanly with a `ToolExit` instructing the user to check their Flutter SDK cache (e.g., run `flutter doctor` or `rm -rf <flutter>/bin/cache`).

### Related Issues & PRs
- Related Windows Application Control `dartaotruntime` issue: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/191899
- Prior closed/locked user reports: https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/193018, https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/190553, https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/189771, https://github.com/flutter/flutter/issues/187976

In `WebDriverService.startTest` (`packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/drive/web_driver_service.dart:199-219`), `async_io.createDriver(...)` only catches `SocketException`:

        desired: getDesiredCapabilities(...),

    } on SocketException catch (error) {

`WebDriverService.startTest` should catch `async_io.WebDriverException` (or `SessionNotCreatedException`) and call `throwToolExit` with the underlying WebDriver error message rather than crashing `flutter_tools`.

### Stack Trace & Error Message

ShaderCompilerException: Shader compilation of "/opt/flutter/packages/flutter/lib/src/widgets/shaders/stretch_effect.frag" to "build/unit_test_assets/shaders/stretch_effect.frag" failed with exit code 1.
Stderr:
Could not write file to "build/unit_test_assets/shaders/stretch_effect.frag"

<asynchronous suspension>

<asynchronous suspension>

### Root Cause Analysis
1. In `writeBundle` (`packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/bundle_builder.dart`), if `bundleDir.deleteSync(recursive: true)` fails or races with another concurrent `flutter test` process (or when the workspace `build/` directory is read-only / locked), `impellerc` fails with exit code 1 (`Could not write file to "build/unit_test_assets/shaders/..."`).
2. `ShaderCompiler.compileShader` (`packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/build_system/tools/shader_compiler.dart`) throws an unhandled `ShaderCompilerException` when `fatal: true` (the default), which is not caught by `writeBundle` or `TestCommand._buildTestAsset` and surfaces as an unhandled tool crash rather than a `ToolExit`.

### Expected Behavior
`writeBundle` / `ShaderCompiler.compileShader` should handle shader output write failures (or convert `ShaderCompilerException` into a `ToolExit` with an actionable error message) instead of crashing the tool with an unhandled exception.

title: [web] Render soft hyphens (`Hyphens` API) on WebParagraph
body:
#185152 adds a `Hyphens` API (`ParagraphStyle.hyphens`, `Text.hyphens`, etc.) so that soft hyphens (U+00AD) render as a visible hyphen at line breaks. On native platforms the engine passes this through to Skia's `ParagraphStyle::setRenderSoftHyphens`.

CanvasKit and Skwasm now render soft hyphens: CanvasKit in #194339 (with Skia's binding from https://skia-review.googlesource.com/c/skia/+/1378836) and Skwasm in #193850. WebParagraph, the experimental pure-Dart text renderer, still stores `hyphens` without acting on it: its line breaker and painter don't draw a hyphen when a line breaks at U+00AD.

Splitting this out of #18443 so that #185152 can close that issue for native platforms, per https://github.com/flutter/flutter/pull/185152#issuecomment-5625236222.

Related: #189617 (customizing the hyphen string), #189234 (hyphen glyph excluded from selection highlight).

title: flutter test --platform chrome hangs/fails on Windows: CanvasKit assets 404 due to backslash path from path.fromUri
body:
# `flutter test --platform chrome` hangs/fails on Windows: CanvasKit assets 404 due to backslash path from `path.fromUri`

## Summary

On Windows, `flutter test --platform chrome` fails for **every** web test (not just widget tests — a bare `test()` with no rendering fails identically) because the local CanvasKit-serving handler in `flutter_tools` builds a filesystem-style path from the request URL and then compares it against a hardcoded forward-slash prefix. `path.fromUri` returns a backslash-separated path on Windows, so the comparison never matches, every CanvasKit asset request 404s, the Flutter web engine's bootstrap throws an uncaught `TypeError`, and the test harness never reports a result — so the CLI either fails fast with a generic "Connection closed before test suite loaded" or hangs indefinitely, depending on timing.

## Steps to reproduce

1. On Windows, with Chrome installed, create a brand-new project:
   ```
   flutter create canvaskit_repro
   cd canvaskit_repro
   ```
2. Run the default generated test on Chrome:
   ```
   flutter test --platform chrome
   ```

No changes to `pubspec.yaml`, `test/widget_test.dart`, or any other generated file are needed — this reproduces with the completely unmodified output of `flutter create`.

## Expected behavior

The default counter-app widget test passes on the `chrome` platform, as it does on `vm`/other platforms.

## Actual behavior

The command either:
- fails within about a second with:
  ```
  00:00 +0: loading test\widget_test.dart
  00:00 +0 -1: loading test\widget_test.dart [E]
    Failed to load "test\widget_test.dart": Connection closed before test suite loaded.
  00:00 +0 -1: Some tests failed.
  ```
- or hangs indefinitely with no further output once Chrome has been launched (`[CHROME]: DevTools listening on ws://...`).

Both are the same underlying failure; which one you see depends on the exact timing of the browser's WebSocket teardown after the uncaught exception below.

## Root cause (found via live Chrome DevTools Protocol inspection)

Attaching to the running Chrome page via CDP (`Runtime.enable` / `Log.enable`) while the command is stuck shows the actual in-page failure, which the `flutter test` CLI never surfaces:

```
Log.entryAdded (network, error): Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)
  url: http://localhost:<port>/canvaskit/chromium/canvaskit.wasm
Log.entryAdded (network, error): Failed to load resource: the server responded with a status of 404 (Not Found)
  url: http://localhost:<port>/canvaskit/chromium/canvaskit.js

Runtime.exceptionThrown (Uncaught in promise):
  TypeError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module: http://localhost:<port>/canvaskit/chromium/canvaskit.js
```

`flutter_test` always bootstraps the rendering engine — including CanvasKit — even for a test that never pumps a widget, so this 404 is fatal for every web test on Windows, not only widget tests.

title: [Impeller][Android] Adreno ≤ 650 builds a full Vulkan context on every cold start before falling back to OpenGL ES (~44 ms probe + ~91 ms GLES pipelines before first frame; regression 3.35 → 3.44)
body:
### Summary

Since 3.44, `DriverInfoVK::IsKnownBadDriver()` sends Adreno ≤ 650 to OpenGL ES (the rule cites #178285 and #178498). That check only runs after `GetActualRenderingAPIForImpeller` has created a complete `AndroidContextVKImpeller`, so every one of these devices pays for Vulkan setup on each cold start and then throws it away. The GLES backend it falls back to then builds its pipelines in `ContentContext`'s constructor, also on the raster thread and also before the first frame.

On a Snapdragon 678 / Adreno 612 phone that is ~150 ms of raster-thread CPU on the cold-start critical path. It didn't exist on 3.35.7, where these GPUs stayed on Vulkan.

The ordering is unchanged on `master` today: the emulator, Huawei, MediaTek and `IsKnownBadSOC` checks return early, and the Adreno rule is still only reached through the `ContextVK` that gets built right after them.

### Environment

- Flutter 3.44.9 stable (framework 6b182d2c75, engine 5a2a6a42cc), release AOT build (`profileable` for measurement)
- Redmi Note 10 (M2101K7AI), Snapdragon 678, **Adreno 612**, 4 GB RAM, Android 15 (AOSP build), `ro.product.board=sm6150`

### Evidence

logcat on one cold start (both lines from the same process, 18 ms apart):

```
15:13:09.699 I flutter : [IMPORTANT:flutter/shell/platform/android/android_context_vk_impeller.cc(62)] Using the Impeller rendering backend (Vulkan).
15:13:09.717 I flutter : [IMPORTANT:flutter/shell/platform/android/android_context_gl_impeller.cc(104)] Using the Impeller rendering backend (OpenGLES).
```

simpleperf (cpu-clock, dwarf call graphs, unstripped `libflutter.so`), raster thread, launch → first frame:

| Phase | Raster CPU | Top frames |
|---|---|---|
| Vulkan probe | ~44 ms (of 62 ms in `SetupImpellerContext`) | `AndroidContextDynamicImpeller::SetupImpellerContext` → `AndroidContextVKImpeller::AndroidContextVKImpeller` → `impeller::ContextVK::Setup` → `vulkan::api::CreateInstance` → `vulkan.adreno.so` |
| GLES pipeline pre-build | ~91 ms | `PlatformViewAndroid::CreateRenderingSurface` → `AndroidSurfaceGLImpeller::CreateGPUSurface` → `AiksContext` → `impeller::ContentContext::ContentContext` → `GenericRenderPipelineHandle` → `PipelineLibraryGLES::GetPipeline` |

Also on the critical window, on a worker: `FlutterJNI.prefetchDefaultFontManager` → `SkFontMgr_Android::addFamily`, ~118 ms CPU.

Cold start, `am start -W` TotalTime, 15 runs each, same device, medians:

| Build | Impeller (GLES after probe) | Skia (`--enable-impeller=false`) |
|---|---|---|
| A | 877 ms | 770 ms |
| B | 838 ms | 761 ms |

Field data for our app: Play Vitals "slow cold start" went from **4.71%** on the release built with 3.35.7 to **8.44%** on the next release (3.44.9), concentrated on 3–4 GB devices on Android 10/11. That release also added one analytics SDK, but profiling puts its CPU after the first frame, so we attribute the jump mainly to the engine. It isn't all Adreno: the same tier includes MediaTek phones, which this report doesn't cover.

[Pixel Tablet][Impeller] Repeated screen rotation causes GPU (dma-buf) memory leak, app silently killed by lowmemorykiller
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Device: Pixel Tablet, Android 17
First detected using Flutter 3.38.7, but also confirmed to be reproducible in Flutter 3.47.4 as well.
1. Create a fresh Flutter project: `flutter create rotation_test` (default counter app, no custom code).
2. Run the app on the device.
3. Rotate the screen repeatedly (physically or via automation) about 150–300 times within roughly 5 minutes.

Currently we can only reproduce this on the Pixel Tablet Android device. Testing on a LAVIE Tab E (Android 10) does not cause a crash, so we suspect it could be a device-specific bug

### Expected results

The app keeps running normally through repeated rotation.

### Actual results

After approximately 150–300 rotation cycles (~5 minutes), the app process is silently killed by the OS. There is no FATAL EXCEPTION, no native tombstone, and no ANR — the process simply disappears (WINDOW DIED / Process ... has died).

Reproduced twice independently with consistent results (crash at cycle 278 and cycle 301 in two separate runs).

Root cause appears to be a GPU (dma-buf) memory leak in Impeller's Android render surface: `dmabuf_pss` grows to ~4.5–4.9 GB before the OS's lowmemorykiller kills the app — even though the app is in the foreground (oom_score_adj 0, normally very hard to kill). This memory growth is invisible to `dumpsys meminfo <package>` (graphics_pss stays flat throughout), so standard memory monitoring gives no warning.

To confirm this is specific to Impeller, I compared the same app, same device, same rotation pattern, changing only the renderer. With Impeller enabled (the default, using Vulkan and the default RenderMode.surface), the app consistently crashed around cycle 278–301. Switching RenderMode.surface to RenderMode.texture did not help — it still crashed at around cycle 298 with the same dmabuf_pss leak (the buffer warning just changes from referring to a SurfaceView to a SurfaceTexture, but the leak itself is identical). Adding android:rotationAnimation="jumpcut" to skip the rotation animation didn't help either — it still crashed at cycle 299.
However, when I disabled Impeller (io.flutter.embedding.android.EnableImpeller = false, falling back to Skia) on that same app, the leak disappeared entirely — it ran past 980 rotation cycles with no crash, no lowmemorykiller kill, and no buffer warning at all. As a further sanity check, a hand-written native Android app (a plain SurfaceView continuously redrawn via Canvas, with no Flutter involved) also ran past 1000 cycles on the same device without issue

### Code sample

Default Flutter counter app generated by `flutter create` (Flutter 3.47.4, stable channel) — no custom code was added. The bug reproduces with the completely unmodified starter template.

### Screenshots or Video

This video has been shortened and is only showing the final moment of the app crashing. The total testing duration is about 5 minutes.

### Steps to reproduce

## Steps to reproduce

On a Samsung SM-A5160 (Android 13, Mali-G76, driver r38p1), scrolling newly decoded images under two fixed `BackdropFilter`s causes Skia/GLES Graphics memory to reach approximately 2 GiB while the tracked live GL storage remains below 78 MiB. A diagnostic change that enables non-renderable scratch texture reuse reduces the peak to approximately 150 MiB while retaining mipmaps, blur and the original synchronization. An independent native GLES program also reproduces the growth.

I am reporting a reproducible allocation/lifetime interaction and requesting help with a safe engine-side mitigation and upstream ownership. I have **not** established a permanent leak or the driver's internal allocation mechanism.

### Tested environment

- Samsung SM-A5160, Android 13 / API 33, arm64; physical display 1080 × 2400.
- GPU: Mali-G76. Driver string: `v1.r38p1-01bet0-mbs2v41_0.abf8345db3d3997d6844dcadfe1a9041`.

title: ReorderableListView: an item reparented during a drag stays "dragging" after the drop (Null check in _ReorderableItemState.build)
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Run the code sample below. It rebuilds once a second and, every 3 seconds, moves the `ReorderableListView` to a new parent through a `GlobalKey` (the app bar title flips between "wrapped" and "not wrapped").
2. Long-press item **B** so it lifts, and keep holding it until the title flips.
3. Release it **where it started**, so the order does not change.

### Expected results

The item drops back into place and keeps rendering normally.

### Actual results

The item turns into an error widget and throws on every later rebuild (here once a second, from the timer):

```
Null check operator used on a null value
#0      _ReorderableItemState.build (package:flutter/src/widgets/reorderable_list.dart:1294:57)
#1      StatefulElement.build (package:flutter/src/widgets/framework.dart:5944:27)
...
```

The drop itself usually also throws once:

```
Null check operator used on a null value
#0      SliverReorderableListState._itemOffsetAt (package:flutter/src/widgets/reorderable_list.dart:1132:25)
#1      SliverReorderableListState._dragEnd.<anonymous closure> (package:flutter/src/widgets/reorderable_list.dart:948:30)
```

We first saw it in production: release build 3.47.1 on iOS 26.6.2. A card in a reorderable list rendered as a grey box and threw once a second, because the page rebuilds every second, until the user left the screen.

### Cause

What I found by reading `reorderable_list.dart`:

- `_ReorderableItemState.deactivate()` calls `_listState._unregisterItem(index, this)`.
- Nothing re-registers the item on `activate()`. Registration only happens in `initState`, `didUpdateWidget` and `build`.
- `build` returns the drag placeholder **before** it calls `_registerItem`:
  ```dart
  if (_dragging) {
    final Size size = _extentSize(_listState._dragInfo!.itemExtent, _listState._scrollDirection);
    return SizedBox.fromSize(size: size);
  }
  _listState._registerItem(this);
  ```
- So if the dragged item is deactivated and re-activated during the drag (its subtree moved through a GlobalKey), it is no longer in `_items`.
- `_dragReset()` only resets `_items[_dragIndex]`:
  ```dart
  if (_dragIndex != null && _items.containsKey(_dragIndex)) { ... dragItem._dragging = false; ... }
  ```
- The re-activated item therefore keeps `_dragging == true` after `_dragInfo` is set to null, and every later `build` hits `_dragInfo!`.
- If the drop changes the order, the index-based `_ReorderableItemGlobalKey` replaces the item's state and the problem disappears. If the item is dropped in place, the stuck state survives.

A possible fix, not tested against the framework: re-register in `_ReorderableItemState.activate()`, and/or make `_dragReset` clear `_dragging` on every registered or known item instead of only `_items[_dragIndex]`.

The code is unchanged in 3.47.5, 3.48.0-0.5.pre, 3.49.0-0.1.pre and on `master` as of today.

title: [Google_sign_in] Consider removing the objc exception handler from the plugin
body:
Extracted from: https://github.com/flutter/packages/pull/12658/changes#r4018994922

> Do we actually need ExceptionCatcher.m?
>
> From what I see, the only exceptions the SDK ever throws are invalid arguments:
>
> Missing GIDClientID, which means the app hasn't been configured correctly and won't work (can't happen unexpectedly in the wild for an app; it's a deterministic failure that can only happen if the app was build wrong).
Missing URL scheme handling, same restrictions.
Missing clientID, same restrictions.
Missing view controller, which appears to only be possible if we pass a null view controller into a non-nullable parameter, which a) would be a plugin bug, and b) is something we would have to try very hard to screw up with a Swift implementation of the plugin.
So AFAICT, the three that could happen to clients are all cases where the client built their app incorrectly, and would be found by the client with any testing of the login path. Is it actually worth keeping the plugin hybrid language forever just to make that category of error bubble up to Dart instead of crashing?

title: [google_maps_flutter] Add SDK 11 package for iOS
body:
Version 11 of the Google Maps SDK for iOS was [released in August](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/ios-sdk/release-notes), so with the per-SDK package structure there will need to be a new copy created that uses SDK 11. This will be the first SwiftPM-only version, as there's no CocoaPods release of v11.

Surprisingly, this release didn't drop any iOS versions as the releases have done in past years; it [still supports iOS 16+](https://github.com/googlemaps/ios-maps-sdk/blob/e096f5c46d84c01c0a0a55df7263d5c6631535d6/Package.swift#L20). That means that in theory, it could be added as a range to the `_sdk10` package, but that would be pretty confusing, so I would recommend just making a new `_sdk11` package anyways (even though I'm not aware of any reason someone would want to use 10 instead of 11 at this point). The release notes don't call out any changes, so presumably all the source can continue to be shared.

title: [Android] Image textures expose allocation padding outside logical image bounds
body:
### Steps to reproduce

Android ImageReader textures can draw allocation padding beyond `Image.getWidth()` / `getHeight()`. This produces a green edge or extra border pixels and compresses the useful image into the expected destination rectangle.

1. Run the synthetic reproduction below on a Pixel 9 Pro with Android 17 and stock Flutter 3.47.5, using Impeller Vulkan.
2. Select check 3 of 4: `portrait720`, Texture, Software decoder (`c2.android.avc.decoder`). A green strip appears at the right edge.
3. Switch to Reference (Android PlatformView) with the same decoder. The strip disappears.
4. Select `square322` from the menu while keeping Texture and Software decoder. Its encoded white frame is thicker on the right and bottom.

### Expected results

Only the logical image should be drawn. Pixels outside its dimensions must not become part of the video. The synthetic white frame should have equal thickness on all four sides.

### Actual results

The renderer samples the entire HardwareBuffer allocation. Instrumentation measured:

| Clip | Logical Image size | HardwareBuffer allocation |
|---|---|---|
| square322 | 322 x 322 | 336 x 336 |
| portrait720 | 720 x 1280 | 768 x 1280 |

In a separate 24-check comparison across six clips on Pixel 9 Pro, stock produced six visual failures, all Texture + software decoder. An engine patched to exclude this allocation padding passed all 24 human-rated checks. Both runs used identical video hashes and confirmed Vulkan at startup.

This report is specifically about allocation dimensions exceeding logical Image dimensions. Related #159955 also discusses crop metadata inside a logical Image; this reproduction does not establish that all cases in that report have the same cause. The older #34642 concerns the SurfaceTexture transform path. The MediaTek distortion in #174026 remains reproducible on Xiaomi 23090RA98G with the padding patch.

### Code sample

The reproduction is in the `padding-repro-stock` branch of [ciriousjoker/flutter_packages](https://github.com/ciriousjoker/flutter_packages), commit `df93802584`. It contains the synthetic MP4 files and an example entry point, with a test-only decoder selector to make the software path deterministic. That selector is identical in stock and fixed comparisons; it does not crop the video.

```sh
git clone --branch padding-repro-stock https://github.com/ciriousjoker/flutter_packages.git
cd flutter_packages/packages/video_player/video_player_android/example
fvm install 3.47.5
fvm flutter pub get
GRADLE_OPTS=-Dorg.gradle.daemon=false fvm flutter run --profile --flavor stock   --target lib/crop_repro.dart --enable-impeller   --dart-define=ENGINE_VARIANT=stock   --dart-define=ENGINE_REVISION=stock-flutter-3.47.5
```

The fixture directory documents generation of the clips. No network video or application-specific assets are required. Select the connected Android device if prompted. Confirm the startup log reports the Vulkan backend before comparing results.

title: Wireless iOS debugging: Dart VM Service not discovered when device name contains non-ASCII characters
body:
## Disclaimer
The issue is researched, described, and published by AI.

## Bug
Wireless `flutter run` on a physical iOS device whose **name contains non-ASCII characters** (Cyrillic, accented Latin) launches the app but never attaches the debugger — the Dart VM Service is never discovered and times out. USB works; renaming the device to pure ASCII works.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Rename a physical iPhone (iOS 17+) to a non-ASCII name, e.g. `iPhone (Василий)` or `José’s iPhone`. iOS transliterates the Bonjour hostname to ASCII (`iPhone-vasilij.local`), so it no longer matches the display name.
2. Enable wireless debugging (USB once → "Connect via network" in Xcode → unplug).
3. `flutter create mdns_repro && cd mdns_repro && flutter run --verbose -d <wireless-device-id>`

## Expected result

VM Service connects: `A Dart VM Service ... is available at ...`, hot reload / DevTools available.

## Actual result

App launches and streams console logs, but discovery loops and times out:

```
Checking for available port on com.example.mdrepro._dartVmService._tcp.local
... (repeats)
The Dart VM Service was not discovered after 75 seconds.
```

No VM Service URL, no hot reload, no DevTools. Packet capture confirms the device advertises PTR+SRV+TXT+A correctly; the tool rejects them. ASCII rename fixes it.

## Cause

`packages/flutter_tools/lib/src/mdns_discovery.dart` filters services by device name:

```dart
if (deviceName != null && !deviceNameMatchesTargetName(deviceName, srvRecord.target)) continue;
// deviceName is device.name (display name) for wireless launch (getVMServiceUriForLaunch)

bool deviceNameMatchesTargetName(String deviceName, String targetName) {
  final cleanedNameRegex = RegExp(r'\.local|\W');   // \W is not Unicode-aware -> strips non-ASCII
  ...
  return cleanedDeviceName == cleanedTargetName;
}
```

`\W` deletes non-ASCII chars, so the display name never equals the transliterated hostname:
`"iPhone (Василий)" -> "iphone"` vs `"iPhone-vasilij.local" -> "iphonevasilij"` → `false` → correct SRV rejected → timeout.

Wireless-only: over USB `discoverVMUrlFromLogs` provides a fallback; wireless has none. Introduced in `d631b262856` (#131865), unchanged on stable 3.41.1 and master. Related: #160867 (closed not-repro — those attempts were over USB, where it appears to work).

## Environment

```
Flutter 3.41.1 (stable, 582a0e7c55, Dart 3.11.0)
macOS 26.6.2, Xcode 27.0 (27A266a)
iPhone iOS 26.6.2, wireless (CoreDevice)
```

title: [web] Multi-threaded skwasm hangs or crashes in FreeType: SkMutex is a no-op under -sWASM_WORKERS, so main-thread text layout and the raster worker share one FT_Face
body:
### Steps to reproduce

With multi-threaded skwasm (`flutter build web --wasm`, page served cross-origin isolated so skwasm runs its raster worker), a web app freezes for good -- or crashes with `RuntimeError: memory access out of bounds` inside FreeType -- when the main thread lays out text while the raster worker draws glyphs of the same font.

We hit it in production (a design-editor app: the canvas stops responding, pointer and cursors still alive), and reduced it to a stock `flutter create` app plus one file:

1. `flutter create skwasm_race && cd skwasm_race`
2. Put any TTF into `assets/montserrat.ttf` (reproduced with variable Montserrat and with static Roboto from Google Fonts) and list it under `flutter: assets:` in `pubspec.yaml`.
3. Replace `lib/main.dart` with the code below.
4. `flutter build web --wasm --release`
5. Serve `build/web` with `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` (script below), open it in Chrome and check `crossOriginIsolated === true`.

The page draws one paragraph at six continuously changing fractional scales (the raster worker keeps rasterising glyphs at new ppems), while a main-thread timer keeps laying out paragraphs of the same font at random sizes (SkParagraph shaping -> glyph metrics on the same `FT_Face`).

Controls: `?layout=0` (no main-thread layout, worker alone) runs indefinitely; `?zoom=0` (main thread alone) runs indefinitely. Only the two together hang.

### Expected results

The page keeps animating indefinitely.

### Actual results

Within seconds the tab stops responding: both the main thread and the raster worker spin (renderer ~180 % CPU, DevTools `Runtime.evaluate` times out). Profiling the worker shows it at 100 % in FreeType `af_glyph_hints_reload` (names from `skwasm.js.symbols`). Other runs of the same page end in `RuntimeError: memory access out of bounds` in `FT_Done_Size` / `FT_List_Find`.

### Cause (as far as we can tell)

skwasm links with `-sWASM_WORKERS=1` but without `-pthread`, so Emscripten's pthread stubs (`system/lib/pthread/library_pthread_stub.c`) are linked in and `sem_wait()` / `sem_post()` return immediately. The optimizer folds `SkSemaphore::osWait` / `osSignal` away, so `SkSemaphore` -- and therefore every `SkMutex` -- never blocks. That includes the FreeType face mutex in `SkFontHost_FreeType.cpp` (`f_t_mutex()`) and the strike cache lock. The main thread (paragraph layout) and the raster worker (glyph drawing) then use the same `FT_Face` concurrently, while FreeType says "An FT_Face object can only be safely used from one thread at a time."

#178749 describes the same no-op mutex problem for the strike cache in the wimp (Impeller web) work. This is the stock skwasm renderer shipping in stable today, and the thread-local strike cache work (#190048 / #191014) does not cover the FreeType face lock.

As a workaround we binary-patch the shipped `skwasm.wasm`: `SkSemaphore::wait()` / `signal(int)` are replaced with a spinning

title: [google_sign_in_android] NullPointerException in PlatformGoogleIdTokenCredential.<init> when GoogleIdTokenCredential.getEmail()/getUniqueId() returns null
body:
### Steps to reproduce

1. Use `google_sign_in: ^7.2.0` (resolves to `google_sign_in_android: 7.2.17`) in a release build (R8 enabled).
2. Call `GoogleSignIn.instance.initialize()` then `GoogleSignIn.instance.authenticate()`.
3. On an affected device, pick a Google account in the Credential Manager bottom sheet.

Seen in production Crashlytics on **Redmi A3, Android 16 (SDK 36)**. We cannot reproduce it on our own devices; it appears to depend on the credential returned by the device's Credential Manager provider.

### Expected results

If the returned `GoogleIdTokenCredential` is missing a field that the plugin requires, `authenticate()` should fail with a `GoogleSignInException` (or the missing field should be handled), and the app should keep running.

### Actual results

The app process crashes on the Credential Manager callback thread. The exception is thrown in native code on a background executor, so it cannot be caught from Dart.

**Root cause**

In `GoogleSignInPlugin.java` (`Delegate.getCredential` → `CredentialManagerCallback.onResult`), the credential is mapped like this:

```java
new PlatformGoogleIdTokenCredential(
    googleIdTokenCredential.getDisplayName(),
    googleIdTokenCredential.getFamilyName(),
    googleIdTokenCredential.getGivenName(),
    googleIdTokenCredential.getEmail(),     // @Nullable in googleid 1.2.0
    googleIdTokenCredential.getUniqueId(),  // @Nullable in googleid 1.2.0
    googleIdTokenCredential.getIdToken(),
    profilePictureUri == null ? null : profilePictureUri.toString())
```

In `com.google.android.libraries.identity.googleid:googleid:1.2.0`, `GoogleIdTokenCredential.getEmail()` and `getUniqueId()` are both annotated `@androidx.annotation.Nullable`. However, the pigeon definition declares them as non-null:

```dart
class PlatformGoogleIdTokenCredential {
  String? displayName;
  String? familyName;
  String? givenName;
  late String email;
  late String uniqueId;
  late String idToken;
  String? profilePictureUri;
}
```

The generated Kotlin data class therefore has `val email: String` and `val uniqueId: String`. When either value is null, Kotlin's parameter null check fails. R8 rewrites that check to `param.getClass()`, which produces the NPE in the logs at `Messages.kt:1`.

`getUniqueId()` was introduced in 7.2.14 ("Uses Google Identity APIs to extract the user ID from the ID token"). `getEmail()` was already passed into the non-null `email` field in 7.2.13, so downgrading is not a reliable workaround. The code on `main` is unchanged.

**Suggested fix:** treat a null `email`/`uniqueId` as a structured failure (e.g., `GetCredentialFailure` with `UNKNOWN` or `UNEXPECTED_CREDENTIAL_TYPE`), or fall back to other values (e.g., `getId()` for the email, the `sub` claim of the ID token for the user ID) before constructing `PlatformGoogleIdTokenCredential`.

### Code sample

```dart
import 'package:flutter/material.dart';
import 'package:google_sign_in/google_si

title: [Impeller][Android] 3.47 regression: MediaTek/Mali phones fall back to OpenGLES and freeze (ANR) — `1.io` stuck in `glReadPixels` (`libGLES_mali.so osup_sync_object_wait`), main thread stuck in `nativeSurfaceDestroyed
body:
### Steps to reproduce

We can't reproduce this on demand and don't have an affected device. It is a production regression that appeared when we upgraded from Flutter **3.44.9 to 3.47.2**. We did not change any Impeller or renderer settings between the two builds (Impeller enabled, `EnableHcpp=false`, default `FlutterSurfaceView`).

The conditions it shows up under:

1. A MediaTek phone with a Mali GPU whose vendor partition reports `ro.vendor.build.version.sdk` < 32. Since #186405 these phones no longer get Vulkan, so Impeller runs on OpenGLES. On 3.44 the same phones ran Vulkan.
2. The app calls `ui.Image.toByteData(format: ui.ImageByteFormat.rawRgba)` on decoded network images, for example to sample a dominant colour (the same thing `PaletteGenerator.fromImageProvider` does). For images that are not owned by the raster context, the engine does this readback on the `io` thread: `EncodeImage` posts to the IO runner, then `ImageEncodingImpeller::ConvertImageToRaster` → `BlitCopyTextureToBufferCommandGLES::Encode` → `gl.ReadPixels`.
3. Normal app use. We could not tie it to a specific screen or user action.

### Expected results

The app keeps rendering and responding to input, as it did on 3.44.9 on the same devices.

### Actual results

The UI freezes on the last frame and input is ignored. Android then reports an ANR.
